Coriander seed (Yuan Sui Zi)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%8A%AB%E8%8D%BD%E5%AD%90
Name
Coriander Fruit, Coriander Seed
Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi), Coriander Seed (Xiang Cai Zi).
Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi)
Coriander Seed (Xiang Cai Zi)
Cultivation and Processing of Coriander Fruit (Yuan Sui Zi)
Source
This product is the dried mature fruit of the Apiaceae (Umbelliferae) plant coriander (Yuan Sui; Coriandrum sativum L.).
Characteristics
This product is a schizocarp, globose, 3–5 mm in diameter. Surface pale yellow-brown to yellow-brown, with ten relatively distinct longitudinal secondary ribs and ten less distinct, wavy and curved primary ribs arranged alternately; the apex shows very short remnants of the style and traces of five sepal teeth; the base often retains a small pedicel or pedicel scar about 15 mm long. The ventral surface of each mericarp is centrally concave, with three longitudinal ridges, the central one relatively straight and the two lateral ones curved in an arc. Texture hard; when crushed by hand it emits a characteristic strong aroma and tastes slightly pungent.
Nature, Flavor, and Meridian Entry
Pungent, neutral. Enters the Lung and Stomach channels.
Functions and Indications
Releases the exterior, promotes eruption of rashes, and stimulates the appetite. Used for common cold with nasal congestion, poor eruption of measles/pox, poor appetite, and toothache.
Effects of Coriander Fruit (Yuan Sui Zi)
Actions
This product is the dried mature fruit of the Apiaceae plant coriander. Used for common cold with nasal congestion, poor eruption of measles/pox, poor appetite, and toothache.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decocted, 6–12 g; or added to powdered formulas.
External use: decoction for gargling or for fumigation/washing.
Prescriptions of Coriander Fruit (Yuan Sui Zi)
1. For early-stage measles eruption: Coriander Fruit (Yuan Sui Zi) four liang. After pounding, put into a fired earthenware pot or an aluminum pot, fill with clear water, place in the patient’s room (the room should be small and not ventilated), boil with charcoal so that steam fills the room, adding charcoal and water as needed; stop when the measles have fully erupted. (Zhejiang Journal of Traditional Chinese Medicine (3):32, 1959)
2. Treats dysentery and bloody diarrhea: Coriander Fruit (Yuan Sui Zi) one he. Pound and crush; for the red type mix with sugar water, for the white type mix with fresh ginger juice (Fresh Ginger, Sheng Jiang) and take warm. One prescription instructs taking it mixed with wine. (Pu Ji Fang)
3. For intestinal wind with continuous rectal bleeding that becomes hemorrhoids: Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi), Psoralea Fruit (Bu Gu Zhi) each half liang. Pound and sift the two ingredients into a powder. Each dose two qian, taken with rice water made from aged rice, before meals. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Hu Sui Zi Powder)
4. For hemorrhoids: Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi) stir-fried, finely ground, mixed with wine; take three to five doses. (Hai Shang Fang)
5. For rectal prolapse and anal fistula: Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi) one sheng, Frankincense (Ru Xiang) a small amount, millet bran (su kang) half sheng or one sheng. Use the above to form a clay furnace leaving only a small hole about the size of the anus, preventing smoke from escaping, and fumigate. (Ru Men Ting Qin)
6. For prolapsed rectum: In autumn and winter pound Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi), cook with vinegar and apply as a hot compress. (Shi Liao Ben Cao)
7. For toothache: Coriander Seed (Hu Sui Zi), with five sheng of water, boil down to one sheng, use to gargle and then spit out. (Bei Ji Fang)

Da Guo Lu Huang (Da Guo Lu Huang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E5%A4%A7%E8%BF%87%E8%B7%AF%E9%BB%84
Name
Ginger-flower herb; phlegm medicine.
[Source]
It is the whole herb of the Primulaceae (primrose family) plant Da guo lu huang (Dà guòlùhuáng). Harvested in summer, sun-dried or used fresh.
[Morphology]
Annual or perennial herb; stems usually tufted, bent at the nodes and erect, 10–30 cm high; in shady moist habitats lower stems often prostrate with roots at the nodes, upper parts zigzag ascending, up to 60 cm long, simple or many-branched, densely covered with multicellular hairs 1–1.5 mm long; leaves opposite; petiole 2–12 times shorter than the blade, densely covered with soft hairs; the two pairs of leaves at the stem apex are closely spaced and clustered in a whorl-like manner, often 1–2 times larger than lower leaves; leaf blades ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1.5–8 cm long, 8–40 mm wide, apex acute or slightly obtuse with an abrupt tip, base broadly cuneate, both surfaces with rough appressed hairs, midrib somewhat broad and conspicuous beneath; inflorescence terminal, nearly capitate, many-flowered; pedicels 1–7 mm, densely covered with soft hairs; calyx lobed nearly to the base, lobes lanceolate, abaxial surface with soft hairs; corolla yellow, 10–13 mm long, basal connate portion about 3 mm, apex 5-lobed, lobes obovate, with pellucid gland dots; stamens 5, filaments connate at the base forming a tube and free above, anthers ovate-lanceolate, dehiscence edges ciliate; style up to 8 mm, lower part and apex of the ovary hairy; capsule brown, 3.5–4 mm in diameter; flowering May–June, fruiting August–September.
[Habitat and distribution]
Ecological environment: grows under broadleaf forests and on valley stream banks and roadsides at altitudes of 600–2600 m.
Resource distribution: distributed in Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan and other areas.
Cultivation and processing of Da guo lu huang (Dà guòlùhuáng)
Nature and flavor
Bland; neutral in nature.
Effects of Da guo lu huang (Dà guòlùhuáng)
Efficacy
It is the whole herb of the Primulaceae (primrose family) plant Ye tou guo lu huang (Yètóu guòlùhuáng). Main indications are wind-heat cough, sore throat, and heat-toxin sores and scabies.
Channels entered
Lung; Stomach channels
Main indications
Disperses wind, clears heat and detoxifies. Transforms phlegm. Indicated for wind-heat cough, sore throat, and heat-toxin sores and scabies.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoction, 15–30 g.
External use: appropriate amount, fresh material pounded and applied; or decocted and used as a wash.

Cultivation and Preparation of Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao)
Source
This product is the dried aerial part of the Commelinaceae plant Common Dayflower (Commelina communis L.). Harvest in summer and autumn, sun-dry.
Properties and Flavor
Sweet; Cold; Bland
Processing
Remove impurities, wash clean, cut into sections, and sun-dry.
Appearance
This product can grow up to 60 cm, yellow-green or yellow-white, relatively smooth. Stems have longitudinal ridges, diameter about 0.2 cm, often branched or with adventitious roots, nodes slightly swollen, internodes 3–9 cm long; texture soft, cross-section with pith in the center. Leaves alternate, often wrinkled or fragmented; intact leaves when flattened are ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–9 cm long and 1–2.5 cm wide; apex acute, margins entire, base extending downward into a membranous leaf sheath that clasps the stem, veins parallel. Flowers are often deciduous; spathes are spathe-like, cordate, sides not joined; petals are crumpled and blue. Slight odor, bland taste.
Effects of Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao)
Functions
This product is the dried aerial part of the Commelinaceae plant Common Dayflower.
Main indications
Edema, beriberi, dysuria, common cold, erysipelas, mumps, jaundice hepatitis, febrile dysentery, malaria, epistaxis, hematuria, metrorrhagia, leukorrhea, throat swelling and pain, abscesses and sores.
Meridians
Enters
Lung meridian
;
Stomach meridian
Bladder meridian
Indications
Promotes urination and clears heat, cools the blood and detoxifies. Treats edema, beriberi, dysuria, common cold, erysipelas, mumps, jaundice hepatitis, febrile dysentery, malaria, epistaxis, hematuria, metrorrhagia, leukorrhea, throat swelling and pain, abscesses and sores.
1. Supplement to the Materia Medica: Used for cold and heat miasma and malaria, phlegm-fluid accumulation, localized swellings, indurated flesh masses, pediatric erysipelas, febrile mania and convulsions, abdominal fullness and distension, body and facial edema, febrile dysentery, snake and dog bites, and toxins of boils and carbuncles.
2. Rihuazi Materia Medica: Boil Common Dayflower with adzuki bean (Chi xiao dou) to reduce dampness in the lower burner and promote urination.
3. Materia Medica of South Yunnan: Tonifies qi and blood, treats women's leukorrhea and excessive uterine bleeding, generates new blood, stops hematuria, epistaxis, and bloody strangury.
4. Essentials of Collected Works: Clears heat-toxin and dissipates abscesses.
5. Compendium of Materia Medica: Relieves throat obstruction.
6. Evolution of Materia Medica: Used in large amounts for acute schistosomiasis with high fever. Also used for acute infectious febrile diseases with fever, impaired consciousness, and cardiac failure.
7. Sichuan Materia Medica: Clears heat and promotes diuresis, moistens the lung. Treats traumatic injuries, muscle and bone pain, and painful urinary dribbling.
8. Guangzhou Military Handbook of Common Chinese Herbs: Treats cardiac edema, beriberi edema, nephritic edema, urinary tract infections and calculi.
Usage and Dosage
Internal use: decoct 15–30 g; fresh product 60–90 g, or crush and take the juice.
External use: appropriate amount, crush and apply as a poultice.
Precautions
Use with caution in those with spleen and stomach deficiency and cold constitution.
Formulas Using Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao)
1. For urinary obstruction: Bamboo-chicken Herb (Zhu ji cao) 1 liang, Plantain Herb (Che qian cao) 1 liang. Pound to extract juice, add a little honey, take on an empty stomach. (Binhu Collection of Simple Prescriptions)
Bamboo-chicken Herb (Zhu ji cao)
One liang. Pound to extract juice, add a little honey, take on an empty stomach. (Binhu Collection of Simple Prescriptions)
2. For five types of strangury and painful urination: fresh Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) young stems and tender leaves 4 liang. Pound, add one cup boiled water, squeeze juice, adjust with honey and take internally three times daily. Reduce dose for physically weak patients. (Quanzhou Materia Medica)
3. For red and white dysentery: Blue-girl Herb (Lan gu cao), decoct and take daily. (Complete Book for Raising Children)
4. For jaundice hepatitis: Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) 4 liang, lean pork 2 liang. Stew in water, take the soup and eat the meat, one dose per day. (Jiangxi Herbal)
5. For hypertension: Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) 1 liang, broad bean flower (Can dou hua) 3 qian. Decoction, drink as tea. (Jiangxi Herbal)
6. For edema and ascites: fresh Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) 2–3 liang. Decoction, take for several consecutive days. (Common Folk Herbs of Zhejiang)
7. For hematemesis: juice of Bamboo-leaf Vegetable (Zhu ye cai) taken internally. (Guiyang Folk Herbal)
8. For intermittent nasal bleeding in atrophic rhinitis and epistaxis: Earth Lotus (Di di ou), decoct and take three times. (Materia Medica of South Yunnan)
9. For throat swelling and pain:
(1) Apply Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) juice topically. (Pocket Formulas)
(2) Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) 2 liang. Wash, pound to extract juice, frequently hold and swallow. (Jiangxi Herbal)
10. For pediatric erysipelas, febrile dysentery and as an antipyretic in acute febrile disorders: fresh Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) 2–3 liang (1 liang if dried); severe cases may use 5–7 liang. Decoction or take the juice. (Common Folk Herbs of Zhejiang)
11. For joint swelling and pain, suppurative swellings and ulcers: fresh Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) mashed, add a little strong alcohol (baijiu), apply to the affected area, change once daily. (Common Folk Herbs of Zhejiang)
12. For acute schistosomiasis: fresh Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao), washed, 5–8 liang daily, decoct and drink as tea, one course is 5–7 days. (Selected Compendium: Infectious Diseases)
13. For snakehead-type sore on the finger: fresh Common Dayflower (Ya zhi cao) and realgar (Xiong huang) mashed, apply to the affected area, change once daily. Early application can disperse swelling; if already suppurated it can reduce swelling and relieve pain. (Quanzhou Materia Medica)

Cultivation and Processing of Lu Rong Cao (Lu Rong Cao)
Source
The whole herb of the Scrophulariaceae plant Monochasma savatieri (hairy Lu Rong Cao; Mian Mao Lu Rong Cao).
Morphology
Biennial herb, 15–30 cm tall, whole plant densely covered with silvery-white tomentose hairs. Stems clustered, slender and rigid. Leaves dense, opposite or in whorls of three, sometimes alternate; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate, 1–3 cm long, 1–2 mm wide, entire margin, apex gradually acuminate, base narrow and sessile. Inflorescences with glandular hairs, bracts leaflike, flowers solitary in bract axils; calyx tube nearly as long as the lobes, with 10 ribs, lobes linear; corolla bilabiate, 2–2.5 cm long, longer than the calyx, pale red, throat slightly inflated, upper lip helmet-shaped and curved, 2-lobed, lower lip longer than the upper lip, middle lobe relatively long, throat with two grooves; stamens 4, didynamous, exserted; ovary incompletely two-loculed, with a central axial placenta, ovules numerous. Capsule enclosed within the calyx, oblong, apex sharp, with four longitudinal grooves, dehiscing along one side at maturity. Seeds numerous, flattened. Flowering April–May.
Habitat and Distribution
Grows on rocks or in dry areas. Distributed in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan and other regions.
Taste and Properties
Slightly bitter, astringent, neutral in nature.
Functions and Indications
Clears heat and detoxifies, cools the blood and stops bleeding. Used for feverish vexation in the chest from colds, cough, hematemesis, dysentery with blood, bloody stools, irregular menstruation, rheumatic bone pain, toothache, and mastitis.
Usage and Dosage
Internal use: decoction, 9–15 g;
External use: appropriate amount, decocted for washing or pounded and applied as a poultice.
Appearance
This product appears as gray-white segmented pieces, the whole surface densely covered with white tomentose hairs. Stem segments cylindrical, slender and rigid, some showing leaf scars from opposite, alternate or whorled leaves. Most leaves are broken; intact leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 0.6–3 cm long, 1–3 mm wide, entire margin, sessile, upper surface villous, sparser on the lower surface. Capsules oblong, enclosed in the hairy persistent calyx, apex sharp, with four longitudinal grooves, splitting along one side at maturity. Seeds numerous, small, yellow, ovoid, flattened. Odor slight, taste slightly bitter and astringent.
Effects of Lu Rong Cao
Efficacy
This product is the dried aerial part of the Scrophulariaceae plant Monochasma savatieri. Used for feverish vexation in the chest from colds, cough, hematemesis, dysentery with blood, bloody stools, irregular menstruation, rheumatic bone pain, toothache, and mastitis.
Prescriptions of Lu Rong Cao
1) For cough: Lu Rong Cao four qian, decocted in water and mixed with
rock sugar
take. (Hunan Materia Medica)
2) For rheumatic bone pain: Lu Rong Cao one to three liang, decocted in water and taken. (Hunan Materia Medica)
3) For hematemesis: Lu Rong Cao two liang,
Ophiopogon root (Mai Dong)
five qian,
Fritillaria bulb (Chuan Bei)
two qian. Decoction taken orally, white sugar used as an adjuvant, one dose daily. (Jiangxi Herbal Medicine)
4) For wind-cold common cold: fresh hairy Lu Rong Cao one to two liang, decocted in water and taken.
5) For postpartum common cold: dry hairy Lu Rong Cao one liang, dried whole herb of Bai Niu Dan Gan (Bai Niu Dan Gan) one liang. Decoct in water, sweeten with brown sugar and take.
6) For fatigue, lack of strength, and low back pain: fresh hairy Lu Rong Cao one to two liang, decocted in wine and water and taken; for low back pain add
sword-bean pod (Dao Dou Ke)
five qian,
dried cuttlefish
one piece, simmered in wine and water and taken. (Formulas 4 and following from Fujian Chinese Materia Medica)
7) For dysentery with blood: Liu Yue Shuang three qian, brown sugar five qian (stir-fried until dark). Decoction taken orally. (Experimental Research in Traditional Chinese Medicine)
8) For intestinal wind with bloody stools: Liu Yue Shuang three qian, together with
pig large intestine
stew until cooked, eat the intestine and the soup. (Experimental Research in Traditional Chinese Medicine)
9) For irregular menstruation and flooding and spotting: Lu Rong Cao four to six qian, decocted in water and taken. (Hunan Materia Medica)
10) For wind-fire toothache: Liu Yue Shuang, Xiu Hua Zhen (Xiu Hua Zhen),
Vitex root (Huang Jing Gen)
three qian each. Decoction taken orally. (Experimental Research in Traditional Chinese Medicine)
11) For deficient-fire toothache: Liu Yue Shuang two qian,
Lycium root (Gou Qi Gen)
five qian,
hairy ginger (Mao Jiang)
three qian. Decoction taken orally; or stew with 2–3 liang of lean pork and take as a soup. (Experimental Research in Traditional Chinese Medicine)
12) For breast cancer and mastitis: Mountain Gate Dome (Shan Men Qiong) five qian, mash to extract juice and mix with sweet fermented wine and take, three times daily.
13) For hemangioma: Mountain Gate Dome (Shan Men Qiong),
Gardenia root (Shan Zhi Gen)
five qian each. Decoct for eye wash.
14) For ulcerated foot sores: Mountain Gate Dome (Shan Men Qiong) two liang, decoct and wash with the liquid. (Formulas 12 and following from Hangzhou Materia Botanica)

Cultivation and processing of Bai Xian Pi
Source
This product is the dried root-bark of the Rutaceae plant Bai Xian (Dictamnus dasycarpus Turcz.). The roots are dug in the spring and autumn seasons; remove soil and coarse bark, strip the root-bark, and dry.
Properties and taste
Bitter; Salty; Cold
Processing
Pick out impurities, remove coarse bark, wash clean, moisten slightly, slice, sun-dry or stir-fry with wine.
Appearance
The Bai Xian root-bark appears as rolled tubes, length 5–15 cm, diameter 1–2 cm, thickness 2–5 mm. The outer surface is gray-white or pale gray-yellow, with fine longitudinal wrinkles and fine root scars, often with raised granular small dots; the inner surface is off-white, with fine longitudinal lines. The texture is brittle; when broken dust flies, the fracture surface is uneven, slightly lamellate; when the outer layer is removed and held to the light, tiny sparkling spots are visible. It has a mutton-like odor and a slightly bitter taste. Preferred are large strips, thick-fleshed, coated gray-white, with separated fracture surfaces.
Actions of Bai Xian Pi
Functions
This product is the dried root-bark of Bai Xian, a Rutaceae plant.
Main indications are wind-heat sores and toxins, scabies, pruritic dermatitis, rheumatic painful obstruction, and jaundice.
Channels entered
Spleen channel
;
Lung channel
;
Small Intestine channel
;
Stomach channel
;
Bladder channel
Indications
Expels wind, dries dampness, clears heat, detoxifies. Treats wind-heat sores and toxins, scabies, pruritic dermatitis, rheumatic painful obstruction, and jaundice.
① Benjing: Treats wind in the head, jaundice, reversed coughing, urinary dribbling, swelling and pain in the female genital region, damp-bi causing muscle death with inability to flex or extend, to start or stop, or to walk.
② Bie Lu: Treats restless limbs, intermittent excessive abdominal heat, drinking water, desire to walk, loud crying, childhood convulsions, and postpartum residual pain.
③ Yao Xing Lun: Treats all hot-toxin winds, malignant wind, wind sores, scabies with red ulceration, brittle eyebrow and hair loss, spasmodic skin and muscle disorders, high fever with aversion to cold; chiefly resolves heat jaundice, alcohol jaundice, acute jaundice, grain-related jaundice, and labor-related jaundice.
④ Bingbu Shou Ji Fang: Treats lung cough.
⑤ Ri Hua Zi Ben Cao: Unblocks joints, benefits the nine orifices and the blood vessels, and treats all wind-bi with weakness and lassitude of tendons and bones; unblocks small-intestine water qi, seasonal epidemic diseases, headaches and eye pain. The root-bark is good; the flowers have the same functions.
⑥ Ben Cao Yuan Shi: Treats all scabs, malignant wind, scabies, yangmei, and various sores with heat toxins.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoct 6–15 g; or make into pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, decoct for wash or grind to powder and apply.
Precautions and contraindications
Contraindicated in cases of deficiency-cold.
① Bencao Jing Jizhu: Incompatible with mantis egg-case (Piao Xiao), Platycodon root (Jie Geng), Poria (Fu Ling), and Smilax rhizome (Bi Xie).
② Bencao Jing Shu: Those with cold deficiency in the lower part of the body should not use, even if damp symptoms are present.
Formulas of Bai Xian Pi
① For wind-heat stored in the lungs, toxic qi attacking the skin causing pruritus, chest and diaphragm obstruction, occasional vexation: Bai Xian Pi (Bai Xian Pi), Siler root (Fang Feng) (remove lateral branches), Ginseng (Ren Shen), Anemarrhena rhizome (Zhi Mu) (roasted), Adenophora root (Nan Sha Shen) each one liang, Baical skullcap root (Huang Qin) (remove black core) three fen. Pound the above six into a powder. Each dose two qian, water one cup, decoct to six tenths, take warm, lie down after eating. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu Bai Xian Pi powder)
② For epileptic jaundice: Bai Xian Pi, Artemisia capillaris (Yin Chen), Artemisia (Hao) in equal parts. Boil with two zhong of water, take twice daily. (Shen Shi Zun Sheng Shu Bai Xian Pi decoction)
③ For plague lesions with cores and suppurating blood: Bai Xian Pi, boil and take one sheng. (Bu Que Zhou Hou Fang)
④ For postpartum stroke when the weak patient cannot take other medicines: Bai Xian Pi 3 liang. With 3 sheng of water, boil down to 1 sheng, divide and take. Those who tolerate alcohol may boil equal parts wine and water. (Xiao Pin Fang Yi Wu Bai Xian Tang)
⑤ For skin eczema and pruritus: Bai Xian Pi and Sophora root (Ku Shen) each 90 g, made into water pills. Each dose 6 g, twice daily, taken with warm water. Bai Xian Pi may also be used alone—appropriate amount decocted for external wash once or twice daily. (Qingdao Zhong Cao Yao Shou Ce)
⑥ For palmar eczema ('goose palm wind'): chew Bai Xian Pi in the mouth until mushy and rub on the hands. (Wan Shi Mi Chuan Wai Ke Xin Fa)
⑦ For acute hepatitis: Bai Xian Pi 9 g, Artemisia capillaris (Yin Chen) 15 g, Gardenia fruit (Zhi Zi) 9 g, Rhubarb (Da Huang) 9 g. Decoction. (Nei Meng Gu Zhong Cao Yao)
⑧ For postpartum wind-deficiency: Bai Xian Pi and Angelica pubescens root (Du Huo) each 3 liang. Coarsely powdered, wine and water each two cups, decoct to two cups, divide into three doses. Alternatively, Bai Xian Pi alone is also effective. (Wei Sheng Yi Jian Fang)
⑨ For traumatic bleeding: grind Bai Xian Pi into a fine powder and apply externally. (Ning Xia Zhong Cao Yao Shou Ce)
Remarks
In the Xinjiang region, the root-bark of the related species narrow-leaved Bai Xian (Xia Ye Bai Xian) is also used as Bai Xian in medicine.

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E4%B8%9C%E5%8D%97%E9%95%BF%E8%92%B4%E8%8B%A3%E8%8B%94
Name
Southeast long-fruited Lactuca (Dongnan changshuo jutai), Shima po zi grass (Shimapozicao)
Stone tea (Shicha)
Cultivation and processing of Southeast long-fruited Lactuca (Dongnan changshuo jutai)
Source
Whole herb of the plant of the family Lactucaceae, Southeast long-fruited Lactuca (Dongnan changshuo jutai). Harvested in spring and sun-dried.
Morphology
Southeast long-fruited Lactuca (Dongnan changshuo jutai) is a perennial herb. Rhizome cylindrical, about 4 cm long. Leaves 4–16, all basal; petioles 1.8–8 cm long, stout, with short coarse hairs; leaf blades papery, oblong or oblong-elliptic, 2.2–10 cm long, 1–3.6 cm wide, apex acute or slightly acute, base cuneate, margins with dense small teeth, both surfaces with short appressed hairs, lateral veins 5–7 per side. Inflorescences cymose-umbellate, 2–4, 2–3 times branched, with short appressed hairs; calyx 4.5–7 mm long, 5-lobed to the base, lobes narrow linear, abaxial surface with short appressed hairs, adaxial surface glabrous; corolla 1.5–2 cm long, abaxial surface with short soft hairs, adaxial surface nearly glabrous, narrowly campanulate, upper lip 3–5 mm long, 2-lobed to the middle, lobes obliquely flattened triangular, lower lip 3-lobed to the middle, lobes ovate; stamens glabrous, anthers elliptic, 2 staminodes degenerate, about 0.5 mm long; disc ring-shaped; pistil about 1.6 cm long, sparsely with small glands; ovary sessile, stigma flattened globose. Achene (cypsela) linear, 2–3.4 cm long, glabrous. Seeds narrowly elliptic or fusiform, 0.4–0.5 mm long. Flowering around April.
Habitat and distribution
Ecology: grows under forest in mountain valleys or on stones on mountain slopes or on rock cliffs.
Distribution: occurs in Jiangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Guangdong and other areas.
Properties and taste
Taste bitter; pungent; nature cold
Effects of Southeast long-fruited Lactuca (Dongnan changshuo jutai)
Efficacy
Whole herb of the plant of the family Lactucaceae, Southeast long-fruited Lactuca (Dongnan changshuo jutai). Mainly used for wind-heat attack, nasal congestion with nasal discharge, sneezing, cough.
Indications
Disperses wind-heat and relieves toxicity. Indicated for wind-heat invasion, nasal congestion with nasal discharge, sneezing, cough.
Usage and dosage
Internal use: decoction, 6–9 g.

Cultivation and processing of Asarum (Du Heng)
Source
This herb is the dried whole herb of the Aristolochiaceae plant Asarum forbesii Maxim., Asarum (Du Heng).
Processing
Remove dirt and other impurities from the raw material, cut into short sections, and sieve off ash and debris.
Appearance
This product appears in segments. Roots numerous, slender and cylindrical, diameter 1.5–3 mm; surface gray-yellow to gray-brown, fine longitudinal wrinkles visible, residual rootlets and rootlet scars; cross-section yellow-white.
Rhizomes irregularly nodular or cylindrical-nodular, diameter 2–3 mm, gray-brown, nodes distinct, leafstalk scars and root scars visible.
Leaves few, leaf blades mostly cut, wrinkled or broken, gray-green to brown-green; intact leaves broad cordate, apex blunt or rounded, petioles slender, gray-brown to dark brown.
Brittle in texture. Odor aromatic, especially in the roots and rhizomes; taste pungent and acrid.
Properties and channels entered
Pungent, warm; slightly toxic. Enters the Lung and Kidney channels.
Functions and indications
Dispel wind and scatter cold, relieve pain, transform phlegm and stop cough. Used for wind-cold headache, joint pain, phlegm-retention cough and asthma; externally used for toothache.
Dosage and administration
1–3 g; for external use as appropriate, grind to powder and sprinkle on the affected area.
Efficacy of Asarum (Du Heng)
Efficacy
This herb is the dried whole herb of Asarum forbesii Maxim., Asarum (Du Heng). Used for wind-cold headache, joint pain, phlegm-retention cough and asthma; externally for toothache.
Prescriptions of Asarum (Du Heng)
① For wind-cold headache and initial stages of common cold or influenza characterized by headache and fever: Horse-hoof Fragrance (Ma ti xiang) as powder, each dose one qian (about 3 g), mixed with hot wine and taken; after a short while drink a bowl of hot tea to induce sweating. (From "Xinglin Zhaiyao" — "Essentials of the Apricot Grove"; formula: Xianghan San — Fragrant Sweat Powder)
② For respiratory wheeze and asthma when there is a feeling of stagnation in the chest and disharmony in the epigastrium: Gua Di (melon pedicel) 2 fen, Asarum (Du Heng) 3 fen, Ginseng (Ren Shen) 1 fen; pound and sieve, take one qian (about 3 g) with decoction, two or three times daily. (From "Buque Zhouhou Fang" — "Supplement to the Post-Elbow Formulas")
③ For wheeze and panting: Horse-hoof Fragrance (Ma ti xiang), dry-roast and grind into fine powder, each dose 2–3 qian; if during an acute attack, mix with light vinegar and take, expect effect when phlegm and saliva are expelled. (From "Puji Fang" — "Universal Relief Formulas"; formula: Hei Ma Ti Xiang San — Black Horse-hoof Fragrance Powder)
④ For summer rashes: Asarum root (powdered) 3–4 fen. Swallow with boiling water.
⑤ For traumatic pain and snakebite: Asarum (powdered) take 2 fen each time; externally use fresh Asarum, pounded and applied to the affected area.
⑥ For snakebite: Asarum root 1–2 qian, Qingpeng leaves (Asteraceae: Artemisia species) and Zhuyexiqing leaves (Orchidaceae: striped-leaf orchid) in equal amounts, Honeysuckle (Jin Yin Hua) 3–4 qian, Yegangzi (Ye gang zi; Loganiaceae/"drunken-fish herb") 5–6 qian; decoct in water and take three times daily before meals.
⑦ For sores and toxins: Asarum root and Qingpeng leaves 1–2 qian each; pound and apply to the affected area. (Formulas 4 and following from "Zhejiang Tianmu Mountain Materia Medica")
⑧ For unnamed swellings and carbuncles, early-stage vine-carbuncle presenting as diffuse swelling without a head, hard pain without redness, and spreading lesions: seven fresh Asarum leaves, rinse briefly with boiling water, simmer for one hour, take once daily to produce slight sweating; mash the residue, heat and apply as a poultice. (From "Fujian Folk Materia Medica")
⑨ For dental caries pain: fresh Asarum leaves chewed or mashed and packed into the carious cavity. (From "Fujian Folk Materia Medica")

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%B5%AE%E8%90%8D

Cultivation and processing of duckweed
Source
This product is the dried whole herb of the Lemnaceae plant Ziping (Spirodela polyrrhiza (L.) Schleid.). Collected from June to September, washed clean, impurities removed, sun-dried.
Taste and property
Pungent, cold.
Characteristics
This product is a flattened leaf-like body, ovate or ovoid, major axis 2–5 mm. Upper surface pale green to gray-green, slightly lateral with one small depression, margin even or slightly curled. Lower surface purple-green to purple-brown, bearing several adventitious roots. Light in weight, easily crushed between fingers. Slight odor, bland taste.
Effects of duckweed
Functions
This product is the dried whole herb of the Lemnaceae plant Ziping.
Main indications: epidemic febrile diseases, rashes that do not surface, wind-heat urticaria, skin itching, edema, urinary retention, sores and ringworm, erysipelas, burns.
Channels
Enter
Lung channel
.
Indications
Induce sweating, dispel wind, promote urination, clear heat, detoxify. Treat epidemic febrile diseases, rashes that do not surface, wind-heat urticaria, skin itching, edema, urinary retention, sores and ringworm, erysipelas, burns.
① Benjing (The Classic of Materia Medica): treats violent fever with body itching, expels water qi, superior to wine, promotes beard and hair growth, stops wasting-thirst.
② Bie Lu (Collected Records): brings down qi; used in baths to promote hair growth.
③ Tang Bencao (Tang Materia Medica): treats fire sores.
④ Bencao Shiyi (Supplement to Materia Medica): powdered and applied to the face; crushed juice taken internally treats edema and promotes urination; for poisoning, take dried pingzi powder and take a small spoonful with wine; also used as an ointment to promote hair growth.
⑤ Rihuazi Bencao (Rihuazi Materia Medica): treats heat-toxin wind-heat diseases, heat delirium, melting swellings and toxins, scalds and fire sores, wind rashes.
⑥ Bencao Tujing (Illustrated Materia Medica): treats epidemic febrile diseases, also capable of inducing sweating.
⑦ Diannan Bencao (South Yunnan Materia Medica): induces sweating, detoxifies. Treats scabies, tinea, and dispels wind causing skin itching.
⑧ Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica): treats wind-damp paralysis, beriberi, contusions and injuries, eye redness and membranes, mouth and tongue ulcers, vomiting blood, nosebleed, apoplectic paralysis, erysipelas.
⑨ Yuqiu Yaojie (Yuqiu's Medicinal Explanations): pungent and cooling to release the exterior. Treats epidemic rashes, stroke with facial deviation, paralysis; treats boils and hot swellings, hidden rashes and itching, yangmei-like lesions, acne, tinea versicolor.
⑩ Lingnan Caiyao Lu (Lingnan Drug Collection): for sufferers of wind-itch bathe several times with purple-backed duckweed; for water toxin causing hands and feet up to elbows and knees to be cold, decoct and wash with it.
⑾ Zhongguo Yaoshi Tujian (Illustrated Guide to Chinese Medicinal Plants): crush and apply the juice to insect bites.
Dosage and administration
Internal: decoct, 3–9 g, fresh 15–30 g; or crush and drink the juice; or include in pills or powders.
External: appropriate amount, decoct for fumigating washes; grind to powder and sprinkle or make into a paste to apply.
Precautions and contraindications
Contraindicated for those with exterior deficiency and spontaneous sweating.
1. Ben Cao Jing Shu (Commentary on the Materia Medica): do not use in exterior qi deficiency with spontaneous sweating.
2. Ben Cao Cong Xin (Newly Compiled Materia Medica): do not use lightly unless there is great excess heat.
3. Depei Bencao (Matched Materia Medica): contraindicated in blood deficiency with dry skin, and in qi deficiency with wind-induced pain.
Formulas using duckweed
① For epidemic febrile disease, to induce sweating: Duckweed herb (Fupingcao) 1 liang; Ephedra (Mahuang) (nodes removed, prepared) ½ liang, Cinnamon bark (Rougui) ½ liang, Prepared Aconite (Fuzi) (processed and split, remove navel and skin) ½ liang. Pound the four substances finely and sift. Each dose two qian; use one medium cup of water, fresh ginger half fen, decoct until reduced to six-tenths, take hot with the dregs regardless of timing. (Bencao Tujing)
② For wind-heat on the skin, widespread urticaria: Burdock seed (Niubangzi) and duckweed (Fuping or Fupingcao) equal parts. Use Mint (Bohe) decoction to take two qian, twice daily. (Yangsheng Biyong Fang)
③ For generalized weakness itching: Duckweed powder (Fuping) one qian, yellow duckweed (Huangping) one qian. Decoction with the same Four-Substance Decoction (Siwu Tang) and take. (Danxi Zuanyao)
④ For incessant thirst with vexation and irritability: aquatic duckweed (wash, sun-dry to powder), mix with human breast milk into pills the size of a wutong seed. Take regardless of timing, swallow quickly with congee thirty-nine. (Shenghui Fang)
⑤ For wasting-thirst (diabetes): dried duckweed (Fuping) and Trichosanthes root (Tianhuafen) equal parts. Powder the two ingredients, mix with human breast milk into pills the size of a wutong seed. On an empty stomach take twenty pills, three times a day. (Qianjin Fang — Duckweed Pills)
⑥ For heat toxin: crush duckweed and apply the juice all over. (Zimu Milu)
⑦ For severe wind disease phlegm: 1) Duckweed herb (Fupingcao) harvested in March, washed three to five times, fermented in a pit three to five days, baked into powder, do not expose the mouth; each dose three qian, take with warm wine before meals. 2) In July take purple-backed duckweed (Zibei fuping), sun-dry to powder, half sheng, add to Good Xiaofeng Powder (Xiaofeng San) five liang. Each dose five qian, decoct in water frequently; also use the decoction for bathing. (Shibian Liangfang)
⑧ For abscesses: an appropriate amount of Ziping or purple duckweed (Ziping/Zibei fuping), extract the juice; powdered root bark of Hongjunxiang (Shanmuxie) one tablespoon. Mix and apply externally, thin in the middle and thick on the outside, leaving a hole in the center. (Selected Single and Empirical Prescriptions)
⑨ For urinary obstruction, relieve bladder fullness and edema: surface-collected duckweed, sun-dry, powder, take a small measuring spoonful, three times a day. (Ganjin Fang)
⑩ For acute nephritis: Duckweed herb (Fupingcao) 2 liang, black soybean (Heidou) 1 liang. Decoction in water and drink. (Inner Mongolia: Selected New Medical Methods for Chinese Materia Medica)
⑾ For sores and rashes entering the eye with unbearable pain and fear of damaging the eye: Duckweed herb (Fupingcao), shade-dried to powder, one to two qian per dose; take half a jin of lamb liver, place in a basin, mash and break with a bamboo stick, add half he of water, press out the liver juice, take the medicine after meals with the liver juice. (Children’s Health Total Micro-Discussions — Duckweed Powder)
⑿ For tinea versicolor and abscess wind: purple-backed duckweed (Zibei fuping), sun-dried. Use four liang to decoct for bathing, and rub with duckweed. Alternatively add Han Fangji (Hanfangji) two qian. (Pocket Formulas)
⒀ For powdery spots on the face: small ditch duckweed, make into powder, repeat application several times. (Shenghui Fang)
⒁ To neutralize snake-venom cough entering the abdomen: crush duckweed herb (Fupingcao), squeeze the juice and drink. (Pinhui Jingyao)
⒂ For persistent nosebleed: dry duckweed herb powder, blow into the nostrils. (Shenghui Fang)
⒃ For pterygium encroaching the eye: a small amount of green duckweed (Qingping), grind to a paste, add a little animal brain, apply to the eye. (Shiyi Dexiao Fang)

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%A6%99%E8%96%B7
Name
Chinese Mosla Herb, Herb of Haichow Elsholtzia
Xiangmao (Xiangmao), Xiangrong (Xiangrong), Shixiangmao (Shixiangmao), Shixiangru (Shixiangru), Xiangrong (Xiangrong), Zihua Xiangmao (Zihua Xiangmao), Mifengcao (Mifengcao), Xiangru (Xiangru), Xiye Xiangru (Xiye Xiangru), Xiao Xiangru (Xiao Xiangru), Man Shan Xiang (Man Shan Xiang), Qing Xiangru (Qing Xiangru), Xiangru Cao (Xiangru Cao), Tu Xiangru (Tu Xiangru), Tu Xiangcao (Tu Xiangcao), Shiai (Shiai)
Xiangrong (Xiangrong)
Xiangrong (Xiangrong)
Shixiangmao (Shixiangmao)
Xiangrou (Xiangrou)
Zihua Xiangmao (Zihua Xiangmao)
Mifengcao (Mifengcao)
Xiye Xiangru (Xiye Xiangru)
Xiao Ye Xiangru (Xiao Ye Xiangru)

Tu Xiangcao (Tu Xiangcao)

Cultivation and Processing of Xiangru
Source
From the whole plant with roots or the aerial parts of Lamiaceae plants Jiang Xiangru (Jiang Xiangru) or Hua Qizhu (Hua Qizhu). Harvest when stems and leaves are luxuriant and flowers begin to open in summer and autumn, cut and shade-dry or sun-dry, and tie into small bundles.
Properties and Flavor
Taste acrid; nature slightly warm
Preparation
Pick out impurities, spray with water to moisten, remove remaining roots, cut into sections, sun-dry to obtain.
Description
This product is 30–50 cm long, base purplish red, upper part yellow-green or pale yellow, whole plant densely covered with white puberulent hairs. Stem quadrangular and cylindrical; diameter 1–2 mm, nodes distinct, internodes 4–7 cm long; brittle, breaks easily. Leaves opposite, often curled or deciduous; when leaf blades are flattened they are oblong-ovate or lanceolate, dark green or yellow-green, margins with sparse serrations. Spike inflorescences terminal and axillary, bracts broadly ovate, caducous or persistent; calyx persistent, campanulate, pale purplish red or gray-green, apex 5-lobed, densely pubescent. Nutlets 4, nearly globose, reticulate, meshes depressed forming shallow pits. Aroma clear and strong, taste slightly acrid and cool.
Effects of Xiangru
Functions
From the whole plant with roots or the aerial parts of Lamiaceae plants Jiang Xiangru (Jiang Xiangru) or Hua Qizhu (Hua Qizhu).
Main Indications
Treats cold-damp accumulation from summer, headache, fever, aversion to cold without sweating, chest fullness and epigastric and abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea, edema, beriberi.
Channels Entered
Lung channel, Stomach channel
Indications
Induces sweating and relieves summer heat, promotes urination and disperses dampness, warms the stomach and harmonizes the middle burner. Treats cold-damp accumulation in summer, headache, fever, aversion to cold without sweating, chest fullness and abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea, edema, beriberi.
① "Bielu": Treats cholera, abdominal pain with vomiting and diarrhea, disperses edema.
② Meng Shen: Dispels hot wind, sudden convulsions, can boil the juice and take it in one gulp. Also dried powder stops nasal bleeding, taken with water.
③ "Rihuazi Materia Medica": Descends qi, removes vexing heat, treats vomiting and rebellious cold qi.
④ "Luchanyan Materia Medica": Arrests seasonal cold damage.
⑤ "Ben Cao Yan Yi Supplement": Treats summer injury, promotes urination.
⑥ "Dian Nan Materia Medica": Releases the exterior and expels pathogenic factors, treats summer heat headache, summer diarrhea and intestinal pain, summer-heat cough, induces sweating, warms the stomach, harmonizes the middle.
⑦ Wang Ying "Food Materia Medica": Boiled as a beverage instead of tea in summer, can prevent febrile disease, harmonize the middle and warm the stomach; hold the juice and gargle to remove bad breath.
⑧ "Compendium": Treats beriberi cold and heat.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 3–9 g; or used in pills or powders, or decocted and used as a gargle.
External use: appropriate amount, pounded and applied.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated for those with exterior deficiency.
1. "Ben Cao Cong Xin": Do not use when there is no external pathogenic factor.
2. "De Pei Materia Medica": Contraindicated for those with vigorous fire and qi deficiency, or yin deficiency with heat.
Formulas of Xiangru
① For disharmony of spleen and stomach, oppression and fullness of the chest and diaphragm, internal contraction by wind-cold, external invasion of cold pathogenic factors, aversion to cold with fever, body aches and limb fatigue, cholera vomiting, spleen pain with inverted stomach, drunkenness unaroused, seasonal cold headache: Xiangru (stolized soil removed) 2 liang, Licorice (Gancao) (honey-fried) 0.5 liang, White Hyacinth Bean (Bai Bian Dou) (stir-fried), Magnolia Bark (Houpo) (peeled, ginger-juice fried), Poria Shen (Fushen) each 1 liang. Grind into fine powder. Each dose 2 qian, pour boiling soup in and take with salt. (Jufang Xiangru Decoction)
② For cholera with vomiting and diarrhea, limb vexation and pain, cold sweat, great thirst: Xiangru 2 liang, Liaozi 1 liang. Coarsely pound and sieve the two ingredients. Each dose 2 qian, water one cup, decoct to seven-tenths, remove dregs and take warm, three times daily. (Shengji Zong Lu Xiangru Decoction)
③ For cholera abdominal pain, vomiting and dysentery: fresh Xiangru (cut) 1 sheng, small garlic 1 sheng (crushed), Magnolia Bark (Houpo) 6 liang (roasted), Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 10 liang. Cut the four ingredients, use one dou of water, boil to obtain 3 sheng, divide into three doses; causes vomiting and dysentery to stop, each dose must be warm. (Emergency Formulas Xiangru Decoction)
④ For sudden edema from water-retention, or water in sores, whole-body swelling: dry Xiangru 1 jin, Atractylodes Rhizome (Baizhu) 7 liang. Pound the two and sift; concentrate boil Xiangru to obtain juice, mix with Baizhu to form pills the size of a parasitic seed. Each dose 10 pills, take four to five times day and night, very effective to promote urination. In summer using flowers and leaves together is also good. Avoid grass carp, seaweed, mustard greens, peaches, plums, and sparrow meat. (Sengshen Collection Xiangru Baizhu Pills)
⑤ For sudden small holes appearing on the tongue bleeding as if drilled: drink one sheng of Xiangru juice three times daily. (Zhouhoufang)
⑥ For summer heat injury (lying damp and exposed to wind in summer, or excessive raw cold intake, headache, fever, cramps, dry retching, cold limbs, etc.): Xiangru 1 jin, Magnolia Bark (Houpo) (ginger-juice fried), White Hyacinth Bean (Bai Bian Dou) (slightly fried) each 0.5 jin, shred and pulverize. Each dose 5 qian, add 2 bowls of water and 0.5 bowl of wine, decoct to one bowl, let cool in water to settle and take. Take two doses consecutively, very effective. This formula is called Xiangru Drink. The biandou in the formula can be replaced with Coptis (Huanglian) (ginger-juice fried).
⑦ Edema: Xiangru 50 jin, chop into pot, add water and simmer for a long time, remove dregs and concentrate boil until can be rolled into pills the size of a paulownia seed. Each dose 5 pills, taken three times a day; dose may be increased a little each day until urination is smooth. This formula is called Xiangru Decoction. Another formula: Xiangru leaves 1 jin, water 1 dou, boil until soft, remove dregs and reduce to a paste, add 7 liang of Baizhu powder and make into pills the size of a paulownia seed. Each dose 10 pills, take with rice soup. This formula is called Deep Master Xiangru Baizhu Pills.
⑧ For vexation and rib-side pain: pound Xiangru and take 1–2 sheng of juice.
⑨ For unstoppable nasal bleeding: grind Xiangru and take one qian with water.
⑩ For summer-heat vexation and thirst: Xiangru 2 liang. Pound into a powder, each dose 2 qian, water one cup, decoct to seven-tenths, do not remove dregs, take warm at any time. (Shengji Zong Lu Xiangru Powder)
⑾ For water diseases with massive swelling, abdominal fullness, poor appetite: dry Xiangru 50 jin. Finely chop and place in inner pot, cover with water to immerse Xiangru several cun, boil, remove dregs, clarify, reduce over low fire until can be made into pills, take 5 pills the size of paulownia seeds three times daily, gradually increase so that urination is smooth. No worry. (Waitai)
⑿ For infantile localized alopecia areata with no hair growth, sweating and severe pain: concentrate boil old Xiangru juice a little, mix with fat and lead white and apply. (Zimu Secret Records)
⒀ For halitosis: one handful of Xiangru, boil with one dou of water, obtain 3 sheng, slightly swish and gargle. (Qianjin Yaofang)
⒁ For multiple boils and prickly heat: fresh Hua Qizhu appropriate amount, pound and apply externally. (Jiangxi Herbal Manual)
⒂ For skin itching and vulvar eczema: whole plant Hua Qizhu appropriate amount, decoct and wash externally. (Zhejiang Medicinal Plant Records)
⒃ Sword Bean Xiangru Drink:
Sword bean seeds 25 g, Xiangru 10 g, Licorice (Gancao) 3 g. Decoction of the above three herbs in water, add appropriate rock sugar or honey to taste, drink.
Functions
Releases the exterior and warms the middle.

Ephedra (Ma Huang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%BA%BB%E9%BB%84
Name
Ephedra
Longsha, Gougu, Beixiang, Beiyan
Longsha
Beixiang
Beiyan
Herbaceous Ephedra (Cǎo Máhuáng)
Mawang
Red root
Honey-fried Ephedra (Zhì Máhuáng)
Cultivation and preparation of Ephedra (Máhuáng)
Source
Derived from the herbaceous stems of Ephedraceae plants: herbaceous Ephedra (Cǎo Máhuáng), Mùzéi Ephedra (Mùzéi Máhuáng) or medium Ephedra (Zhōng Máhuáng). Between August and October cut the green slender branches, or pull up with roots, remove soil and roots, place in a ventilated location to air-dry or dry until about 60 percent dry, then sun-dry. Store in a dry, ventilated place; protect from moisture and mildew.
Nature and Taste
Acrid, slightly bitter, warm.
Processing
1. Ephedra (Máhuáng): pick out impurities, remove all woody stems and residual roots, wash with water, slightly moisten, then cut into sections and dry to obtain.
2. Ephedra floss (Máhuáng róng): take clean Ephedra (Máhuáng) that has been processed and chopped, place in a grinding trough, and grind until the fibers loosen and form a floss-like texture.
3. Honey-treated Ephedra (Mì Máhuáng): take Ephedra sections, add cooked refined honey and a little boiling water, mix evenly, let steam slightly, place in a pot and stir-fry over low heat until not sticky to the touch, remove and cool. (Per 100 jin of Ephedra sections, use 10–15 jin of refined cooked honey)
Characteristics
1. Herbaceous Ephedra (Cǎo Máhuáng)
Also called: field Ephedra. Stems are slender, cylindrical and slightly compressed, with few branches, diameter about 1–2 mm, usually cut into small sections about 2–3 cm long. Surface pale green to yellow-green, with fine longitudinal ridges, slightly rough to the touch, nodes obvious, internodes 2.5–6 cm long. Nodes bear two membranous scale leaves (rarely three), about 3–4 mm long; upper part gray-white, acuminate, triangular, tips reflexed, bases brown-red, fused into a tubular sheath. Stem brittle and easily broken; fracture slightly fibrous, outer ring greenish-yellow, central pith red-brown. Slight aromatic odor, taste slightly bitter-astringent.
2. Mùzéi Ephedra (Mùzéi Máhuáng)
Stems are slender and cylindrical, highly branched, slightly finer than herbaceous Ephedra, diameter about 1–1.5 mm. Surface grass-green to yellow-green, with longitudinal ridges, not rough to the touch, internodes 1.5–3 cm long. Nodes bear two (rarely three) membranous scale leaves about 1–2 mm long; upper part short triangular, gray-white, tips mostly not reflexed, bases brown-red to dark brown, united into a tubular sheath. Otherwise similar to the above species.
3. Medium Ephedra (Zhōng Máhuáng)
Stems slender and cylindrical, diameter 1.5–3 mm, whole plant yellow-green, nodes bear three membranous scale leaves in whorls about 2–3 mm long, gray-white with acute tips, internodes 2–6 cm long, rough to the touch.
Among the three, the best specimens are those that are dry, have thick stems, pale green color, solid cores, and a bitter-astringent taste.
Actions of Ephedra (Máhuáng)
Efficacy
Derived from the herbaceous stems of Ephedraceae plants such as herbaceous Ephedra (Cǎo Máhuáng), Mùzéi Ephedra (Mùzéi Máhuáng) or medium Ephedra (Zhōng Máhuáng).
Main indications: treats exterior excess in cold damage (shanghan) presenting with fever, aversion to cold and absence of sweating, headache, nasal congestion, pain of bones and joints; cough and asthma; wind-water edema with difficult urination; stubborn wind-bi causing numbness of the skin; wind rashes and pruritus.
Channels (Meridians)
Enters
Lung channel, Bladder channel.
Indications
Induces sweating, calms wheezing, and promotes urination. Treats exterior excess of cold damage with fever, aversion to cold and absence of sweating, headache, nasal congestion, and pain of bones and joints; cough and asthma; wind-water edema with difficulty urinating; stubborn wind-bi, skin numbness, and itchy wind rashes.
1. Benjing (The Classic Materia Medica): treats windstroke, headache from cold damage, and warm malaria. Induces sweating to release the exterior and expel pathogenic heat, stops rebellious cough and breath, dispels cold and heat, and dissolves hard accumulations.
2. Bielu: treats urgent and sluggish pathogenic qi of the five viscera, flank pain due to wind, residual afflictions of the breast. Stops excessive salivation, opens the interstices, releases the muscles; drains out noxious qi, disperses red and black spots and toxins.
3. Yaoxing Lun: treats stubborn toxic wind-bi on the body, causing numbness of skin and flesh.
4. Rihuazi Materia Medica: unblocks the nine orifices, regulates the blood vessels, and resists mountainous mists and miasma.
5. Zhenzhu Nang: drains excess in the protective qi, dispels cold from the nutritive qi, and induces sweating of the Taiyang and Shaoyin.
6. Diannan Materia Medica: treats nasal orifices blocked and obstructed, inability to smell fragrances, and lung-cold cough.
7. Compendium of Materia Medica (Bencao Gangmu): disperses red swollen painful eyes, treats edema, wind-swelling, and postpartum blood stasis.
8. Scientific Folk Herbs: treats asthma, hay fever, pertussis, bronchitis, etc.
9. Modern Practical Chinese Medicine: effective for joint pain.
10. Identification Methods of Chinese Medicine Properties: treats abdominal pain, diarrhea, hernia, eye disorders and common colds.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 1.5–10 g; or incorporated into pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, grind to powder for nasal insufflation or apply powdered.
Raw use: strong diaphoretic power; use for inducing sweating and promoting urination.
Honey-fried use: weaker diaphoretic power; honey-frying also moistens the Lung, stops cough and calms wheezing, and is commonly used.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated in those constitutionally weak who have spontaneous sweating, night sweats, or chronic asthma.
1. Ben Cao Jing Ji Zhu: Magnolia bark (Hòupò) is used as an assistant. Incompatible with Magnolia flower bud (Xìnyí) and Pyrrosia (Shíwéi).
2. Bielu: should not be taken in large amounts; it causes debility.
3. Shu Materia Medica: Baiwei (Bái Wēi) is used as an assistant.
4. Introduction to Medicine: contraindicated in common colds with sweating and in those with yin deficiency or digestive impairment.
5. Ben Cao Jing Shu: contraindicated in exterior deficiency with spontaneous sweating, yin deficiency with night sweating; in lung deficiency with heat and abundant phlegm causing nasal obstruction; in sores with severe heat not due to cold stagnation; in debilitated persons with wind-cold, qi-deficient asthma; in yin-deficiency with blazing fire causing dizziness and headache; in southern windstroke paralysis, and in people with chronic yang deficiency and loose interstices.
Formulas of Ephedra (Máhuáng)
1. For Taiyang disease with headache and fever, body and lumbar pain, pain of bones and joints, aversion to wind without sweating and wheezing: Ephedra (Máhuáng) 3 liang (remove nodes),
Cinnamon twig (Guìzhī)
2 liang (peel removed),
Licorice (Gāncǎo)
1 liang (honey-fried), Apricot kernel (Xìngrén)
Bitter apricot kernel (Kǔ Xìngrén)
70 pieces (peel and tips removed). The above four ingredients: with 9 sheng of water, first boil Ephedra, reduce by 2 sheng, remove the scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 2.5 sheng, strain off dregs, warm dose 8 hé, cover to induce slight sweating; no need to sip gruel. (From Treatise on Cold Damage (Shāng Hán Lùn): Ma Huang Tang)
2. For Taiyang disease after sweating where Gui Zhi Tang should not be given, sweat produced and wheezing without great fever: Ephedra (Máhuáng) 4 liang (remove nodes), Apricot kernel (Xìngrén)
Bitter apricot kernel (Kǔ Xìngrén)
50 pieces (peel and tips removed), Licorice (Gāncǎo)
2 liang (honey-fried), Gypsum (Shígāo)
Half jin (crushed, wrapped in cotton). The above four ingredients: with 7 sheng of water, boil Ephedra until reduced by 2 sheng, remove the scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 2 sheng, strain, warm and take 1 shēng. (From Treatise on Cold Damage: Ma Huang Xing Ren Gan Cao Shi Gao Tang)
3. For disease with whole-body pain, fever worse in the evening, called wind-damp, resulting from exposure to wind after sweating or long injury from cold: Ephedra (remove nodes) 0.5 liang (soak in decoction),
Licorice (Gāncǎo)
1 liang (honey-fried),
Coix seed (Yìyǐrén)
0.5 liang, Apricot kernel (Xìngrén)
10 pieces (peel and tips removed, stir-fried). Grind the above into coarse powder; each dose 4 qian, with 1 cup and a half of water, decoct to 80 percent, strain and take warm; produces slight sweat and avoid wind. (From Essentials from the Golden Cabinet (Jīn Guì Yào Lüè): Ma Huang Xing Ren Yi Yi Gan Cao Tang)
4. For wind-bi with obstruction of the nutritive and defensive qi, limb pain: Ephedra 5 liang (remove roots and nodes, measured), Cinnamomi Cortex (Rou Gui)
2 liang. Pound and sift into a powder, decoct with 2 sheng of wine over low heat until syrupy. Each dose taken at any time, mixed with hot wine, one teaspoon administered frequently, sweating as the guide. (From Sheng Hui Fang)
5. For cold damage with heat emerging exterior and jaundice: Ephedra 3 liang, cook in pure wine 5 sheng, decoct to obtain 1.5 sheng and take all, warm; sweating indicates cure. In winter use clear wine; in spring water is suitable. (From Qian Jin Fang: Ephedra with Pure Wine Decoction)
6. For common cold wind-cold with nasal obstruction, heavy voice and inability to speak; or wind-cold headache and dizziness, limb stiffness and fatigue, cough with abundant phlegm and chest fullness and shortness of breath: Ephedra (nodes not removed), Apricot kernel (Xìngrén) (skins and tips not removed), Licorice (Gāncǎo) (raw) in equal parts. Make a coarse powder; each dose 5 qian with 1 cup and a half of water, add 5 slices of ginger, decoct to one cup, strain and take warm, cover with clothing and blankets to sleep and produce slight sweat. (From Local Formulary: San Ao Tang)
7. For pustular sores that collapse and become black: Ephedra (cut off nodes) 0.5 liang, stir-fry with one spoon of honey for a long time, decoct with half a sheng of water, when boiling remove the scum and decoct again until reduced by one-third, do not use the dregs. Take while hot, avoid wind, and observe for sores to reemerge. Another method uses clear yellow wine for decoction; children who cannot drink wine may find it hard to take, though effect is faster. (From Ben Cao Yan Yi Sheng)
8. For simultaneous Taiyang and Shaoyin pattern where fever returns and the pulse is deep: Ephedra 2 liang (remove nodes), Asarum (Xìxīn)
2 liang, Prepared Aconite (Fùzǐ)
one piece (processed, peel removed, broken into eight pieces). The three ingredients: with one dou of water, first boil Ephedra reducing by 2 sheng, remove scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 2 sheng, strain and take warm one shēng three times daily. (From Treatise on Cold Damage: Ma Huang Fu Zi Tang with Xi Xin)
9. For cold damage exterior not relieved, water accumulation under the heart, dry vomiting, fever with cough, or thirst, or diarrhea, or choking sensation, or difficult urination, or lower abdominal fullness, or wheezing: Ephedra (remove nodes), White peony (Bái Sháo), Asarum (Xìxīn), Dried ginger (Gānjiāng), Licorice (Gāncǎo) (honey-fried), Cinnamon twig (Guìzhī) (peel removed) each 2 liang, Schisandra (Wǔwèizǐ)
half sheng, Pinellia (Bànxià)
half sheng (washed). The above eight ingredients: with one dou of water, first boil Ephedra, reduce by 2 sheng, remove scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 3 sheng, strain and take warm 1 shēng. (From Treatise on Cold Damage: Xiao Qing Long Tang)
10. For cough and asthma with upward qi, throat producing gurgling watery sounds: Belamcanda (Shègān)
13 pieces, Ephedra 4 liang, Fresh ginger (Shēngjiāng)
4 liang, Asarum (Xìxīn),
Aster (Zǐwǎn),
Coltsfoot flower (Kuǎndōnghuā)
each 3 liang, Schisandra (Wǔwèizǐ)
half sheng, Jujube (Dàzǎo)
7 pieces, Pinellia (large pieces, washed)
8 pieces. The above nine ingredients: with 1 dou 2 sheng of water, first boil Ephedra for two boils, remove scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 3 sheng, divide into three warm doses. (From Jīn Guì Yào Lüè: She Gan Ma Huang Tang)
11. For wind-water or pernicious wind causing whole-body swelling, floating pulse, no thirst, continuous spontaneous sweating without high fever: Ephedra 6 liang, Gypsum (Shígāo)
half jin, Fresh ginger (Shēngjiāng)
3 liang, Jujube (Dàzǎo)
15 pieces, Licorice (Gāncǎo)
2 liang. The above five ingredients: with 6 sheng of water, first boil Ephedra, remove scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 3 sheng, take three warm doses. (From Jīn Guì Yào Lüè: Yue Bi Tang)
12. For water disease with deep small pulse belonging to Shaoyin: Ephedra 3 liang, Licorice (Gāncǎo)
2 liang, Prepared Aconite (Fùzǐ)
one piece (processed). The three ingredients: with 7 sheng of water, first boil Ephedra, remove scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 2.5 sheng, warm dose 8 fen, take three times daily. (From Jīn Guì Yào Lüè: Ma Huang Fu Zi Tang)
13. For water qi disease with skin edema without sweating: Licorice (Gāncǎo)
2 liang, Ephedra 4 liang. The two ingredients: with 5 sheng of water, first boil Ephedra, remove scum, add Licorice, decoct to obtain 3 sheng, warm dose 1 shēng. If sweating recurs but no sweat, take again; be cautious of wind-cold. (From Jīn Guì Yào Lüè: Gan Cao Ma Huang Tang)
14. For windstroke with hand and foot rigidity, pain in all joints, vexation and agitation with aversion to cold, prolonged lack of desire to eat: Ephedra 30 zhu, Radix Angelicae Pubescentis (Dúhuó)
1 liang, Asarum (Xìxīn)
12 zhu, Astragalus (Huángqí)
12 zhu, Scutellaria (Huángqín)
18 zhu. Pound the five ingredients and decoct with 5 sheng of water to obtain 2 sheng, divide into two doses; one dose produces slight sweat, the second produces profuse sweat. (From Qian Jin Yao Fang quoting Zhang Zhongjing: Three Huang Decoction)
15. For cold damage with internal stasis heat causing yellowish body color: Ephedra 2 liang (remove nodes), Forsythia (Liánqiào)
2 liang, Apricot kernel 40 pieces (peel and tips removed), Adzuki bean (Chìxiǎodòu)
1 sheng, Jujube 12 pieces (broken), raw catalpa bark (Shēng zǐ bái pí)
1 sheng (cut), Fresh ginger 2 liang (sliced), Licorice (Gāncǎo)
2 liang (honey-fried). The above eight ingredients: with one dou of water, first boil Ephedra until boiling, remove scum, add the other herbs, decoct to obtain 3 sheng, strain and divide into three warm doses to be taken within half a day. (From Treatise on Cold Damage: Ma Huang Lian Qiao Chi Xiao Dou Tang)
16. For internal stagnation of fluid reaching the heart causing palpitations: Pinellia and Ephedra in equal parts. Grind into powder, bind with refined honey into pills the size of a small bean. Take three pills per dose, three times daily. (From Jīn Guì Yào Lüè: Ban Xia Ma Huang Wan)
17. For people who are excessively sleepy and like to sleep: Ephedra and Atractylodes (Shú) each five fen, Licorice (Gāncǎo)
three fen. Pound into powder; take one small amount (about one quarter teaspoon) three times daily. (From Zhou Hou Fang)
18. For copious phlegm and all yin sores, diffuse swellings without heads, flattened white depressed ulcers: Ephedra 5 fen, Prepared Rehmannia (Shú Dì Huáng)
1 liang, White mustard seed (Bái Jièzǐ)
2 qian (stir-fried and ground), Prepared ginger charcoal 5 fen, Licorice 1 qian, Cinnamon bark 1 qian, Deer glue 3 qian. Decoction taken with water. (From Wai Ke Quan Sheng Ji: Yang He Tang)
19. For scabies sores: lard 4 liang, Banmao (Mylabris) 3 pieces, Ephedra 5 qian, Castor seeds (shelled and pounded) 100 pieces, Large hemp seeds (Dà fēng zǐ) (shelled and pounded) 100 pieces. First melt the lard, add banmao and boil several times, then remove banmao, add Ephedra and boil until dry, strain off residue, mix with the pounded hemp and castor seed flesh and apply to the affected area. (From Medical Heart Enlightenment: Ma Huang Ointment)
20. For alcoholic rhinophyma: Ephedra and Ephedra root each 2 liang, five jars of top-grade wine. Put the herbs into the wine and decoct for the time of three incense coils, leave overnight, and drink 3–5 cups each morning and evening. (From Yizong Jinjian: Ma Huang Lung-Opening Wine)
21. For internal and external eye obstructions: Ephedra 1 liang, Angelica sinensis root (Dāngguī shēn) 1 qian. Grind the two into a coarse powder, fry until black, add a little musk and frankincense, and make a fine powder. Moisten and place in the nostril (for nasal insufflation). (From Lan Shi Mi Cang: Ma Huang Powder for Nasal Insufflation)
22. For unilateral eye pain and head wind: Ephedra (burned to ash) 0.5 liang, potash nitre (pén xiāo) 2.5 qian, a small amount of musk and bezoar. Make a fine powder and insufflate through the nostril. (From Xi Ji Fang: Ru Sheng San)
Dietary Therapy
Ephedra and Apricot Porridge
Ephedra 5 g, Apricot kernel 15 g, milled rice 100 g. Decoction of Ephedra with water, remove scum and dregs; peel and trim the apricot kernels (preferably sweet apricot kernels), place in the decoction and cook 6–7 minutes, then add the milled rice and cook into porridge, then consume.
Efficacy: Acrid-warm to release the exterior, transforms phlegm and stops cough.

Fire-charred Mother Herb (Huo Tan Mu Cao)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%81%AB%E7%82%AD%E6%AF%8D%E8%8D%89
Names
Fire-charcoal-hair (Essentials of the Nature of Raw Medicinal Herbs), Black Charcoal Seed (Extended Illustrated Examination of Plant Names and Substances), Medicine Transporter (Classified Nature of Medicinal Herbs), Mountain Buckwheat Grass (Fujian Folk Medicinal Herbs), Yellow Eel Vine, Dizzying Medicine (Sichuan Materia Medica), Black White Rice Grass (Quanzhou Materia Medica), Fire-charcoal Star, Magpie Sugar Plum (Lingnan Materia Medica), Red Earth Benefit, Black Rice Vine, Water Sandthorn Seed, Quail Cormorant Rice, Water-Reducing Sha (Fujian Chinese Medicinals), Red Plum-leaf, White Rice Grass, Large-leaf Sandbank (Guangdong Chinese Medicinals), Mouse Sugarcane (Guangxi Chinese Medicinals).
Cultivation and Processing of Fire-charcoal-mother Herb
Source
The whole herb of a Polygonaceae plant, Fire-charcoal-mother Herb. Harvested in summer and autumn, sun-dried.
[Morphology]
A perennial erect or semi-climbing herbaceous plant, about 1.5 meters long. Stems slightly winged with ridges, smooth or sparsely haired or glandular-hairy, reclining on the ground or clinging to supports, lower part woody, often branched, prostrate individuals root at the nodes, young branches purple-red. Leaves alternate, petiolate, with a winged petiole; leaf blades ovate-elliptic or ovate-triangular, 7–12 centimeters long, entire or with fine rounded teeth, base truncate, rounded or nearly cordate, sometimes with two auriculate lobes; upper-branch leaves cordate, with short petioles or sessile and clasping the stem; upper surface fresh green or with V-shaped dark markings, underside with hairs along the main vein; stipule sheaths membranous, obliquely truncate. Capitate inflorescences, further arranged into panicles or umbel-like clusters, inflorescence axis often with pustular hairs, without an involucre; bracts smooth, usually acuminate; small flowers white, pale red, or purple; perianth 5-parted; stamens 8; ovary superior, style 3-cleft. Achenes ovoid, black, three-angled, enclosed by persistent perianth. Flowering in September (Sichuan).
[Habitat and Distribution]
Grows on sunny grassy slopes, forest edges, and roadside moist soils in hilly areas. Distributed in Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, and Guizhou. Produced in Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Fujian and other regions.
Taste and Nature
Sour and sweet, cold.
① Illustrated Materia Medica: taste sour, neutral, non-toxic.
② Compendium of Essential Tastes: taste sour and sweet, nature neutral, non-toxic.
③ Compendium (Bencao Gangmu): sour, neutral, toxic.
④ Essentials of the Nature of Raw Medicinal Herbs: taste sour, nature cold.
⑤ Guangxi Chinese Medicinals: taste slightly sour and slightly astringent, nature slightly cold.
Characteristics
Dried stems very long, brown to brown-purple, with longitudinal wrinkles, internodes rather long, nodes swollen; brittle and easily broken, pith loose. Leaf blades wrinkled, dried yellow or yellow-green, purple-black patches on both sides of the midrib, faintly visible; stipule sheaths tawny yellow-brown, often broken and incomplete. Smell faint, taste slightly bitter. Best when dry and free of impurities.
Effects of Fire-charcoal-mother Herb
Functions
The whole herb of a Polygonaceae plant, Fire-charcoal-mother Herb. Used for diarrhea, dysentery, jaundice, wind-heat sore throat, weakness with dizziness, summer fever in children, convulsions, female leukorrhea, abscesses and damp sores, and traumatic injuries.
Indications
Clears heat and drains dampness, cools the blood and resolves toxicity. Treats diarrhea, dysentery, jaundice, wind-heat sore throat, weakness with dizziness, summer convulsions in children, convulsions, female leukorrhea, abscesses and damp sores, and traumatic injuries.
① Illustrated Materia Medica: dispels wind-heat from the skin, leucorrhea, and painful swollen joints and abscesses of the bones and joints.
② Essentials of the Nature of Raw Medicinal Herbs: stir-fried with honey and eaten can stop dysentery. Apply to sores, apply to bruises, paste on ulcerated feet, draw out toxins, dry exudation, and promote closure.
③ Lingnan Collection of Medicinal Herbs: treats childhood febrile convulsions and abdominal distention.
④ Fujian Folk Medicinal Herbs: activates blood, resolves toxicity, stops dysentery, treats leukorrhea.
⑤ Sichuan Materia Medica: treats dizziness and blurred vision, qi deficiency and tinnitus.
⑥ Guangzhou Military Common Chinese Medicinals Handbook: clears and drains damp-heat, reduces stagnation and resolves toxicity. Treats dysentery, enteritis, indigestion, hepatitis, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, boils and abscesses, traumatic sprains, dermatitis, eczema, and itching.
⑦ Nanchuan Common Chinese Medicinals Handbook: tonifies qi and activates blood circulation, dispels wind and clears heat. Treats weakness, wind-heat conditions, dizziness, and pain from blood and qi stagnation.
⑧ Guangdong Chinese Medicinals: cools the blood and resolves toxicity. Treats childhood summer heat.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoct, 9–15 g; fresh material 30–60 g.
External use: appropriate amount, pounded and applied; or decocted water for washing.
Formulas Using Fire-charcoal-mother Herb
① For red and white dysentery: Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao) and
Sea Gold Sand (Hai jin sha) pounded to extract juice, diluted with boiling water, add a little sugar and take. (Lingnan Collection of Medicinal Herbs)
② For dysentery, enteritis, indigestion: Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao), Little Phoenix-tail (Xiao feng wei), Cloth-dregs Leaf (Bu zha ye) each six qian, decoct in water and take. (Guangdong Selected Prescriptions of Chinese Medicinals)
③ For acute and chronic bacillary dysentery: Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao), Wild Rose Mallow (Ye mu dan) each two liang. Decoction in water, one dose daily, divided into three portions. For chronic bacillary dysentery, the same dosages can be used as a retention enema twice daily, seven to ten days per course. (Guangxi New Therapies of Chinese Medicinals Prescription Collection)
④ For damp-heat jaundice: Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao) one liang,
Chicken-bone Herb (Ji gu cao) one liang, decoct in water and take. (Guangxi Chinese Medicinals)
⑤ For female leukorrhea: fresh Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao) two to three liang, white
Cockscomb Flower (Bai ji guan hua) three to five blooms. Add water as appropriate, decoct to half a bowl, take after meals, twice daily. (Fujian Folk Medicinal Herbs)
⑥ For skin wind-heat, leucorrhea, and painful swollen joints and abscesses of bones and joints: Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao) leaves, decocted water for washing. (Lingnan Collection of Medicinal Herbs)
⑦ For abdominal distention: Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao), decocted water for fumigation and washing and pounded application. (Lingnan Collection of Medicinal Herbs)
⑧ For abscesses: fresh Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao) one liang, decocted in water, adjusted with wine and taken; the dregs mixed with honey or glutinous rice and pounded, applied to the affected area. (Fujian Chinese Medicinals)
⑨ For eczema: fresh Fire-charcoal-mother Herb (Huo tan mu cao) one to two liang, decoct and take; also take fresh whole herb, decoct and wash. (Fujian Chinese Medicinals)

Forsythia (Lian Qiao)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%BF%9E%E7%BF%98
Name
Forsythia Fruit
Lianqiao pericarp (Lianke), Yellow-flower strip (Huanghuatiao), Yellow-chain-flower (Huangliantiaohua), Huangqidan (Huangqidan), Green Lianqiao (Qingqiao), Fallen Lianqiao (Luoqiao)
Lianqiao pericarp (Lianke)
Yellow-flower strip (Huanghuatiao)
Yellow-chain-flower (Huangliantiaohua)
Huangqidan (Huangqidan)
Green Lianqiao (Qingqiao)
Fallen Lianqiao (Luoqiao)
Lianzhao (Lianzhao)
Old Lianqiao (Laoqiao)
Yiqiao (Yiqiao)
Forsythia pericarp (Lianqiao ke)
Sanlian (Sanlian)
Yiqiao (Yiqiao)
Lianqiao tree (Lianqiao)
Forsythia core (seed) (Lianqiao xin)
Large Lianqiao fruit (Daqiaozi)
Cultivation and Processing of Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao)
Source
This product is the dried fruit of the Oleaceae plant Forsythia suspensa (Thunb.) Vahl (Lianqiao). Fruits are harvested in autumn when they are beginning to ripen and still green; impurities are removed, they are steamed, then sun-dried, commonly called "green Lianqiao" (Qingqiao); when fruits are fully ripe they are harvested, sun-dried and impurities removed, commonly called "old Lianqiao" (Laoqiao).
Taste and Properties
Bitter, slightly cold.
Description
The product is oblong-ovoid to ovoid, slightly flattened, 1.5–2.5 cm long, 0.5–1.3 cm in diameter. The surface has irregular longitudinal wrinkles and numerous raised small spots, and there is one obvious longitudinal groove on each side. The apex is acuminate; the base has a small fruit stalk or it may have fallen off. Green Lianqiao mostly does not split, surface greenish-brown, fewer raised gray-white small spots, hard texture; seeds numerous, yellow-green, slender, with a wing on one side. Old Lianqiao splits from the apex or into two valves, surface yellow-brown or red-brown, inner surface mostly pale yellow-brown, smooth, with a longitudinal septum; brittle; seeds brown and mostly fallen out. Slight aromatic odor, bitter taste.
Effects of Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao)
Functions
This product is the dried fruit of the Oleaceae plant Forsythia (Lianqiao).
Main indications: warm-heat disorders, erysipelas, rashes, carbuncles and toxic swellings, scrofula, painful urinary dribbling/strangury.
Channels Entered
Enters the Lung meridian, Heart meridian, and Small Intestine meridian.
Indications
Clears heat, resolves toxicity, disperses nodules, reduces swelling. Treats warm-heat disorders, erysipelas, rashes, carbuncles and toxic swellings, scrofula, painful urinary dribbling/strangury.
1. Benjing: "Treats chills and fever, shu-wei, scrofula, carbuncles, malignant sores, goiter, and heat accumulations."
2. Bielu: "Expels white parasites."
3. Yaoxinglun: "Facilitates the five types of urinary dribbling, relieves urinary retention, removes pathogenic heat invading the heart."
4. Rihuazi Materia Medica: "Opens the small intestine, drains pus. Treats sores and boils, relieves pain, and unblocks the menses."
5. Li Gao: "Disperses blood stasis and qi accumulations in the channels; reduces swelling."
6. Wang Haogu: "Treats deafness with a sensation of dullness and fullness."
Usage and Dosage
Internal use: decocted, 6–15 g; or used in pills or powders.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated for those with spleen and stomach deficiency, fever due to qi deficiency, and for suppurative sores that have ruptured with thin, pale pus.
Formulas Using Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao)
1. For Taiyin wind-warmth, warm-heat, warm epidemic, winter-warm disease in early stage with heat without aversion to cold and with thirst: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 1 liang, Honeysuckle (Jinyinhua) 1 liang, Bitter Platycodon root (Kujiegeng) 6 qian, Mint (Bohe) 6 qian, Lophatherum leaf (Danzhuye) 4 qian, raw Licorice (Gancao) 5 qian, Mustard spike (Jingjie, labeled as Jie sui) 4 qian, Prepared fermented soybean (Dandouchi) 5 qian, Burdock fruit (Niubangzi) 6 qian. Pound into powder; take 6 qian per dose, decoct in fresh reed-root soup; when the aroma emerges take immediately, do not overboil. For severe disease, take approximately every two hours, three times daily, once at night; for mild cases, every three hours, three times daily, once at night; if not resolved, take again. (Wenbing Tiaobian: Yin Qiao San)
2. For all pediatric fevers: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Licorice (honey-fried) (Gancao [zhi]), Gardenia fruit (Zhizi) equal parts. Grind into powder, 2 qian per dose, boil in about half a teacup of water to three-quarters, strain and take warm. (Leizheng Huoren Shu: Lianqiao Drink)
3. For red wandering toxin rashes: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) alone, decoct and drink. (Yuqiao Yiling)
4. For breast carbuncle and breast lumps: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao), male-rat excrement (Xiongshushi), Dandelion (Pugongying), Sichuan fritillary bulb (Chuanbeimu) 2 qian each. Decoction and take. (Yuqiao Yiling)
5. For scrofula and indolent lymph nodes: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao), Guijianyu (Guijianyu), Dianthus (Qumai), Licorice (honey-fried) (Gancao [zhi]) equal parts. Grind to fine powder, 2 qian per dose, take at bedtime with rice-washing water. (Yang family household formula: Lianqiao powder)
6. For tongue fissures and oral ulcers: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 5 qian, Phellodendron bark (Huangbai) 3 qian, Licorice (Gancao) 2 qian. Decoction for gargling. (Yuqiao Yiling)
7. For stagnation of pathogenic heat in the upper and middle jiao causing chest-and-diaphragm heat accumulation, symptoms include body heat, thirst, red face and scorched lips, chest vexation and heat, oral and tongue ulcers, or sore throat with epistaxis, constipation and red urine, or difficult defecation, red tongue with yellow coating, slippery rapid pulse: Scutellaria (Huangqin) and Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) formula: Scutellaria (Huangqin) 10 liang each, Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 2.5 jin. Grind coarsely; 2 qian per dose, one cup of water, add seven bamboo leaves, a little honey, decoct to three-quarters, strain, take warm after meals; children can take half a qian, adjust with age. Stop when bowel movement is achieved. (Local formularies: Liangge San)
8. For mastitis: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 15 g, Dandelion (Pugongying) 30 g, Vaccaria seed (Wangbuluxing) 9 g, Wild chrysanthemum (Yejuhua) 15 g, decoct and take.
9. For intestinal abscess: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 15 g, Scutellaria (Huangqin) 12 g, Gardenia (Zhizi) 12 g, Honeysuckle (Jinyinhua) 18 g, decoct and take. (Formulas 8–9 from Qingdao Handbook of Chinese Materia Medica)
10. For allergic purpura: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 12 g, Red dates 30 g, decoct and take. (Ningxia Handbook of Chinese Materia Medica)
11. For sudden deafness and abrupt loss of hearing: Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) 1 liang, Xanthium (Cangerzi) 2 liang, decoct to a concentrated decoction and sip slowly. (Yuqiao Yiling)
12. For constipation: Remove stems from dried Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao), wash and dry in the sun, store in a jar. Each time take 15–30 g, steep in water or boil and drink as a tea. Continue for 1–2 weeks, then stop when bowel movement returns. (Shandong Journal of Traditional Chinese Medicine 1985,(5):44)
Notes
1. Forsythia Fruit is cooling and bitter, lightly clearing and ascending; it can treat heat in the upper jiao and is especially effective at detoxifying and resolving carbuncles and dispersing nodules, thus it is an essential herb for sores.
2. When paired with Honeysuckle (Jinyinhua), Mint (Bohe), Schizonepeta (Jingjie) and Licorice (Gancao) it disperses wind and clears heat; when paired with Scrophularia (Xuanshen), Ophiopogon (Maidong), Green lotus heart (Qinglianxin) and Bamboo leaves it clears the heart and drains heat; when paired with Honeysuckle (Jinyinhua), Dandelion (Pugongying), Viola (Zihuadiding) and Red peony root (Chishao) it detoxifies and reduces swelling; when paired with Scrophularia (Xuanshen), Prunella (Xiakucao), and Fritillaria (Beimu) it disperses masses and reduces scrofula.
3. Honeysuckle (Jinyinhua) and Forsythia Fruit (Lianqiao) both have good heat-clearing and detoxifying actions; they can both release exterior heat and clear interior heat and resolve carbuncle toxins, so they are often used together clinically. However, Honeysuckle also cools the blood and stops dysentery, while Forsythia Fruit clears heart heat and disperses nodules and scrofula.
4. In past medicinal practice this product was classified into Forsythia pericarp and Forsythia core (seed). Forsythia pericarp is the fruit body and Forsythia core is the seed; it was generally believed that the core had superior heart-clearing function. In the Shanghai region the classification has been simplified to a single Forsythia product, no longer divided into two medicines.
