Fraxinus Bark (Qin Pi)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%A7%A6%E7%9A%AE
Name
Ash Bark
Cenpi (Cenpi), Fanqiu bark (Fanqiu pi), Qinbai bark (Qinbaipi), Wax tree bark (Lashu pi)
Cenpi (Cenpi)
Fanqiu bark (Fanqiu pi)
Qinbai bark (Qinbaipi)
Wax tree bark (Lashu pi)
Fraxinus bark (Shenpi)
Northern Qinpi (Beiqinpi)
Kuli bark (Kuli pi)
Cultivation and Processing of Qinpi
Source
This product is the dried branch bark or dried bark of Oleaceae plants Manchurian ash (Fraxinus rhynchophylla Hance), Chinese ash (Fraxinus chinensis Roxb.), Szabo's ash (Fraxinus szaboana Lingelsh.) or Stylosa ash (Fraxinus stylosa Lingelsh.). It is peeled in the spring and autumn seasons and sun-dried.
Taste and properties
Bitter, cold.
Processing
Pick out impurities, wash clean, moisten thoroughly, then cut into pieces or sections and sun-dry.
Characteristics
Branch bark: forms rolled tubular or grooved pieces, length 10–60 cm, thickness 1.5–3 mm. Outer surface gray-white, gray-brown to black-brown or mottled, flat or slightly rough, with gray-white round lenticels and fine oblique wrinkles, some with branch scars. Inner surface yellow-white or brown, smooth. Texture hard and brittle, fracture fibrous, yellow-white. Odorless, bitter taste.
Dry bark: long strip-like flakes, thickness 3–6 mm. Outer surface gray-brown, with cracked grooves and red-brown round or transversely elongated lenticels. Texture hard, fracture strongly fibrous.
Effects of Qinpi
Functions
This product is the dried branch bark or dried bark of Oleaceae plants Manchurian ash, Chinese ash, Szabo's ash or Stylosa ash.
Main indications: bacillary dysentery, enteritis, leukorrhea, chronic bronchitis, red swollen painful eyes, lacrimation in wind, psoriasis.
Channels entered
Enters
Liver channel, Gallbladder channel.
Indications
Clears heat and dries dampness, relieves wheezing and stops cough, brightens the eyes. Treats bacillary dysentery, enteritis, leukorrhea, chronic bronchitis, red swollen painful eyes, lacrimation in wind, psoriasis.
1. Benjing: indicated for wind-cold-damp painful obstruction (bi), washes away cold qi, removes heat, bluish opacities and white membranes in the eye.
2. Bie Lu: treats male sperm deficiency, female leukorrhea, childhood convulsions and feverishness; can be used to wash the eyes as a decoction.
3. Yaoxing Lun: brightens the eyes, removes chronic heat in the liver, two red swollen painful eyes with continuous tearing from wind; treats childhood fever: use as a bathing decoction.
4. Rihuazi Materia Medica: washes the liver, benefits the essence, brightens the eyes, calms childhood febrile convulsions, treats wind obstruction of the skin, reduces fever.
5. Zhang Yuansu: treats excessive uterine bleeding in women.
6. Tangye Materia Medica: indicated for severe dysenteric diarrhea due to heat, lower burner deficiency.
7. Jilin Chinese Materia Medica: treats intestinal wind with bloody stools.
8. Heilongjiang Commonly Used Chinese Materia Medica Manual: treats enteritis and diarrhea.
9. Shaanxi Chinese Materia Medica: treats stye (hordeolum).
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoction, 6–12 g; or included in pill formulations.
External use: decoction for washing.
Precautions and contraindications
Contraindicated in those with spleen and stomach deficiency-cold.
1. Bencao Jing Jizhu: Euphorbia (Da Ji) acts as its envoy; incompatible with Evodia (Zhu Yu).
2. Yaoxing Lun: incompatible with Kuhu and Fangkui.
3. Benjing Fengyuan: contraindicated for those with stomach deficiency and poor appetite.
Formulas containing Qinpi
1. For hot dysenteric diarrhea with continuous discharge:
Pulsatilla (Baitouweng) two liang, Phellodendron bark (Huangbai) three liang, Coptis (Huanglian) three liang, Qinpi three liang. Take the four ingredients in seven sheng of water, boil down to two sheng, remove dregs, take warm one sheng. If not cured, take another sheng. (Treatise on Febrile Diseases (Shanghan Lun): Baitouweng Decoction)
2. For chronic bacterial dysentery: Qinpi 12 g, raw Sanguisorba (Diyu) 9 g, Toona root bark (Chungenpi) 9 g each. Decoction in water. (Hebei Chinese Materia Medica Manual)
3. For diarrhea: Qinpi three qian. Decoction with sugar, take in divided doses. (Heilongjiang Commonly Used Chinese Materia Medica Manual)
4. For red eyes and eye ulcers: Qinpi one large liang. Soak in one large sheng of clear water in a white porcelain bowl; in spring and summer soak for more than one meal time until a bluish color appears; then wrap the end of a chopstick with soft cloth, dip in the bluish liquid and apply to the affected eye while lying supine, first from the outer canthus filling inwards; slight pain not to be feared; repeat three to five times between meals; then lie on one side to let hot juices drain. Apply ten times or more daily; usually cured within two days. Avoid vinegar and radish. (Recent Effective Formulas)
5. For stye with constipation: Qinpi 9 g, Rhubarb (Dahuang) 6 g. Decoction in water. Contraindicated in pregnancy. (Hebei Chinese Materia Medica Manual)
6. For female leukorrhea red or white discharge and continuous uterine bleeding: Qinpi three liang, Moutan bark (Mudanhpi) two liang, Angelica (Danggui) one liang of the body; wash all in wine, fry and grind to powder, refine with honey into pills the size of sycamore seeds. Take five qian each morning with plain decoction. (Materia Medica Huiyan)
7. For pediatric convulsions with fever and intermittent steaming fevers: Qinpi and Poria (Fuling) each one qian, Licorice (Gancao) five fen, Juncus pith (Dengxincao) twenty strands. Decoction in water. (Essentials of Pediatrics)
8. For psoriasis: Qinpi 30–60 g, decoct and wash affected areas daily or every 2–3 days; each decoction can wash three times (use warm water). (National Compilation of Chinese Materia Medica)
9. For acute bacillary dysentery: Qinpi and Sophora flavescens root (Kushen) each 12 g, fried radish seed (Laifuzi) and Guangmuxiang (Aucklandia, Guangmuxiang) each 9 g. Grind to fine powder, mix with boiling water to form a paste, take 9–12 g each dose, 3–4 times daily. (Guoyi Forum 1986, (2):52)
10. For chronic protracted bloody diarrhea formula: Sage (Shuweicao), Rose root (Qiangwei gen), Qinpi. The three herbs in equal parts, chew orally, then soak and decoct in water, remove dregs, boil in a heavy copper pot into pills the size of sycamore seeds, take five or six pills three times daily, increase slightly as needed until cured. Can also take a half sheng of concentrated juice. (Prescriptions Worth a Thousand Gold)
11. For acute hepatitis: Qinpi 9 g, Capillaris herb (Yinchen) and Dandelion (Pugongying) each 30 g, Phellodendron bark (Huangbai) 9 g, Rhubarb (Dahuang) 9 g. Decoction in water. (Shanxi Chinese Materia Medica)
12. For toxic ulcers from the "field spider" (spider bite sores resembling scabies): Qinpi strongly decocted and taken orally; apply shell powder (Bengfen), talc (Huashi), and Chuan fritillary (Chuanbeimu) powder topically. (Zhi Zhi Fang)

Fresh ginger (Sheng Jiang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%94%9F%E5%A7%9C
Name
Fresh Ginger, Common Ginger
Ginger rhizome (Jianggen), Bailayun (Bailayun), Hooked-Finger (Gouzhuangzhi), Yindixin (Yindixin), Hot-and-Cool Lad (Yanliang Xiaozi), Fresh Ginger (Xianshengjiang), Honey-Fried Ginger (Mizhi Jiang), Ginger (Jiang)
Ginger rhizome (Jianggen)
Bailayun (Bailayun)
Hooked-Finger (Gouzhuangzhi)
Yindixin (Yindixin)
Hot-and-Cool Lad (Yanliang Xiaozi)
Fresh Ginger (Xianshengjiang)
Honey-Fried Ginger (Mizhi Jiang)
Ginger (Jiang)
Cultivation and Preparation of Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang)
Source
Derived from the fresh rhizome of the ginger plant of the Zingiberaceae family. Harvested from October to December when stems and leaves turn yellow. Dig up the rhizomes and remove stems, leaves, and adventitious roots.
Properties and Taste
Acrid, slightly warm.
Processing
Remove impurities, wash clean, and cut into thick slices when used.
Description
Rhizome irregularly lobed, slightly flattened, with finger-like branches, 4–18 cm long, 1–3 cm thick. Surface yellow-brown or gray-brown, with nodes; branch tips bear stem scars or buds. Texture brittle, breaks with a short fracture; cross-section pale yellow; cortex with distinct concentric rings; vascular bundles scattered. Aromatic, with a characteristic pungent taste.
Actions of Fresh Ginger
Functions and Efficacy
Derived from the fresh rhizome of the ginger plant of the Zingiberaceae family.
Main indications: wind-cold common cold, vomiting, phlegm-fluid retention, wheezy cough, abdominal distention, diarrhea; antidote for Pinellia (Banxia), Arisaema (Tiannanxing), and poisons from fish, crabs, birds, and beasts.
Meridians Entered
Enters the Lung, Spleen, and Stomach meridians.
Indications
Releases the exterior, disperses cold, stops vomiting, transforms phlegm. Treats wind-cold common cold, vomiting, phlegm-fluid retention, wheezy cough, abdominal distention, diarrhea; antidote for Pinellia (Banxia), Arisaema (Tiannanxing), and poisons from fish, crabs, birds, and beasts.
1. Bencao: removes foul odors and restores mental clarity.
2. Belu: treats cold damage with headache and nasal congestion, cough with rebellious qi.
3. Tao Hongjing: enters the five zang, expels phlegm and descends qi, stops vomiting, eliminates wind-damp cold and heat.
4. Yaoxinglun: resolves phlegm and water accumulation and descends qi; both fresh and dry ginger treat cough and acute seasonal disease and stop vomiting without suppressing appetite. Fresh combined with Pinellia (Banxia) treats acute epigastric pain; if there is internal heat and inability to eat, pound and take the juice with honey. Its juice combined with apricot kernel and boiled makes a decoction that descends all types of constrained qi and fullness of chest and diaphragm and alternating cold-heat qi.
5. Qianjin·Dietary Therapy: induces sweating and removes foul odors above the diaphragm.
6. Shiliao Bencao: eliminates excessive heat, treats cramps and fullness of the heart; stops vomiting, relieves vexation and depression, and opens stomach qi.
7. Bencaoshiyi: juice detoxifies medicines, breaks blood stasis and harmonizes the middle, removes cold and phlegm, and stimulates appetite.
8. Zhenzhuang: benefits Spleen and Stomach, disperses wind-cold.
9. Yiyuan: warms the middle and removes dampness; treats toxicity of Magnolia (Houpo) and Pinellia (Banxia).
10. Riyong Bencao: treats cold damage, wind-cold, headache, and obstruction of the nine orifices; enters Lung to open appetite, removes cold from the abdomen, and resolves fetid filth; antidote for bacterial and fungal toxins.
11. Materia Medica: raw ginger disperses, cooked ginger harmonizes the middle; resolves poisoning from eating wild birds; juice used to treat red eyes; pounded juice with yellow gelatin boiled into a plaster for wind-damp pain.
12. Bencao Congxin: ginger juice opens phlegm, treats food-induced choking, rescues sudden collapse, treats foul body odor, and rubs frozen ears. Roasted ginger harmonizes the middle and stops vomiting.
13. Huiyue Yijing: roasted ginger treats stomach cold, diarrhea, and acid regurgitation.
14. Modern Practical Chinese Materia Medica: effective for intestinal hernia pain.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 3–10 g; or pound to a juice and take.
External use: appropriate amount, pound and apply as a poultice; or stir-fry and apply hot as a compress; or squeeze juice and rub on.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated for those with yin deficiency and internal heat.
1. Materia Medica: long-term ginger consumption accumulates heat and harms the eyes. Hemorrhoid patients who eat much ginger with alcohol may develop rapid exacerbation. Those with ulcers who eat much may develop malignant flesh.
2. Bencao Jingshu: prolonged use injures yin and damages the eyes; contraindicated in yin deficiency with internal heat, yin-deficiency cough with hemoptysis, external deficiency with heat sweating, spontaneous sweating and night sweating, viscera toxins with bleeding, vomiting due to heat, fiery abdominal pain; avoid similarly to Allium.
3. Suixi Ju Diet Manual: contraindicated in internal heat and yin deficiency, red eyes and throat disease, blood disorders and ulcer pain, vomiting and diarrhea with heat, summer-heat symptoms, severe asthmatic wheeze, and in pregnancy and convalescence or after smallpox.
Prescriptions Using Fresh Ginger
1. For wind-cold common cold: five slices of fresh ginger, one liang of Perilla leaf (Zisuye). Decoction with water. (Bencaohuiyan)
2. For vomiting resistant to many medicines: one liang fresh ginger, cut to the size of green beans, marinate with seven he of vinegar, boil in a silver vessel to obtain four he, take on an empty stomach and sip the sediment. (Shiyi Xin Jing)
3. For patients whose chest feels like choking but not wheezing, like vomiting but not vomiting, like belching but not belching, and a frustrated, helpless feeling in the heart: half a sheng of Pinellia Rhizome (Banxia), one sheng fresh ginger juice. Use the two with three sheng of water, boil the Pinellia to obtain two sheng, add ginger juice and boil to obtain one and a half sheng, cool slightly. Divide into four doses, take three doses daily and one dose at night, stop when resolved, continue after stopping if needed. (Jinkui Yaolue, Shengjiang Banxia Tang)
4. For cold-phlegm cough: two liang fresh ginger, one liang rock candy. Three bowls water, decoct to half a bowl, drink warm and slowly. (Bencaohuiyan)
5. For a thirty-year cough: one jin white honey, two jin fresh ginger (take the juice). Weigh the two ingredients in a copper cauldron to determine amounts; add the honey, then add ginger juice and simmer over low heat until ginger juice evaporates and only the measured amount of honey remains. Take one dose in the morning like a date-sized pill, hold in the mouth; three times daily. Avoid all other foods. (Qianjin Fang)
6. For consumptive cough: four liang each of honey and ginger juice, one bowl each of white radish juice, pear juice, and human breast milk. Simmer together into a paste, take several spoons with hot soup morning and evening. (Yanjing Guangji, Five-Juice Paste)
7. For cold-damage with sweating and post-sweat disharmony in the stomach, epigastric fullness, dry belching, fetid eructation, hypochondrial dampness, and borborygmus with diarrhea: four liang sliced fresh ginger, three liang roasted Licorice root (Gancao), three liang Ginseng (Renshen), one liang Dried Ginger (Ganjiang), three liang Scutellaria (Huangqin), half a sheng washed Pinellia Rhizome (Banxia), one liang Coptis (Huanglian), twelve pieces split Jujube (Dazao). Use eight ingredients with one dou of water, boil down to six sheng, remove dregs, boil down to three sheng. Warm, take one sheng three times daily. (Shanghan Lun, Shengjiang Xiexin Tang)
8. For pathogenic qi bound in the chest, hypochondrium, or under the ribs with firm pain and distention: one jin fresh ginger, mash and retain juice, slowly stir-fry until moist; wrap in silk and apply as a warm compress to the affected area, allow to cool, then stir-fry the residue with juice again and reapply until great relief. (Shanghan Liushu)
9. For cholera with epigastric fullness, shortness of breath, and not yet vomiting or purging: one jin fresh ginger, slice, boil seven sheng of water down to two sheng, divide into three doses. (Zhouhou Fang)
10. Wind-damp painful obstruction: ginger juice cooked with yellow gelatin into a plaster. (Bencao Congxin)
11. For central qi collapse and fainting with phlegm obstruction: five qian fresh ginger, one qian five fen each of Pinellia Rhizome (Banxia), Aged Tangerine Peel (Chenpi), and Costus Root (Muxiang), eight fen Licorice root (Gancao). Decoction; add one cup of infant urine at time of administration. (Bencaohuiyan)
12. For seasonal cold malaria: four liang fresh ginger, two liang Atractylodes (Baizhu), one liang tsaoko seed (Caoguo Ren). Five large bowls water, decoct to two bowls, drink early before paroxysm. (Bencaohuiyan)
13. For deficient stomach qi, wind-heat unable to eat: half an egg-shell of ginger juice, a little Rehmannia glutinosa juice (Shengdihuang) and one small spoon of honey. Mix with three he of water and take at once. (Shiliao Bencao)
14. For abdominal fullness preventing swallowing of medicine: roast fresh ginger, wrap in cotton and insert into the lower abdomen; when cool replace with a warm one. (Meishi Jiyan Fang)
15. For peeling of the hands: one liang fresh ginger, slice, soak in two liang wine for twenty-four hours, apply twice daily. (Inner Mongolia, Selected New Clinical Methods of Chinese Herbal Medicine)
16. For baldness: pound fresh ginger, warm, apply to the scalp two to three times. (Guizhou TCM Clinical Formulas)
17. For chronic non-scabbing ulcers, hemorrhoids, and fistulae: slice fresh ginger with skin, apply alum powder, char, grind fine, and apply as a plaster without moving. (Puji Fang)
18. For early-stage acute back eruptions: one piece fresh ginger, char over coal, scrape one layer off at a time to powder, mix with pig bile to apply. (Haishang Fang)
19. For vitiligo and leukoderma: frequent rubbing with fresh ginger is effective. (Yijian Fang)
20. For severe dog bites: drink pounded ginger root juice. (Buque Zhouhou Fang)
21. For viper venom: apply powdered ginger thinly, dry and repeat. (Qianjin Fang)
22. For contusions and sprains: mix ginger juice with wine and raw wheat paste and apply. (Yijian Fang)
23. For toothache with constant moaning: slice old fresh ginger, place on tile and heat over charcoal, mix alum with the ginger and wait until charred to powder, rub on painful tooth. (Haishang Fang, remedy named Fuyan San)
24. For insects in the ear: drop a little ginger juice into the ear. (Yijian Fang)
25. For retching with cold hands and feet: four liang Aged Tangerine Peel (Chenpi), half a jin fresh ginger. Pound and boil seven sheng water to three sheng, divide into three doses; if not stopped, continue. (Qianjin Yaofang, Chenpi Tang)
26. For reversed stomach with morning eating and evening vomiting or vice versa, continuous vomiting: seven sheng sugarcane juice, one sheng fresh ginger juice. Combine and divide into three doses. (Haishi Jiyan Fang)
27. For cholera with nausea and no vomit, desire to purge but no stool: one liang salt, five qian fresh ginger. Pound, stir-fry until color changes. One bowl water, decoct and take; in severe cases add one cup infant urine. (Chishui Xianzhu, Ginger-Salt Drink)
28. For elderly with upper respiratory distress, cough, wheeze, vexation-heat, poor appetite with vomiting after eating, and abdominal distention: five he fresh ginger juice, four liang granulated sugar. Combine and warm over low heat until one or two brief boils then stop. Hold half a spoonful and let dissolve gradually. (Anlao Huaiyou Shu, Ginger-Sugar Decoction)
29. For postpartum deficiency with edema and dyspnea relieved immediately upon bowel movement: two liang each of fresh ginger juice and white flour, seven Pinellia Rhizomes (Banxia) washed to remove mucilage. Mix ginger juice with flour and coat each Pinellia to make seven patties; char until cooked, grind to powder. Mix with hot water one qian, administer to prompt a small stool and effect. (Chanyu Baoqing Ji, Qiming San)
30. For chronic morning diarrhea: four liang fresh ginger cut to bean size, two liang Coptis (Huanglian) finely cut. Soak together overnight, slowly fry the ginger until purple and discard the ginger. Take Coptis powder two qian per dose with preserved tea; one dose cures. Also excellent with rice water or wine for chronic white diarrhea. (Zhengzhi Zhunsheng, Xiangjiang San)
31. For suppurative bloody dysentery: one liang each fresh ginger and Pinellia Rhizome (Banxia), three fen Aconite (Fuzi), half liang Veratrum (Lilu). Pound and sift into powder, boil sufficient mature vinegar, mix with powder into pills the size of wutong seeds. Thirty pills per dose with aged rice water, repeat at noon. (Puji Fang, Shengjiang Wan)
32. For elderly urinary and fecal obstruction: four liang fresh ginger, a pinch of salt, thirty pieces fermented soybean (dandouchi), one stalk scallion including root and leaves cleaned. Pound the four ingredients, place on the navel; after a while normal defecation occurs. (Jianyi Puji Liangfang, Yunqi San)
33. For lumbar pain: one jin fresh ginger, extract four liang juice, one liang gelatin, simmer into a paste. Spread on thick paper and apply over the lumbar region; highly effective. (Chuan Ya Neibian, Waist Plaster)
34. For headache: one slice fresh ginger split open, place realgar (Xionghuang) inside, wrap in damp paper and warm. While hot apply to the temple. (Shen Family Clinical Experience, Headache Miracle Recipe)
35. For poisoning from eating mushrooms or fungi: four liang finely chopped fresh ginger, four liang soy milk, two liang and a half sesame oil. Mix and grind evenly, steam until cooked, take at any time; all such poisoning is immediately relieved. (Puji Fang)
36. For contusions and persistent swelling pain: fresh ginger juice, rice vinegar, and bovine hide glue melted together, add puffball mushroom powder (Mabo) in any amount, stir into a plaster. Spread on paper flowers and apply to the swollen area; pain stops immediately and repeated application is beneficial. (Baiyi Xuanfang)
Dietary Therapy Recipes
1. Angelica sinensis (Danggui) and Fresh Ginger Mutton Soup
30 g Angelica sinensis (Danggui), 30 g fresh ginger, 500 g mutton. Wash Danggui and fresh ginger with water and slice into large pieces. Remove membranes from mutton, blanch in boiling water to remove blood, remove, cool and cut into strips about 5 cm long, 3 cm wide, 1 cm thick. In a clay pot add appropriate clear water, place mutton strips, then add Danggui and fresh ginger. Bring to a boil over high heat, skim scum, then simmer over low heat about 1.5 hours until mutton is tender. Eat meat and drink soup.
Efficacy: nourishes blood and warms the middle, regulates menstruation and relieves pain. Indicated for blood deficiency with cold and abdominal cold pain, postpartum cold abdominal pain in women, or cold-type dysmenorrhea.

8 g fresh ginger, two jujubes, 100 g rice, season with salt and sesame oil. Slice or finely shred 8 g fresh ginger, two jujubes (for wind-cold common cold omit jujubes and use two scallion whites), 100 g rice, cook together with broth into congee, season with salt and sesame oil.
Contraindications: avoid in heat syndromes.
Efficacy: for headache and nasal congestion, chronic bronchitis, susceptibility to colds, obesity, Spleen and Stomach yang deficiency, stomach pain, etc.

Cultivation and Processing of Zhi Zi
Source
This product is the dried mature fruit of Gardenia jasminoides Ellis, family Rubiaceae; its root can also be used medicinally. Fruits are harvested when ripe and red-yellow from September to November, stems and impurities removed, steamed until steam issues or briefly scalded in boiling water, removed and dried. Roots are dug in summer and autumn, washed and sun-dried.
Macroscopic morphology
Gardenia (Shan Zhi) is an evergreen shrub, 1–2 m tall. Young twigs green, initially pubescent then nearly glabrous. Leaves opposite, sometimes ternate or whorled with short petiole; two stipules on the inner side of the petiole; leaf blade leathery, ovate, broadly lanceolate or obovate, 6–14 cm long, 2–7 cm wide, apex acute or acuminate, base cuneate, entire margin, glossy above, only with short hairs clustered in axils under the veins; lateral veins pinnate. Flowers large, very fragrant, terminal or axillary with short pedicel; calyx green, 2–3 cm long, 5–7 lobes linear-lanceolate, usually slightly longer than the calyx tube; corolla campanulate-dish-shaped, white turning creamy yellow, fused at base into a tube with 6–7 lobes arranged in a rotate manner, lobes rounded at apex; stamens equal in number to corolla lobes, attached at the throat of the corolla, filaments very short, anthers linear, longitudinally dehiscent, two locules; pistil one, ovary inferior, one locule. Fruit deep yellow, obovoid or oblong-ellipsoid, 2–4 cm long, with 5–9 wing-like longitudinal ribs, apex with a linear persistent calyx. Seeds numerous, fresh yellow, flattened-ellipsoid. Flowering May to July, fruiting August to November.
Habitat and distribution
Ecology: grows in hilly mountains or shrublands on slopes.
Distribution: found in central-south and southwest China and in Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan and other areas.
Taste and properties
Bitter, cold.
Processing
1. Raw Zhi Zi: sieve out ash and debris, pick out impurities, crush and sift; or trim both ends.
2. Shan Zhi Ren: take clean Zhi Zi, cut in half with scissors, peel off outer skin and remove kernels.
3. Shan Zhi Pi: the outer pericarp peeled from raw Zhi Zi.
4. Fried Zhi Zi: take crushed Zhi Zi, place in a pan and stir-fry over low heat until golden yellow, remove and cool.
5. Jiao Zhi Zi (charred Zhi Zi): take crushed Zhi Zi, place in a pan and stir-fry over high heat until charred, remove and cool.
6. Zhi Zi Charcoal: take crushed Zhi Zi, place in a pan and stir-fry over high heat until dark brown-black while retaining efficacy, remove and cool.
7. From Lei Gong Pao Zhi Lun: when using Zhi Zi, first peel it completely, take the required amount, soak in licorice (Gan Cao) water overnight, strain and dry, then pound and sieve into a powder like red-gold dust before use.
Characters (appearance and organoleptic)
Zhi Zi: dried fruit oblong or ellipsoid, 1–4.5 cm long, 0.6–2 cm thick. Surface deep red or red-yellow, with 5–8 longitudinal ribs. Apex with remaining calyx, other end slightly tapered with pedicle scar. Pericarp thin and brittle, inner surface red-yellow and glossy, with 2–3 raised false septa, many seeds inside bound into a mass. Seeds rounded-flattened, deep red or red-yellow, densely covered with small wart-like protrusions. When soaked in water the water is dyed bright yellow. Aroma faint, taste slightly sour. Best quality are small, intact, with full kernels and red color inside and out. Lower quality are large, pericarp brown-yellow, kernels shriveled, color red-yellow.
Jiao Zhi Zi (charred Zhi Zi): shape like Zhi Zi or irregular fragments, surface charred brown or black. Pericarp thin and brittle, inner surface brown, seed mass brown or brownish-black. Aroma faint, taste slightly sour and bitter.
Therapeutic actions of Zhi Zi
Functions
This product is the dried mature fruit of Gardenia (Zhi Zi) of the Rubiaceae family.
Treats vexation and insomnia from febrile disease, jaundice, strangury, diabetes (wasting-thirst), red eyes, sore throat, vomiting blood, nosebleed, bloody dysentery, hematuria, heat-toxic sores and ulcers, sprains and swelling pain.
Channels entered
Enters the Heart channel, Liver channel, Lung channel, Stomach channel.
Main indications
Clears heat, drains fire, cools the blood. Treats vexation and insomnia from febrile disease, jaundice, strangury, wasting-thirst, red eyes, sore throat, vomiting blood, nosebleed, bloody dysentery, hematuria, heat-toxic sores and ulcers, sprains and swelling pain.
1. Ben Jing: treats pathogenic qi of the five viscera, heat qi in the stomach, facial redness, alcohol blisters and bloody nose, vitiligo white lesions, red lesions, sores and ulcers.
2. Ben Cao Jing Ji Zhu: resolves zhi zhu toxin.
3. Bie Lu: treats eye heat and pain, intense heat of chest and large or small intestine, vexation in the heart, heat in the stomach.
4. Yao Xing Lun: kills scorpion and insect poison, eliminates heat-toxic wind, promotes urination for five types of strangury, treats central evil, unblocks urination, resolves five kinds of jaundice, brightens the eyes, treats intermittent febrile diseases by clearing heat and wasting-thirst and parched mouth.
5. Shi Liao Ben Cao: treats aphonia, purpura wind, jaundice and accumulated heat causing restlessness.
6. Yi Yuan Yi Xue Qi Yuan: treats heat invading the Heart channel, relieves vexation, removes upper-jiao deficiency heat, treats wind.
7. Yao Lei Fa Xiang: treats vexation and inability to sleep, mind in turmoil to near collapse, blood stasis with difficult urination.
8. Zhu Zhenheng: drains fire of the three jiaos, clears heat in the epigastrium and blood, treats heat syncope chest pain, resolves heat accumulation and moves stagnated qi.
8. Ben Cao Gang Mu: treats vomiting blood, nosebleed, bloody dysentery, lower body bleeding, blood strangury, trauma with blood stasis, recovery from cold damage with chronic fatigue, heat syncope headache, hernia, scalds and burns.
10. Ben Cao Bei Yao: raw Zhi Zi drains fire, charred Zhi Zi stops bleeding, ginger-juice fried treats vexation and vomiting, use kernel (ren) for internal heat, pericarp (pi) for exterior heat.
11. Guangzhou Military Commonly Used Chinese Herbs Manual: clears heat and detoxifies, cools blood and drains fire. Treats jaundice-type hepatitis, favism jaundice, high fever from cold, dysentery, nephritis with edema, nosebleed, mouth and tongue ulcers, mastitis, sores and swollen toxins.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoction, 5–10 g; or used in pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, grind into powder or mix and apply as a poultice.
Precautions and contraindications
Contraindicated in spleen-deficiency with loose stools.
1. Ben Cao Hui Yan: for vomiting blood or nosebleed not due to violent yang-fire, avoid use.
2. De Pei Ben Cao: contraindicated when the pathogen is at the exterior and deficiency fire rises.
Prescriptions using Zhi Zi
1. For cold-damage with sweating and vomiting; after purging if there is deficiency vexation and inability to sleep, oppression in the chest: Zhi Zi 14 pieces (split), fragrant fermented soybean (lightly fermented soybeans, Dan Dou Chi) 4 he (wrapped in cotton). Boil the two ingredients in four sheng of water until two and a half sheng remain, add the fermented soybean and boil to one and a half sheng, remove dregs, divide into two doses. Warm take one dose; if it induces vomiting, stop; take the second dose afterwards. (Shang Han Lun: Zhi Zi Chi Tang)
2. For convalescence from severe cold-damage with lingering fatigue: Bitter Orange (Zhi Shi) three pieces (roasted), Zhi Zi 14 pieces (split), fermented soybean one sheng (wrapped in cotton). Boil these three in seven sheng of clear liquid until four sheng remain; add Zhi Shi and Zhi Zi and boil to two sheng, then add fermented soybean and boil five or six times; remove dregs, warm and divide into two doses, cover to induce slight sweating. If there is retained food, take Da Huang about five or six pieces the size of checkers. (Shang Han Lun: Zhi Shi Zhi Zi Chi Tang)
3. For jaundice after cold-damage: fatty Zhi Zi 15 pieces (split), Licorice (Gan Cao) 1 liang (honey-fried), Phellodendron bark (Huang Bai) 2 liang. Boil these three in 4 sheng water to 1.5 sheng, remove dregs, divide and warm to take. (Shang Han Lun: Zhi Zi Bai Pi Tang)
4. For damp-heat jaundice: Zhi Zi (Shan Zhi) 4 qian, Ji Gu Cao (Ji Gu Cao) and Centella (Ji Xue Cao) each 1 liang. Decoction, take three divided doses daily. (Guangxi Chinese Materia Medica)
5. For strangury with blood and hematuria: fresh Zhi Zi 2 liang, rock sugar (Bing Tang) 1 liang. Decoction and take. (Min Dong Materia Medica)
6. For urinary retention: Zhi Zi kernels 27 pieces, rock salt a little, one clove of garlic. Pound to paste, spread on paper and place over the navel, or apply to the scrotum; after a while urination opens. (Pu Ji Fang)
7. For acute gastroenteritis with abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea: Shan Zhi 3 qian, Pan Zhu Nan Wu Wei (Zi Jin Pi) root 5 qian, Qing Mu Xiang 2 qian. Fry the herbs to black to retain efficacy, add honey 5 qian. Decoction in water, divide into two doses. (Collection of Single and Effective Formulas)
8. For mouth ulcers, throat obstruction and inability to eat: Da Qing 4 liang, Zhi Zi and Phellodendron bark (Huang Bai) each 1 liang, white honey half jin. Slice and decoct 3 sheng water to 1 sheng, remove dregs, add honey and boil another liang of water, use as a gargle. (Pu Ji Fang: Zhi Zi Decoction)
9. For red eyes: take 7 Shan Zhi pieces, bore through and roast in embers until cooked, decoct in 1.5 sheng water to eight he, remove dregs, add powdered Da Huang 3 qian, stir, take warm after meals. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Zhi Zi Decoction)
10. For epigastric fire pain: seven or nine large Shan Zhi pieces, fry to char, decoct in one cup of water to seven-tenths, add fresh ginger juice and drink. (Dan Xi Zuan Yao)
11. For nasal bleeding from the nostrils: burn Shan Zhi to ash and insufflate. (Jian Yi Fang Lun)
12. For pulmonary-wind nasal redness and nosebleed from alcohol misuse: old Shan Zhi powdered, mixed with equal parts yellow wax; form into balls the size of a pellet and chew with tea or wine on an empty stomach. Avoid alcohol and roasted decoctions. (Ben Shi Fang)
13. For acute or chronic dysentery with blood: Zhi Zi kernels 47 pieces, scrape and decoct in 1.5 sheng of slurry water to five he, remove dregs. Take warm before meals in two doses on empty stomach. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Zhi Zi Kernel Decoction)
14. For edema from heat: Zhi Zi 5 qian, Mu Xiang 1 qian 5 fen, Bai Zhu 2 qian 5 fen. Finely slice and decoct in water. (Dan Xi Xin Fa)
15. For excessive uterine discharge and edema in women: fried Shan Zhi one he, grind to powder, swallow with rice gruel or form into pills. (Dan Xi Xin Fa)
16. For traumatic swelling and pain: Zhi Zi and wheat flour pounded together and applied topically. (Bin Hu Ji Jian Fang)
17. For carbuncles and erysipelas: pound Zhi Zi and mix with water and apply as a poultice. (Mei Shi Ji Yan Fang)
18. For early-stage fire sores before blisters: ash of Zhi Zi kernels mixed with sesame oil and applied thickly. (Qian Jin Fang)
19. For sores and swollen painful ulcers: Shan Zhi, Dandelion (Pu Gong Ying), Honeysuckle (Jin Yin Hua) each 4 qian. Decoction, take three divided doses daily. Also take some fresh honeysuckle vines, pound and apply to lesions. (Guangxi Chinese Materia Medica)
20. For burns: powdered Zhi Zi mixed with raw egg white and applied thickly. (Jiu Ji Fang)
21. For painful bloody strangury: raw Zhi Zi powder and talc (Hua Shi) equal parts, take with scallion broth. (Jing Yan Liang Fang)
22. For diarrhea with fresh blood: burn Zhi Zi kernels to ash and take one spoonful with water.
23. For heat-toxic bloody dysentery: Zhi Zi 14 pieces, peel removed, pounded to powder, mixed with honey into pills the size of chinese parasol tree seeds. Take three pills three times a day; effect rapid. Can also be decocted in water.
24. To assist labor and promote delivery: roast Zhi Zi, grind to powder and take three qian with rice soup. If upper-jiao heat present, use with pericarp.
25. For cholera with convulsions, abdominal fullness, vomiting and diarrhea: roast about a dozen Zhi Zi pieces, grind to powder, take with cooked wine.
26. For relapse of illness after febrile disease due to improper diet or sexual activity: use 30 Zhi Zi pieces, add 3 sheng water, decoct to 1 sheng and take; slight sweating is desirable.
27. For pediatric mania and agitation from heat below with fever and delirium and poor intake: Zhi Zi kernels 7 pieces, fermented soybeans (Dan Dou Chi) 5 qian, add one bowl water, decoct to 70% and give; effective whether it induces vomiting or not.
28. For eye-related constipation: seven Shan Zhi pieces, bore holes and roast, decoct in water to half a sheng, remove dregs, add 3 qian Da Huang, take warm.
29. For wind-phlegm headache: apply Zhi Zi powder with thick honey to the tongue; induced vomiting relieves the pain.
30. For flame-type erysipelas: pound Zhi Zi and mix with water to apply topically.
31. For tinea between the eyebrows: roast Zhi Zi, grind to powder, mix with oil and apply.
32. For acute yellowing from cold-damage: Zhi Zi kernels, Bupleurum (Chai Hu) (remove small sprout), Manna salt (Po Xiao) (separately pounded), Artemisia capillaris (Yin Chen) each half liang. Except for Po Xiao, finely scrape the herbs. Use three large cups of water, decoct to two large cups, remove dregs, add Po Xiao and stir until uniform. Take in three warm doses regardless of time, dose according to bowel movement. (Pu Ji Fang)
33. For heat toxin attacking stomach and intestines with yellow-red discharge and rotten flesh and severe abdominal pain: Zhi Zi kernels 37 pieces, fermented soybeans (Dan Dou Chi) two he, Allium macrostemon (Xie Bai) a handful (sliced). Use two large cups water, decoct to one cup, remove dregs, divide into two doses. (Sheng Hui Fang)
34. For Qi stagnation chest pain: fried Shan Zhi six qian, Cyperus (Xiang Fu) one qian, Evodia (Wu Zhu Yu) one qian. Grind to powder, steam into small pill the size of a peppercorn. Wash raw Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang) with wine and decoct with fresh ginger soup, use to take twenty pills. (Dan Xi Xin Fa)
35. For severe stabbing chest pain: Zhi Zi two liang, processed Aconite root (Fu Zi) one liang. Take three qian per dose, decoct in one large cup of water with three cun of Allium macrostemon (Xie Bai) until five-tenths remain, take warm. (Su Shen Liang Fang)
36. For violent vomiting and nosebleed from extreme heat driving reckless behavior: use Shan Zhi fried black one liang, raw Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang) two liang, roasted ginger ash five qian. Boil three bowls of water to one bowl and take slowly. (Ben Cao Hui Yan quoting Long Tan Family Secrets)
37. For heat-toxic lower-body bleeding: Zhi Zi 30 pieces, broken, boil 3 sheng to 1 sheng, remove dregs and take. (Mei Shi Ji Yan Fang)
38. For external trauma with bleeding and swelling: Zhi Zi, Angelica sinensis blood regulator (Xue Dang Gui), and rice wine three to seven. Pound together, add appropriate white wine, heat fry and apply to the wound. (Miao Ethnic Materia Medica Collection)
39. For sprains and contusions: Zhi Zi powdered with a little flour and egg white, apply as a poultice. (Bin Hu Ji Jian Fang)
Dietary therapy recipe
Zhi Zi Fresh Lotus Root and Imperata Root Congee
Zhi Zi 10 g (kernels ground into fine powder and reserved), fresh lotus root 60 g, Imperata root (Bai Mao Gen) 30 g, japonica rice 100 g. Wash and thinly slice the fresh lotus root; decoct Imperata root and strain out dregs. Put Imperata root juice, lotus slices and rice into a pot, add appropriate water and cook into congee. When cooked, add Zhi Zi kernel powder and simmer a little longer. Take one dose daily in two divided portions for 3–5 days as one course.
Function: clears heat, generates fluids, cools the blood and stops bleeding. Indicated for stomach heat with vomiting blood and related conditions.

Gentian (Long Dan)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%BE%99%E8%83%86
Name
Chinese Gentian Root
Ling You (Ling You), Grass Chinese Gentian (Cao Long Dan), Chinese Gentian (Long Dan), Bitter Gentian Grass (Ku Long Dan Cao), Dan Cao (Dan Cao), Mountain Chinese Gentian (Shan Long Dan), Four‑leaf Gentian (Si Ye Dan), Water Gentian (Shui Long Dan)
Chinese Gentian Herb (Long Dan Cao)
Dan Cao (Dan Cao)
Wine‑fried Chinese Gentian (Jiu Long Dan)
Ling You (Ling You)
Grass Chinese Gentian (Cao Long Dan)
Bitter Gentian Grass (Ku Long Dan Cao)
Mountain Chinese Gentian (Shan Long Dan)
Four‑leaf Gentian (Si Ye Dan)
Cultivation and Processing of Chinese Gentian
Source
This product is the dried roots and rhizomes of Gentianaceae plants: Gentiana manshurica Kitag. (Tiao Ye Long Dan), Gentiana scabra Bunge (Long Dan), Gentiana triflora Pall. (San Hua Long Dan), or Gentiana rigescens Franch. (Dian Long Dan). The first three are commonly called Long Dan; the latter is commonly called Jian Long Dan. Harvested in spring and autumn, washed clean, and dried.
Properties and Flavor
Bitter, cold.
Processing
Remove impurities, wash clean, moisten thoroughly, cut into sections, and dry.
Description
(1) Chinese Gentian: rhizomes mostly prostrate, length 0.5–3 cm, diameter 3–8 mm, with multiple stem scars; below are more than 4–30 roots, often more than 20; roots slender cylindrical, slightly twisted, diameter 1–3 mm; surface gray‑white or yellow‑brown, upper part with distinct transverse striations, lower part with longitudinal wrinkles and fine root scars. Texture brittle, absorbs moisture and softens easily; fracture surface yellow‑brown, wood portion dotted yellow‑white, in rings, central pith obvious. Slight odor, extremely bitter taste.
(2) Gentiana manshurica (Tiao Ye Long Dan): rhizomes mostly erect, nodular or long nodular, length 0.5–1.5 cm, diameter 4–7 mm, below clustered with 2–16 roots, often fewer than 10. Roots about 15 cm long, diameter 2–4 mm; surface yellow‑brown or gray‑brown, with twisted longitudinal wrinkles, upper part with dense transverse striations and a few raised lateral root scars.
(3) Gentiana triflora (San Hua Long Dan): rhizomes mostly erect, length 1–5.5 cm, diameter 0.7–1.5 cm, below more than 4–30 roots, often more than 15, root diameter 1–6 mm; surface yellow‑white. Transverse striations are generally distinct throughout.
(4) Gentiana rigescens (Dian Long Dan): rhizomes nodular, with 1–10 or more old stems, below more than 4–30 roots; roots slender spindle‑shaped, slightly curved, diameter 1–4 mm; surface light brown or brown‑black; cross section shows white wood in the center.
Effects of Chinese Gentian
Actions and Indications
This product is the dried roots and rhizomes of Gentianaceae plants Tiao Ye Long Dan, Long Dan, San Hua Long Dan, or Jian Long Dan.
Mainly treats excessive heat in the liver channel, convulsions and mania, type B encephalitis, headache, red eyes, sore throat, jaundice, summer‑heat dysentery, abscesses and ulcers, swollen and painful scrotum, and damp itching of the genital area.
Channels Entered
Enters the Liver channel and the Gallbladder channel.
Indications
Drains Liver and Gallbladder excess fire, clears damp‑heat from the lower burner. Treats excess heat in the Liver channel, convulsions and mania, type B encephalitis, headache, red eyes, sore throat, jaundice, summer‑heat dysentery, abscesses and ulcers, swollen painful scrotum, and damp itching of the genital area.
1. Benjing: treats alternating cold and heat between the bones, fright and lameness from pathogenic qi, restores disconnected injuries, stabilizes the five zang, and kills gu poison.
2. Bie Lu: eliminates latent stomach heat, seasonal warm‑heat, heat‑induced diarrhea, expels small intestinal parasites, benefits Liver and Gallbladder qi, and stops fright and vigilance.
3. Yaoxing Lun: treats pediatric convulsions entering the heart, robust fever and bone heat, and abscesses; treats epidemic fevers with yellowing and mouth ulcers.
4. Rihuazi Bencao: treats rebellious behavior, pediatric marasmus (gan qi), delirium with febrile disease, sores and scabies, clarifies the eyes, and relieves vexation.
5. Bencao Tujing: ancient formulas frequently use it for treating jaundice.
6. Luchanyan Bencao: treats alcohol‑induced toxic bloody stools and intestinal wind bleeding.
7. Yixue Qiyuan: treats yellow eyes and red swelling of the eyes, eyeball distention, raised nodular congealed flesh that is unbearably painful. The "Zhu Zhi Mijue" says: treats lower‑body wind‑damp and damp‑heat, swelling and pain from below the navel to the feet, and cold‑damp beriberi.
8. Diannan Bencao: treats sore throat, and is used to wash ulcers and scabies toxins and swellings.
9. Yixue Rumen: treats sudden cardiac pain, heart pain due to parasitic attack, and limb pain.
10. Bencao Gangmu: treats sore throat, wind‑heat, and night sweating.
Usage and Dosage
Internal use: decoct and drink, 3–6 g; or include in pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, decoct for washing; or grind to powder and mix for topical application.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated in spleen and stomach deficiency with diarrhea and in those without damp‑heat or excess fire; do not take on an empty stomach.
Formulas Using Chinese Gentian
1. For typhoid fever with mania: Powder Grass Chinese Gentian (Cao Long Dan), add chicken egg white and white honey, dilute with cool water and take two qian. (Shanghan Yunyao)
2. For excess fire and damp‑heat of the Liver and Gallbladder channels with ribside pain, deafness, bitter taste in the mouth from gallbladder discharge, muscle weakness, seminal sweating, genital swelling and pain, white turbidity in urine and bloody urine: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao, wine‑fried), Baical Skullcap (Huang Qin, dry‑fried), Gardenia Fruit (Zhi Zi, wine‑fried), Alisma (Ze Xie), Akebia (Mu Tong), Plantain Seed (Che Qian Zi), Chinese Angelica (Dang Gui, wine‑washed), Raw Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang, wine‑fried), Bupleurum (Chai Hu), Licorice (Gan Cao, raw); decoct in water and drink. (Jufang Long Dan Xie Gan Tang)
3. For night blindness (unable to see at night): one liang Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao) and one liang Coptis (Huang Lian). Grind both into fine powder; after eating, dip hot sheep liver in the powder and take. (Luchanyan Bencao)
4. For summer heat causing gritty eyes: fresh Chinese Gentian (crushed for juice) one he, Coptis (soaked for juice) one spoonful, mix and apply as drops. (Shi Yi De Xiao Fang)
5. For purulent discharge from the eye: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao) and Chinese Angelica (Dang Gui) in equal parts, powdered. Each dose two qian, take with warm water. (Fei Hong Ji)
6. For grain‑induced jaundice with dizziness after eating, anxiety and yellowing caused by overeating and stomach qi rising and attacking: Sophora Root (Ku Shen) three liang, Chinese Gentian (Long Dan) one he, form Ox Gall pills about the size of wuzi, take five pills with raw wheat juice three times daily. (Buque Zhouhou Fang)
7. For sore throat and swelling: a handful of Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao), crush for juice and gargle and swallow. (Bencao Huiyan)
8. For sudden unstoppable lower bleeding: a handful of Grass Chinese Gentian (Cao Long Dan), cut and boil five liters of water down to two and a half liters, divide into five doses; if not better, continue. (Yao Sengtan Collection of Tested Prescriptions)
9. For persistent night sweating after typhoid, or all night sweats in women and children: any amount of Chinese Gentian, dry roast, grind to fine powder; each dose one large qian, mix with three liang pig gallbladder juice and a little warm wine, take on an empty stomach before lying down. (Yang Family Treasury Formula: Long Dan Decoction)
10. For scrotal wind ulcers, itching, or rupture with discharge, also called embroidered‑ball wind: Bitter Chinese Gentian (Ku Long Dan Cao), frost‑treated peach leaves (Jing Shuang Tao Ye), Beehive/Honeycomb (Feng Fang), Veratrum (Li Lu), Psoralea (Bu Gu Zhi). Grind to a fine powder and mix with sesame oil for topical application. (Diannan Bencao)
11. For acute icteric infectious hepatitis: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan) and Artemisia (Yin Chen) 12 g each, Curcuma (Yu Jin) and Phellodendron (Huang Bai) 6 g each; decoct in water and drink. (Qingdao Chinese Herbal Manual)
12. For yin jaundice: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan) and Qin Jiao (Qin Jiao, roots washed of soil) one liang and a half each, Cimicifuga (Sheng Ma) one liang. Coarsely pulverize the first two herbs and sieve. Each dose five qian and a spoonful, soak in one and a half bowls of water overnight, decoct to eight tenths the next morning, add five he of yellow ox milk, decoct down to one bowl, strain. Take on an empty stomach in two warm doses, repeat once a day as needed to produce bowel movement. (Shengji Zonglu Long Dan Tang)
13. For sudden bloody urine with stem‑center pain: a handful of Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao), decoct and drink.
14. For scrotal itching that remains moist and does not dry, eventually making the scrotal skin dry and rough and increasing the itch: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao) two liang, Chinese Gall (Wu Bei Zi) five qian, Liu Ji Nu (Liu Ji Nu) one liang. Boil in one large jar of water to near boiling, strain out the dregs, add five fen camphor (ground), wait until the decoction cools enough to handle, and soak to wash. (Three to four formulas from Bencao Huiyan)
15. For hypertension: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao) 9 g, Prunella (Xia Ku Cao) 15 g. Decoction in water and drink. (Fujian Materia Medica)
16. For congestion of the pupil and violent red eye pain or pterygium formation: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao), Asarum (Xi Xin), Saposhnikovia (Fang Feng) each two liang. Decoction with a small piece of refined sugar and drink. (Zhengzhi Zunsheng)
17. For roundworm attacking the heart like stabbing pain with vomiting clear water: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan) one liang (remove head, grate). Two bowls of water boiled down to one bowl, strain. Fast overnight, take at dawn in one dose. (Shenghui Fang)
18. For yang‑toxin typhoid with poisonous qi in the viscera, wild speech, and inclination to run away: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan) one liang (remove the pith head), iron powder (Tie Luo) two liang. Pulverize finely and make into powder. Each dose one qian, mixed with whetstone water for administration at any time. (Puji Fang)
19. For pediatric persistent fever with convulsions: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan, remove pith head) and Dragon Tooth (Long Chi) each three fen, Calculus Bovis (Niu Huang) one fen finely powdered. Grind into fine powder, add Musk (She Xiang) two qian, form pills with refined honey the size of a grain of millet. Administer at any time with five pills following Jing Jie decoction. (Shenghui Fang)
20. For infantile malnutrition with fever: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao, remove pith), Coptis (Huang Lian, remove rootlets, lightly fried), Green Tangerine Peel (Qing Pi, remove white pith), Quisqualis Seed (Shi Jun Zi, peel removed and roasted). Grind equal parts into fine powder, mix with pig gallbladder juice into pills the size of radish seeds. Each dose twenty pills, adjust as needed, take at bedtime with hot water. (Jufang Long Dan Pills)
21. For sore throat and chronic throat constriction with difficulty swallowing congee: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan) one liang, Alum (Dan Fan, ground), Frankincense (Ru Xiang, ground) each one fen. Pound and grind the three to a uniform powder, bind with refined sugar into pills the size of peas. Each dose one pill, wrap in cotton, hold in mouth to dissolve and swallow saliva; if not improved, repeat. (Shengji Zonglu Long Dan Gao)
22. For scrofula under the neck whether new or old, if hot select and clean Long Dan; pound the single herb into a powder. Each dose one qian and a spoonful, take with wine or rice beverage after meals and before bed. On overcast days, continue taking. (Shengji Zonglu Qingliang San)
23. For infants who sweat all over during the night: Chinese Gentian (Long Dan Cao) in any amount, or add Saposhnikovia (Fang Feng), powdered and made into vinegar‑paste pills the size of green beans. Each dose five to seven pills, take with rice beverage. (Youke Le Cui Tongshen Wan)
24. To promote lactation postpartum when milk does not flow: Di Dan Cao (Di Dan Cao), Trichosanthes Root (Tian Hua Fen) (as Gua Lou Gen), and Lettuce Seed (Wo Ju Zi) in equal parts, powdered. Each dose two qian, mix with warm scallion and wine and take, three to four times daily. (Puji Fang)

Golden cicada flower (Jin Chan Hua)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%87%91%E8%9D%89%E8%8A%B1
Names
Cicada Pupa Herb (Chanyongcao), Pupa Fungus (Yongrong), Cicada Fungus (Chanrongjun), Insect Flower (Chonghua), Cicada Flower (Chanhua), Large Cicada Herb (Dachancao)

Pupa Fungus (Yongrong)
Cicada Fungus (Chanrongjun)
Insect Flower (Chonghua)
Cicada Flower (Chanhua)
Large Cicada Herb (Dachancao)
Cultivation and Preparation of Cicada Flower (Jinchanhua)
Source
It consists of the conidiophore clusters of the Clavicipitaceae fungus Chanbangshubaojun (Chanbangshubaojun), the stromata of Large Cicada Herb (Dachancao) and the insect bodies they parasitize. From June to August, they are dug out from the soil, cleaned of dirt, and sun-dried.
[Original morphology]
1. Chanbangshubaojun fungus: conidiophore clusters grow in tufts, arise from the anterior end of the host, white when fresh, 1.5–6 cm high; stalks branched or unbranched, 0.1–0.2 cm in diameter, sometimes connected at the base, branched at the apex and covered with a powdery layer of conidia. Conidia oblong-ovoid, slightly acute at both ends, (6–9) μm × (2–2.5) μm, often contain two oil globules, hyaline and colorless.
2. Large Cicada Herb (Dachancao): insect body long-ellipsoid, slightly curved, about 3 cm long, 1–1.4 cm in diameter, resembling a cicada exuviae. The head of the insect bears 1–2 rod-shaped stromata, linear or curled, branched or unbranched, 3–7 cm long, 3–4 mm in diameter, dark brown, apex slightly swollen, surface with numerous small punctate protrusions.
[Ecological environment]
Grows on cicada larvae.
[Resource distribution]
1. Distributed in Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, Sichuan, Yunnan and other areas.
2. Distributed in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Sichuan, Yunnan and other areas.
Processing
Take the crude drug, remove impurities, wash clean, dry, and sieve off ash and debris.
[Nature, Taste and Channels Entered]
Sweet and salty, cold. Enters the Lung and Liver channels.
[Functions and Indications]
Dispel wind and clear heat, promote eruption of rashes, extinguish wind and stop convulsions, brighten the eyes and reduce ocular opacities. Used for externally-contracted wind-heat presenting with fever, dizziness, sore throat; early-stage measles with incomplete eruption; pediatric convulsions, night crying; red, swollen and painful eyes; and opacity of the ocular membrane obstructing vision.
[Dosage and Administration]
Internal use: decoction, 3–9 g.
Description
(1) Chanbangshubaojun fungus
This product consists of the insect body and the conidiophore clusters growing from its head. The insect body is long-ellipsoid, slightly curved, about 3 cm long, 1–4 cm in diameter, surface yellow-brown, mostly covered with gray mycelium, head bearing dense conidiophore clusters. Conidiophore clusters are branched or unbranched, 1.6–6 cm long, divided into a bulbous portion and a stalk; the bulbous portion is long-ellipsoid, ovoid or fusiform, 5–8 mm long, 2–3 mm in diameter, folded and powdery in appearance; the stalk is 1–2 mm in diameter, brown to dark brown. Brittle and easily broken; the insect body is filled with white or off-white soft material. Slight fragrance, mild taste.
(2) Large Cicada Herb (Dachancao)
This product consists of the insect body and the stromata growing from its anterior end. There are 1–2 stromata, branched or unbranched, 3–7 cm long, brown; the head is swollen and tapers toward the tip, 4–6 mm long, 6.5–7 mm in diameter, the surface showing small dots (ostiole openings where perithecia protrude), the stalk 4–5 mm in diameter. The insect body is white, its interior filled with white mycelium. Brittle and easily broken. Slight odor, mild taste.
Effects of Cicada Flower (Jinchanhua)
Efficacy
This product is the dried conidiophore clusters of the Clavicipitaceae fungus Chanbangshubaojun or the dried stromata of Large Cicada Herb (Dachancao) together with the dried parasitized insect bodies. Used for externally-contracted wind-heat: fever, dizziness, sore throat, early-stage measles with incomplete eruption, pediatric convulsions, night crying, red, swollen, painful eyes, and ocular membrane opacity obstructing vision.

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%B0%B7%E7%B2%BE%E8%8D%89
Name
Pipewort Flower
ear brush, ear‑picking herb, pearl herb, drumstick herb, button herb, Gu jing pearl
ear brush

drumstick herb
button herb

Cultivation and Processing of Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao)
Source
It is the capitulum inflorescence with flower stalk of the plant Gu jing cao in the Eriocaulaceae family.
Harvested in August to September; pull out the flower stalks, remove mud and impurities, and sun‑dry.
Properties and Flavor
Pungent and sweet, cold.
Appearance
A capitate inflorescence with the flower stalk. The inflorescence is flattened and round, 4–5 millimeters in diameter; at the base there are scaly pale‑yellow involucre bracts, tightly arranged in a disk; 30–40 small flowers, gray‑white, very densely arranged, surface covered with a white fine powder; when rubbed by hand, many black granules and gray‑green small seeds can be seen. The inflorescence is attached to a slender flower stalk about 15–18 centimeters long, yellow‑green, glossy; texture soft, not easily broken. Odorless, mild taste, becomes adhesive after prolonged chewing. Best quality is when the capitula are pearl‑sized and compact, gray‑white, with short, yellow‑green stalks, and free of roots, leaves and impurities.
Effects of Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao)
Functions
It is the capitulum inflorescence with flower stalk of the plant Gu jing cao in the Eriocaulaceae family.
Main indications: ocular opacities, night blindness, headache, toothache, throat obstruction, and epistaxis.
Channels Entered
Enters the Liver and Stomach channels.
Actions
Expels wind and disperses heat, brightens the eyes and reduces ocular opacities. Treats ocular opacities, night blindness, headache, toothache, throat obstruction and epistaxis.
① Kaibao Materia Medica: Mainly treats throat obstruction, tooth wind pain, and various ulcers and scabies.
② Compendium of Materia Medica: Treats headache, eye blindness and ocular films, post‑smallpox films, and stops bleeding.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decocted as a decoction, 9–12 grams; or charred into pills or powders.
External use: burn to preserve the ash, grind to a powder and sprinkle.
Precautions and Contraindications
① Ben Cao Shu: Avoid with iron.
② Depei Ben Cao: Contraindicated for eye disorders due to blood deficiency.
Formulas Using Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao)
① For wind‑heat ocular film or unclear vision at night: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 1–2 liang, duck liver 1–2 pieces (if no duck liver use white tofu). Add appropriate boiled water and stew for one hour; take after meals, once daily. (Fujian Folk Herbal Remedies)
② For ocular films: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) and Saposhnikovia root (Fang Feng) in equal parts. Grind to powder and take with rice water. (Compendium of Materia Medica)
③ For infant ocular films after smallpox: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 1 liang, raw clam shell powder 0.5 fen, black soybean skin 2 qian; add White Peony (Bai Shao) 3 qian (stir‑fry briefly with wine). Grind to fine powder. Take one leaf of pig liver, slice thin with a bamboo knife, fill with the powdered medicine, tie with grass string, place in a ceramic vessel with water and cook slowly until done; give the child to eat at any time, including the cooking juices, once or twice a month until cured. (Shengsheng Zhongmiao Fang)
④ For children with night blindness suddenly not seeing at night: one whole he‑goat liver, do not wash with water, split open with a bamboo knife, insert a pinch of Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao), cook in an earthenware pot until done, give to eat daily. Avoid iron utensils. If the child refuses to eat, roast and crush into pills the size of mung beans, take thirty pills each dose with tea. (Weisheng Jiabao Fang)
⑤ For unilateral or bilateral headache: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 1 liang, grind to powder, mix with wheat flour to make a paste on xuan paper as a plaster, apply to the painful area; replace when dry. (Yao Sengtan Ji Yan Fang)
⑥ For cerebrovascular headache: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) powder, verdigris (Tong Lu) powder each 1 qian, Mirabilite (Mang Xiao) 0.5 qian (powder). Grind and mix; place a pinch in the nostril and blow into the nasal cavity, or for unilateral headache blow into the nostril on the affected side. (Shengji Zonglu — Pipewort Flower Powder)
⑦ For dental wind sores, exposed gums: Burn Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) to ash 1 fen, Alum (Bai Fan) ash 1 fen, Toad venom (Chan Su) one piece (roasted), a little Musk (She Xiang). Grind together to a powder; take a small amount and apply to the affected area. (Sheng Hui Fang — Pipewort Flower Powder)
⑧ For epistaxis that will not stop all day with vexation: Pound Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) into a powder, mix two qian with hot wheat soup and take internally. (Sheng Hui Fang)
⑨ For infantile liver heat with hot palms and soles: whole Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) plant 2–3 liang, pig liver 2 liang. Add boiled water and stew for one hour; take once or twice daily. (Fujian Folk Herbal Remedies)
⑩ For wind‑toxin red eyes, whether old or new: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) remove roots 1 liang, wash clean with well‑spring water, grind to 0.5 liang; roasted fermented soybeans (douchi) dried 0.5 liang; well moss roasted and dried 0.5 liang. Pound these four ingredients into a fine powder. Each dose two qian, take on an empty stomach, mix with well water and take. (Shengji Zonglu)
⑾ For red swollen painful eyes: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 15 g, Shepherd’s‑purse (Jie Cai) 15 g, Wedelia/Small‑leaf ground tea (Ai Di Cha) 15 g. Decoct in water and take. (Hunan Materia Medica)
⑿ For infantile ocular gary with redness and itching: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 1 liang, Atractylodes (Cang Zhu) 0.1 liang peeled and scraped and lightly roasted, Cicada slough ash 0.1 liang, talc powder 0.1 liang. Grind to a fine powder; each dose one qian. (Puji Fang)
⒀ For post‑smallpox eye films or itchy tearing: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 1 liang, raw clam shell powder 2 liang, grind to powder. Take one leaf of boar liver, slice thin with a bamboo knife, pack in the powder, tie with ramie thread, place in a ceramic vessel with water, cook slowly until done, and give the child to eat. (Weisheng Yijian Fang)
⒁ For scaly eruptions with ocular films: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) and pork trotter (stir‑fried) and Mung bean skin and Cicada slough in equal parts. Grind to powder; each dose three qian, take after meals with rice‑soaked water. (Zheng Zhi Zhunsheng)
⒂ For infantile night blindness where the child cannot see at night: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 0.5 liang, Licorice (Gan Cao) 0.5 liang, lightly roasted to slight redness and scraped; Dried Ginger (Gan Jiang) 0.1 liang, scraped. Pound to powder, make with one liang of flour into a baked cake with the medicine placed in the center, warm slowly until cooked, give with good tea. Take one dose each morning; vision may return after three days. (Puji Fang)
⒃ For brain pain and brow pain: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 2 qian, Earthworm (Di Long) 3 qian, Frankincense (Ru Xiang) 1 qian. Grind to powder; take half a qian each time, burn in a smoking tube and let the smoke enter the nostrils left and right. (Ben Cao Shu)
⒄ For common cold with fever, headache, and pharyngitis: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 9–12 g, decoct in water and take. (Shaanxi‑Gansu‑Ningxia‑Qinghai Selected Herbs)
⒅ For severe head wind with eyes closed and extreme pain: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao), Earthworm (Di Long), Realgar (Xiong Huang) in equal parts. Grind to powder, wrap in plum‑red paper rolled into a tube, burn and inhale the smoke through the nose; the eyes will open, then take other medicines. (Danxi Zhaixuan)
⒆ For infantile heatstroke with vomiting and diarrhea: whole Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) plant 30–60 g, fish‑brain stone (Yu Nao Shi) 9–15 g. Decoct in water and take twice daily for several consecutive days until cured. (Quanzhou Materia Medica)
⒇ For malnutrition and accumulation: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) 15 g, Sigesbeckia (Wei Ling Cai) 15 g. Decoct in water and take. (Hunan Materia Medica)
(21) For various sequelae, persistent leukorrhea and difficult urinary dribbling: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) and pig bone marrow each 1 liang. Decoction in wine and take, adjusting to taste. (Wen Tang Ji Yan Fang)
(22) For urinary stones: Pipewort Flower (Gu jing cao) and Imperata cylindrica (Zhuo Rong Cao) each 30 g. Roast and take with water. (Guizhou Herbal Remedies)

input:
Gypsum (Shi Gao)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%9F%B3%E8%86%8F
Name
Gypsum
Fine stone (Xishi), Fine-laminated stone (Xilishi), Soft gypsum (Ruanshigao), Cold-water stone (Hanshuishi), White Tiger (Baihu), Jade large stone (Yudashi), Ice stone (Bingshi)
Fine stone (Xishi)
Fine-laminated stone (Xilishi)
Soft gypsum (Ruanshigao)
White Tiger (Baihu)
Jade large stone (Yudashi)
Lamb stone (Shigao)
Raw gypsum (Sheng Shigao)
Cultivation and processing of gypsum (Shigao)
Source
A sulfate-group gypsum mineral. Generally excavated in winter; after extraction remove adhering soil and miscellaneous stones.
Flavor and properties
Pungent and sweet, cold.
Processing
Raw gypsum (Sheng Shigao): remove impurities and stones, wash off soil, crush into small pieces.
Calcined gypsum (Duan Shigao): take clean gypsum chunks, place in a crucible, calcine in a smokeless furnace until friable, remove, cool, and pulverize.
Appearance
Occurs as long blocky or irregular columnar fibrous crystalline aggregates of varying size. Overall white to off-white. Large blocks have two flat faces, dull and without luster or grain. The material is heavy but loose, easily broken into small pieces; longitudinal fracture shows fibrous texture with a silky luster. Odorless, bland taste. Best quality is large blocks, white in color, loose in texture, fibrous, and free of foreign stone. When burned, the flame is stained pale reddish yellow and it can fuse into white magnetic alkaline beads. When heated to 120°C it loses part of its crystalline water and becomes a white powdery or blocky calcined gypsum.
Effects of gypsum
Actions
A sulfate-group gypsum mineral.
Treats febrile diseases with strong fever that will not remit, vexation and delirium, delirious speech and madness, thirst and dry throat, lung-heat wheezing and panting, summer-heat with spontaneous sweating, stomach-fire causing headache and toothache, excessive febrile toxins causing severe rashes, mouth and tongue sores. Calcined gypsum applied topically promotes tissue generation and restrains sores. Externally treats carbuncles, ulcers that will not close, and scalds and burns.
Channels entered
Enters the Lung meridian and the Stomach meridian.
Indications
Raw use relieves the exterior, clears heat, removes vexation and stops thirst. Calcined and applied externally promotes tissue generation and restrains sores.
Treats febrile disease with strong persistent fever, vexation and delirium, delirious speech and madness, thirst and dry throat, lung-heat wheezing and panting, summer-heat with spontaneous sweating, stomach-fire headache and toothache, excessive heat-toxin with eruption of spots and rashes, mouth and tongue sores. Externally treats carbuncles and ulcers that will not close, scalds and burns.
1. Bencao: Treats wind-cold-heat in the middle burner, counterflow qi under the heart, fright asthma, dry mouth and tongue, inability to breathe, firm abdominal pain, promotes lactation, and metallic wounds.
2. Bie Lu: Removes seasonal headache and body fever, great heat of the three burners, skin heat, heat in the stomach and diaphragm, releases the muscle layer and promotes sweating, stops wasting thirst and rebellious qi, abdominal distention with sudden qi attack and panting, throat heat. Can also be used as a bath decoction.
3. Yaoxing Lun: Treats cold-damage headache like splitting, strong fever, skin hot and dry as if burnt, vexation and thirst, releases the muscle layer, induces toxic sweating, promotes movement of bound stomach accumulations, vexation, oppression under the heart, agitation, treats dry and parched lips and mouth. Decoction with scallion to make tea relieves headache.
4. Ri Hua Zi Materia Medica: Treats pathogenic heat madness, suppresses lactation, dizzy head wind, vexation and agitation, applied to teeth benefits the teeth.
5. Zhenzhu Nang: Stops Yangming headache, relieves wasting thirst, summer-heat, and tidal fever.
6. Yongyao Xinf a: A very cold medicine for the Stomach meridian, moistens the Lung and clears heat, disperses yin pathogens, soothes the Spleen and benefits qi.
7. Bencao Yanyi Buyi: Grind to powder, mix with vinegar into pills the size of mung beans, to purge stomach fire, phlegm-fire, and food accumulation.
8. Yang Shiying: Calcination best for contracting sores and preventing muscle decay.
9. Bencao Mengquan: For severe epigastric pain, swallow.
10. Changsha Yaojie: Clears Heart and Lung, treats vexation and agitation, drains constrained heat, stops dry thirst, treats heat madness and fire cough, checks spontaneous sweating from heat, dissolves hot phlegm, stops nasal bleeding, treats oral sores, relieves throat pain, promotes lactation, resolves breast abscess, relieves fire burns, treats metallic wounds.
11. Bencao Zaixin: Treats headache and fever, dim vision and persistent film over the eye, toothache, kills parasites, promotes urination.
Dosage and administration
15–60 g, decoct first.
Contraindications and cautions
Contraindicated in Spleen and Stomach deficiency cold, and in heat from blood deficiency or yin deficiency.
1. Bencao Jing Jizhu: Egg white as an adjuvant. Incompatible with Mangcao and Mamu du gong.
2. Yaoxing Lun: Incompatible with Croton (Badou). Averse to iron.
3. Yixue Qiyuan: "Secret of Treatments" states it can cold the stomach and suppress appetite; should not be used lightly unless the abdomen is extremely hot.
Formulas using gypsum
1. For combined three-yang disease with abdominal fullness and heavy body, difficulty turning over, numbness of mouth, dirty face, delirious speech and urine discharge, sweating causes delirium, purging causes forehead sweating, hands and feet cold; if spontaneous sweating:
Anemarrhena (Zhimu) 6 liang, Gypsum (Shigao) 1 jin (crushed), Licorice (roasted, Gancao) 2 liang, Polished rice (Jingmi) 6 he. Combine four ingredients, use one dou of water, cook rice until hot, strain the soup, take warm one sheng, three times daily. (Shang Han Lun: Baihu Tang)
2. For early warm-disease with floating and forceful pulse, strong body heat; also for early-stage common cold when there is no aversion to cold but there is internal heat: Raw gypsum (Sheng Shigao) 2 liang (pounded fine), raw polished rice (Sheng Jingmi) 2.5 liang. Use three large bowls of water, decoct until rice is soft and hot to yield about two large bowls of clear juice; drink hot as much as possible to induce sweat over the whole body; disease will be cured. If Yangming bowel heat is already in excess, do not drink at once while hot; sip warm drinks slowly to eliminate the heat. (Yixue Zhongzhong Canxi Lu: Shigao Jingmi Tang)
3. For damp-warmth with excessive sweating, delirious speech and thirst: Gypsum (Shigao) and roasted Licorice (Gancao) equal parts. Grind to powder. Each dose two qian, suspend in gruel and swallow. (Shanghan Zongbeng Lun)
4. For Taiyin warm-disease where sweating must not be induced, sweating without exudation causing rash, or excessive sweating causing delirium and rash:
Gypsum (Shigao) 1 liang, Anemarrhena (Zhimu) 4 qian, raw Licorice (Gancao) 3 qian, Scrophularia root (Xuanshen) 3 qian, Rhinoceros horn & turtle shell (Xigui) 2 qian, white polished rice 1 he. Use eight cups of water, boil down to three cups, take three times daily; reboil the residue once for one bedtime dose. (Wenbing Tiaobian: Huanban Tang)
5. After sweating when GuiZhi Tang should not be used and coughing occurs without high fever:
Ephedra (Mahuang) 4 liang (nodes removed), Bitter apricot kernel (Kuxingren) 50 pieces (skins and tips removed), Licorice (Gancao, roasted) 1 liang, Gypsum (Shigao) half jin (crushed, wrapped in cotton). Use seven sheng of water, decoct ephedra until two sheng reduced, remove scum, add other herbs, decoct to three sheng, strain, take warm one sheng. (Shang Han Lun: Mahuang Xingren Gancao Shigao Tang)
6. For phlegm-heat wheeze with phlegm gushing like a spring:
Hanshuishi (Cold-water stone) and Gypsum (Shigao) equal parts; grind to fine powder. Decoction with ginseng (Renshen) soup, take three qian after meals. (Suwen Bingji Baoming Ji: Shuangyu San)
7. For severe heat cough and wheeze that is chronic: Gypsum (Shigao) 2 liang, Licorice (Gancao, roasted) 0.5 liang. Grind to powder. Each dose three qian, mix with fresh well-water and take; mix with raw ginger juice and honey to take. (Puji Fang: Shigao San)
8. For bone-steaming afternoon fever, dry mouth and thirst: Gypsum (Shigao) 6 liang (crushed, wrapped in cotton and calcined), large Wumei (Mume) 20 pieces. Use seven sheng of water, decoct to four sheng, remove residue, add three he of honey, sip slowly. (Waitai)
9. For wind-evil epilepsy with dry mouth and tongue, vexation, headache and sudden feverish confusion: Gypsum (Shigao) half jin, polished rice 1–3 he. Use five large cups of water, decoct gypsum to two large cups, remove gypsum, cook rice into congee, add two scallion white stalks (Congbai) and two he fermented soybean sauce (Douzhi), cook together, when warm take on an empty stomach. Gypsum can be used three times. (Shenghui Fang: Shigao Congee)
10. For unilateral or bilateral headache with eye pain: Gypsum (Shigao) and Burdock seed (Niubangzi, roasted) equal parts. Grind to fine powder. Each dose two qian, take after meals with warm wine or clear tea. (Qixiao Liangfang: Shigao Niubangzi San)
11. For upper diaphragm accumulation toxin, mouth and tongue sores, swollen painful throat: Cold-water stone (calcined Hanshuishi) 3 liang, Cinnabar (Zhusha) 3.5 qian (separately ground), raw "naozi" half zhi. Grind to powder, apply a small amount to the lesion, rinse saliva, use several times day and night. (Sanyin Fang: Longshi San)
12. For pharyngeal wind: Gypsum (Shigao) 1 liang, Anemarrhena (Zhimu) 3 qian, Licorice (Gancao) 1 qian, Scrophularia root (Xuanshen) 5 qian, Trichosanthes root (Tianhuafen) 3 qian. Decoction and take. (Houk e Geheimet: Shigao Tang)
13. For stomach-fire toothache: good soft gypsum 1 liang, calcine over fire, quench with light wine and grind to powder; add Saposhnikovia (Fangfeng), Schizonepeta (Jingjie), Asarum (Xixin), Angelica dahurica (Baizhi) each 5 fen, grind to powder, use daily to rub teeth. (Baoshoutang Experience Formula)
14. For dim vision and night blurring unresponsive to many treatments: Gypsum powder each dose one qian, place on a slice of pig liver, thin, put the medicine on it, bind in place, simmer in a sand pot until cooked, cut and eat one piece per day. (Mingmu Fang)
15. For pediatric febrile disease with vomiting and diarrhea and yellow emaciation:
Cold-water stone (Hanshuishi) and Gypsum (Shigao) each half liang, Licorice (Gancao raw) 1 qian. Grind together to fine powder. Each dose one zhi, or half qian to one qian, take after meals with warm broth. (Xiao'er Yaozheng Zhijue: Yulu San)
16. For wind-heat causing muscle and bone pain: Gypsum (Shigao) 3 qian, Feiluo flour 7 qian. Grind to powder, mix with water, calcine red, cool and fix, dissolve in hot wine and take, cover and induce sweat, take continuously for three days. (Weisheng Zaxing)
17. For wounds by metal and blades with ongoing bleeding: Gypsum (Shigao), Areca (Binglang), Coptis (Huanglian, root removed) each 1 liang, Phellodendron bark (Huangbai) half liang. Grind to fine powder, apply according to amount to stop bleeding; once bleeding is controlled, immersion in water is permissible. (Xiao'er Weisheng Zhongwei Lun Fang)
18. For scalds and burns: pound gypsum to powder and apply. (Zhouhou Fang)
19. For breast abscess: any amount of gypsum calcined to red, taken from the ground, cover bowl to draw out fire toxin, finely grind. Each dose three qian, take with warm wine; add more wine to intoxication, sleep and take another dose on waking. (Renzhai Zhizhi Fang: One Drunken Gypsum)
20. For carbuncle ulcers that open and discharge pus, to search out pus, clear heat and promote tissue generation: Calcined gypsum (Duan Shigao) 9 qian, Huangling medicine 1 qian. Grind extremely fine, store in porcelain bottle. Use a small amount sprinkled on the lesion. (Yizong Jinjian: 91 Dan)
21. For hemorrhoids with leaking: Calcined gypsum 1 jin, Borneol (Bingpian) 5 g, grind to fine powder, apply externally to lesions. (Inner Mongolia: Selected New Clinical Methods of Chinese Herbs)
22. For pediatric wheeze and cough: fry gypsum in fire until it flies to powder, take half qian with honey. (Weisheng Yijian Fang)
23. For epidemic mumps: Raw gypsum and Phellodendron bark (Huangbai) equal amounts, grind to powder, mix with water or vinegar into a paste, spread on gauze about 0.5 cm thick, apply to affected area 1–2 times daily. (Shaanxi New Medicine 1977(5):35)
24. For eczema: Calcined gypsum 60 g, Bletilla tuber (Bai Ji) 30 g, Mitro-seng (?) (Mi tuo song) 21 g, Calomel (Qingfen) 15 g, Ku fan 9 g. Grind extremely fine, mix with sesame oil or petroleum jelly into a 50% ointment and apply to lesions. If pus exudes, the powder may be sprinkled dry 3–5 times daily. Avoid washing with warm water or soap when using. (National Compilation of Chinese Herbs)
Dietary therapy recipes
1. Gypsum damp-resolving congee
Raw gypsum 120 g, Aged tangerine peel (Chenpi) 6 g, Bitter apricot kernel (Kuxingren) 15 g, Coix seed (Yiyiren) 30 g, Chestnut kernels (Limi) 50 g, rock sugar to taste. Decoction: boil the first four ingredients, strain and keep the liquid, add chestnuts and cook into congee, when cooked add rock sugar and simmer briefly until dissolved. Take appropriate amounts.
Function: Clears summer heat and disseminates qi, strengthens the Spleen and resolves dampness.
2. Gypsum and water buffalo horn cake
Ingredients: Gypsum 60 g, Water buffalo horn powder 60 g, Anemarrhena (Zhimu) 10 g, Moutan bark (Mud anpi) 15 g, Indigo leaf (Daqingye) 15 g, wheat flour 200 g, rock sugar to taste.
Preparation: Decoction gypsum, water buffalo horn powder, Anemarrhena, Moutan bark and Indigo leaf for 30 minutes, strain and reserve the liquid, add rock sugar and simmer until dissolved. When cool, combine the liquid with flour and prepare pancakes in the usual way; divide into 2–3 doses to take.
Function: Clears heat and detoxifies, cools blood and resolves spots.
