Ligusticum root (Gao Ben)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%97%81%E6%9C%AC
Names
Chinese Ligusticum, Jehol Ligusticum, Chinese Ligusticum Rhizome, Jehol Ligusticum Rhizome
Gaobei, Guiqing, Dixin, Shanzhai, Weixiang, Weijing, Gaoban
Gaobei
Guiqing
Dixin
Shanzhai
Weixiang
Weijing
Gaoban
Liao Gaoben
Chuan Gaoben
Xi Huang Gaoben
Cultivation and Processing of Gaoben
Source
This product is the dried rhizome and root of the Umbelliferae family Ligusticum species Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben, Ligusticum sinense Oliv.) or Liao Chinese Ligusticum (Liao Gaoben, Ligusticum jeholense Nakai et Kitag.).
Properties (Taste and Nature)
Taste pungent; nature moist
Appearance
(1) Chinese Ligusticum rhizome is irregularly nodular and cylindrical, slightly twisted, slightly branched, 3–10 cm long. Surface brown to dark brown, rough, with longitudinal wrinkles, cork-like bark that peels off easily; the upper end has one to several round hole-like stem bases; the lower side has numerous point-like protruding root scars and remnant roots. Light in weight, relatively hard, breaks easily; fracture surface yellow or yellow-white, fibrous. Strong aromatic odor; taste pungent, bitter, slightly numbing.
(2) Liao Chinese Ligusticum rhizome is irregularly clumped or columnar, 2–10 cm long, 0.5–1.5 cm in diameter. Surface brownish, the upper end has clustered leaf bases and raised nodes, the lower end has many slender curved roots.
Preferably those that are large, relatively thick, firm in texture, and strongly aromatic.
Effects of Gaoben
Functions
This product is the dried rhizome and root of Ligusticum (Gaoben) or Liao Gaoben of the Umbelliferae family.
Main indications: wind-cold headache, vertex pain, cold-damp abdominal pain, diarrhea, hernia and abdominal masses, scabies and tinea.
Channels
Enters
Bladder meridian
Indications
Dispels wind, cold and damp pathogens. Treats wind-cold headache, vertex pain, cold-damp abdominal pain, diarrhea, hernia and abdominal masses, scabies and tinea.
(1) Benjing: Mainly for women’s hernia and abdominal masses, cold in the genital region, swelling and pain, acute abdominal pain; relieves wind headache.
(2) Bielu: Repels mist and dew and moistens; treats dragging wind pathogens and traumatic wounds.
(3) Yaoxinglun: Treats pernicious wind flowing into the lower back causing cold pain; can promote urination, move blood, dispel headaches, snoring and sores.
(4) Rihuazi Bencao: Treats disorders, and skin blemishes, rosacea, and acne.
(5) Yixue Qiyuan: Treats headache, chest pain, and toothache.
(6) Li Gao: Treats wind-damp of the head, face and whole-body skin.
(7) Wang Haogu: Treats diseases of the Governing Vessel, rigidity of the spine and syncope.
(8) Gangmu: Treats abscesses, promotes pus discharge and relieves internal obstruction.
(9) Bencao Zheng: Treats wind-damp diarrhea, wind epilepsy, miasma and pestilence.
(10) Bencao Zaixin: Treats wind-damp itching and pain, headaches and swollen eyes, diarrhea and malarial dysentery.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoct, 3–10 g; or used in pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, decoct for wash; or grind to powder and mix for topical application.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated for headaches due to blood deficiency.
Formulas Using Gaoben
(1) For wind-damp joint pain: Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) 9 g,
Atractylodes rhizome (Cangzhu)
9 g,
Siler root (Fangfeng)
9 g,
Achyranthes root (Niuxi)
12 g. Decoction with water. (Qingdao Handbook of Chinese Herbal Medicine)
(2) For all wind disorders, unilateral or bilateral headache, ear blockage and mental oppression, great remedy for cold-damage and head wind, widespread sores and tinea, obstinate numbness of the feet:
Chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong)
,
Asarum (Xixin)
,
Angelica dahurica (Baizhi)
,
Licorice (Gancao)
, Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) in equal parts. Grind to powder, each herb four liang, add one jin of calcined gypsum powder, moisten with water into pills, each liang makes eight pills, take one pill, chew with mint tea after meals. (Puji Fang: White Dragon Pill)
(3) For gastric spasm and abdominal pain: Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) five qian,
Atractylodes rhizome (Cangzhu)
three qian, decocted in water and taken. (Xinjiang Handbook of Chinese Herbal Medicine)
(4) For scabies and tinea: decoct Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) for bathing, and use to wash clothing. (Collection of Pediatric Hygiene Formulas)
(5) For adults’ and children’s dry white dandruff: use Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) and
Angelica dahurica (Baizhi)
in equal parts powdered, rub on at night and comb in the morning; the grime will come off. (Collected Notes on Common Materia Medica)
(6) For redness on the nose or face: grind Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) into fine powder. First use soapberry water to rub the red area, wipe dry, mix with cold water or honey and apply; when dry apply again. (Jifeng Puji Fang: Gaoben Powder)
(7) For severe solid abdominal pain when stools have already been discharged: Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) half liang,
Atractylodes rhizome (Cangzhu)
one liang. Make into coarse powder; each dose one liang, with two cups of water, decoct to one cup, take with warm wine. (Baoming Ji: Gaoben Decoction)
(8) If sweating is excessive leading to continuous leakage and the person becomes delirious, this is extreme depletion of Yangming; treat with a formula to stop sweating:
Atractylodes macrocephala rhizome (Baizhu)
, Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben),
Chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong)
, Fragrant,
Angelica dahurica (Baizhi)
in equal parts. Grind into fine powder; each herb powder one liang, fine rice flour one liang five qian, mix evenly, put into a damp raw silk bag and dust over the body. (Xingyuan Shengchun: Shouyang Wen Powder)
(9) For leukorrhea, pediatric malnutrition and worm erosion: Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben) (seedlings removed),
Angelica sinensis (Danggui)
(sliced and roasted),
Bitter apricot kernel (Kuxingren)
(soaked in decoction to remove skins and tips) each half liang. Grind into powder. Use a small bead-sized amount, wrap with cotton and insert into worm holes. (Puji Fang: Gaoben Powder)
(10) For summer prickly heat itching and pain: freshly drawn water mix Gaoben juice with clam powder and apply. Snow water is especially good. (Puji Fang)
(11) For dental carbuncle and ulceration: Chinese Ligusticum (Gaoben),
Cimicifuga (Shengma)
, pig-tooth soap
(intact teeth, burned to ash to preserve properties) each half liang,
Gypsum (Shigao)
one liang and a half. Pound the four ingredients into a fine powder. At bedtime dip a finger and rub onto the teeth, rinse lightly to retain the medicated aroma. (Boji Fang: Black Powder)

Lophatherum (Dan Zhu Ye)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%B7%A1%E7%AB%B9%E5%8F%B6
Name
Common Lophatherum Herb, Common Lophatherum
Bamboo-leaf Ophiopogon (Zhu Ye Men Dong Qing), Foliate Entwining Herb (Mi Shen Cao), Mountain-chicken-seed (Shan Ji Mi), Golden Bamboo Leaf (Jin Zhu Ye), Long Bamboo Leaf (Chang Zhu Ye), Mountain-winter (Shan Dong), Earth Bamboo (Di Zhu), Dan Bamboo Seed (Dan Zhu Mi), Under-forest Bamboo (Lin Xia Zhu)
Bamboo leaf
Dan bamboo
Dan bamboo seed
Sweet bamboo leaf
Foliate Entwining Herb (Mi Shen Cao)
Bamboo-leaf Ophiopogon (Zhu Ye Men Dong Qing)
Mountain-chicken-seed (Shan Ji Mi)
Golden Bamboo Leaf (Jin Zhu Ye)
Long Bamboo Leaf (Chang Zhu Ye)
Mountain-winter (Shan Dong)
Earth Bamboo (Di Zhu)
Under-forest Bamboo (Lin Xia Zhu)
Cultivation and processing of Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye)
Source
This product is the dried stems and leaves of the grass family plant Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye).
Properties and flavor
Sweet; bland; cold
Characteristics
Dried leafy stems and branches, total length 30–60 centimeters. Commercial material is often cut. Stems are grayish-yellow, hollow, flattened-cylindrical in shape, diameter 1–2 millimeters; jointed, leaf sheaths clasp the stem, with long white soft hairs along the edges. Leaves are lanceolate, wrinkled and curled, length 5–20 centimeters, width 2–3.5 centimeters, bluish-green or yellow-green, both surfaces glabrous or with short soft hairs, veins parallel with distinct small transverse veins, texture light and fragile. Odor faint, taste mild. Preferred grade: bluish-green color, large leaves, few petioles, no roots or inflorescences.
Effects of Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye)
Functions
This product is the dried stems and leaves of the grass family plant Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye).
Treats febrile disease with thirst, vexation, dark or painful urination, turbid painful dribbling, oral ulcers and tongue sores, swollen painful gums.
Channels entered
Enters the Heart channel, Lung channel, Gallbladder channel, and Stomach channel.
Main indications
Clears Heart fire, relieves vexation and heat, promotes urination. Treats febrile disease with thirst, vexation, dark or painful urination, turbid painful dribbling, oral ulcers and tongue sores, swollen painful gums.
① Compendium of Materia Medica: relieves vexation and heat, promotes urination, clears the Heart.
② Essentials of the Nature of Crude Herbs: dissolves phlegm and stops thirst, eliminates Upper Burner fire, brightens the eyes, promotes urination, treats leukorrhea, reduces fever, disperses hemorrhoidal pus and toxins.
③ Woling Materia Medica: dispels stomach heat.
④ Materia Medica Renewed: clears Heart fire, promotes urination, relieves vexation and thirst, antidote for pediatric pox toxins; external lesions with malignant toxins.
⑤ Handy Prescriptions from Flora: dissolves phlegm, stops thirst. Treats vexation and heat, cough and asthma, hemoptysis, vomiting and retching, pediatric convulsions.
⑥ Classified Herbal Natures: treats cough and asthma, ocular conditions.
⑦ Modern Practical Chinese Medicine: cools and relieves heat, diuretic. Treats febrile disease with thirst, painful or scanty urination, vexation with insomnia, swollen gums, stomatitis.
⑧ Guangxi Materia Medica Records: treats nasal bleeding.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoction, 9–15 g.
Precautions and contraindications
Use with caution in patients without real fire or damp-heat; contraindicated in constitutional deficiency with cold.
Formulas using Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye)
① For treating febrile thirst: Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye) five sheng, Poria (Fu Ling), Gypsum (Shi Gao) (crushed) each three taels, wheat three sheng, Trichosanthes fruit (Gua Lou) two taels. Boil the five ingredients: first boil the bamboo leaf in two dou of water, take eight sheng, then add the remaining herbs and boil to obtain four sheng, remove dregs and take warm. (Wai Tai Mi Yao formula: Bamboo Leaf Decoction)
② After resolution of typhoid, emaciation and shortness of breath, qi counterflow with retching: bamboo leaf two handfuls, Gypsum (Shi Gao) one sheng, Pinellia (Ban Xia) (washed) half jin, Ginseng (Ren Shen) two taels, Ophiopogon root (Mai Dong) (removed core) one sheng, Licorice root (Gan Cao) (prepared) two taels, Japonica rice half sheng. (Shang Han Lun: Bamboo Leaf and Gypsum Decoction)
③ After cholera relief, vexation, restlessness and thirst, inability to lie still: strongly boil bamboo leaf and drink five or six he (units). (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Bamboo Leaf Decoction)
④ Pediatric heart wind-heat with mental confusion: Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye) one handful, Japonica rice one he, Capillaris wormwood (Yin Chen) half tael. Boil the two herbs in two large cups of water to obtain one cup of juice, remove dregs, add rice and make congee to eat. (Sheng Hui Fang: Dan Zhu Ye Congee)
⑤ Postpartum wind-stroke with fever, face flushed red, panting and headache: bamboo leaf one handful, Kudzu root (Ge Gen) three taels, Saposhnikovia root (Fang Feng) one tael, Platycodon root (Jie Geng) and Licorice root (Gan Cao) each one tael, Cinnamon twig (Gui Zhi) one tael, Ginseng (Ren Shen) one tael, Aconite (Fu Zi) (processed) one piece, Jujube (Da Zao) fifteen pieces, Fresh ginger (Sheng Jiang) five taels. Boil the ten herbs in one dou of water to obtain two and a half sheng, divide and take warm in three doses; cover warmly to induce sweating. (Jin Gui Yao Lue: Bamboo Leaf Decoction)
⑥ For various dribbling painful urinary disorders: Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye), Plantain seed (Che Qian Zi), Jujube (Da Zao), Black bean (Wu Dou) (roasted, shelled), Juncus pith (Deng Xin Cao), Licorice root (Gan Cao) each 1.5 qian. Prepare as one dose: use two cups of water, decoct to seventy percent, remove dregs, take warm at any time. (Qi Xiao Liang Fang: Dan Zhu Ye Decoction)
⑦ For Heart-heat transferring to the small intestine, oral ulcers and painful dribbling: Common Lophatherum Herb (Dan Zhu Ye) 2 qian, Akebia stem (Mu Tong) 1 qian, raw Licorice root (Sheng Gan Cao) 8 fen, Plantain seed (Che Qian Zi) (roasted) 3 qian, Raw Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang) 6 qian, decoct in water and take. (Yi Li Jian Yi: Dao Chi San)
⑧ Postpartum extreme collapse of blood and qi with sweating: Dan Zhu Ye, decoct into three he of soup, take slightly warm, then take another dose shortly after. (Jing Xiao Chan Bao)
⑨ For eruptive head sores that come and go with red burning pain: burn one jin of bamboo leaf to ash, pound and sieve into fine powder, mix evenly with egg white, apply three to four times daily. (Sheng Hui Fang)
⑩ For summer-heat qi deficiency with vexation: fresh bamboo leaf (Xian Zhu Ye) and Pseudostellaria root (Tai Zi Shen) each 9 g, Hyacinth bean flower (Bian Dou Hua) 6 g, fresh Lotus leaf (He Ye) half leaf, decoct and take. (Anhui Materia Medica)

Ma Wei Lian (Ma Wei Lian)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%A9%AC%E5%B0%BE%E8%BF%9E
Name
Meadowrue Root and Rhizome, Root and Rhizome of Baikal Meadowrue, Root and Rhizome of Manyleaf Meadowrue
Mawei Huanglian (Mawei Huanglian), Jinsi Huanglian (Jinsi Huanglian), Cao Huanglian (Cao Huanglian)
Mawei Huanglian (Mawei Huanglian)
Jinsi Huanglian (Jinsi Huanglian)
Cao Huanglian (Cao Huanglian)
Tangsongcao root (Tangsongcao gen)
Cultivation and Processing of Mawei Lian
Source
The rhizomes and roots of plants of the Ranunculaceae family such as Manyleaf Thalictrum (Duoye Tangsongcao) and Baikal Thalictrum (Beijiaer Tangsongcao). Harvested from September to November to the following January to February; after digging, shake off earth and sand, trim off stems and shoots, and sun-dry.
Taste and Properties
Taste bitter; nature cold
Description
The dried rhizome has many bulbils at the upper end, each bulbil about 4 millimeters thick, with traces of stem and shoot scars and often enclosed by thin scale-leaf fragments. The rhizome is elongated, externally brownish; the ventral surface densely produces bundled fibrous roots shaped like a horse tail; the fibrous roots are 13 to 25 centimeters long, 2 to 3 millimeters thick, externally reddish-yellow or golden yellow, glossy, with fine longitudinal striations; the old cork and cortex often shed in ring-like segments, and those not yet shed can be removed by rubbing with the fingers.
Light in weight, brittle and easily broken. The rhizome cross-section has a brownish outer ring and a yellow woody pith inside; the fibrous root cross-section is deep yellow with a thin layer of golden-yellow epidermis externally. Odor slight, taste slightly bitter. The best quality is when the root strands are uniform and golden yellow in color.
Effects of Mawei Lian
Functions and Actions
The rhizomes and roots of Ranunculaceae plants such as Manyleaf Thalictrum (Duoye Tangsongcao) and Baikal Thalictrum (Beijiaer Tangsongcao).
Main Indications
Dysentery, enteritis, infectious hepatitis, common cold, measles, carbuncles and furuncles, conjunctivitis.
Channels Entered
Enters
Heart meridian
;
Liver meridian
;
Large Intestine meridian
Indications
Clears heat and dries dampness, detoxifies. Treats dysentery, enteritis, infectious hepatitis, common cold, measles, carbuncles and furuncles, conjunctivitis.
1. From "Gangmu Taiyi": removes pathogenic heat from the skin, inner membrane, exterior and sinews; used for pediatric colds and pox.
2. From "Commonly Used Tibetan Medicinal Herbs": clears heat and detoxifies, dispels wind and cools the blood, reduces inflammation and stops dysentery. Treats conjunctivitis, infectious hepatitis, carbuncles and furuncles, dysentery. Leaves and flowers treat arthritis.
3. From "Xinjiang Handbook of Chinese Medicinal Herbs": clears heat and dries dampness.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoct as a decoction, 3–15 g, or grind to a powder, or make into an instant powder.
External use: appropriate amount; fresh material pounded and applied; or decoction used to wash; or dry product ground to powder and sprinkled; or made into an ointment and applied.
Precautions and Contraindications
Use with caution in those with spleen and stomach deficiency-cold.
Formulas Using Mawei Lian
1. For pediatric colds with fever and measles about to erupt: Mawei Huanglian (Mawei Huanglian),
Cicada slough (Chan Tui)
,
Chrysanthemum flower (Ju Hua)
, Dali seed (
Burdock seed (Niu Bang Zi)
),
Saposhnikovia root (Fang Feng)
,
Mint (Bo He)
,
Licorice (Gan Cao)
, decoct and drink. (Sichuan Materia Medica)
2. For dysentery and enteritis: Mawei Huanglian nine qian,
Costus root (Mu Xiang)
three qian. Grind to a fine powder. Take 1 to 2 qian each time, three times a day. (Xinjiang Handbook of Chinese Medicinal Herbs)
3. For damp-heat vomiting: Mawei Lian one and a half qian,
Evodia fruit (Wu Zhu Yu)
four fen, decoct and take. (Qinghai Commonly Used Chinese Medicinal Herbs)
4. For febrile disease with vexation and thirst: Mawei Lian and roasted Gardenia (Zhi Zi) three qian each, decoct and take. (Qinghai Commonly Used Chinese Medicinal Herbs)
5. For mouth and tongue sores, conjunctivitis, tonsillitis: Mawei Huanglian three qian,
Baical Skullcap (Huang Qin)
two qian, Phellodendron bark (
Huang Bai
) three qian,
Gardenia (Zhi Zi)
three qian,
Burdock seed (Niu Bang Zi)
two qian,
Forsythia (Lian Qiao)
five qian,
Licorice (Gan Cao)
two qian. Decoction for oral administration. (Xinjiang Handbook of Chinese Medicinal Herbs)
6. For red, swollen carbuncles and furuncles: Mawei Huanglian two qian, decoct for oral use and grind to powder for external sprinkling or make into an ointment for topical use. (Yunnan Chinese Materia Medica)
7. For exudative dermatitis: appropriate amount of Mawei Huanglian, roast dry and grind to powder, sprinkle on the affected area. Or use in equal parts with pine pollen (Song Hua Fen). If the area becomes dry and cracked after sprinkling, mix with sesame oil (Xiang You) and apply. (Xinjiang Handbook of Chinese Medicinal Herbs)
8. For tinea pedis (athlete’s foot): Mawei Huanglian five qian,
Phellodendron bark (Huang Bai)
one liang, one fresh pig bile (Zhu Dan Zhi),
Borneol (Bing Pian)
three fen. First decoct Mawei Huanglian and Huang Bai in water to a paste, remove dregs, then add pig bile, simmer over low heat for 1–2 minutes, remove from heat, wait until warm and stir in borneol until evenly mixed; apply to the affected area every night. (Xinjiang Handbook of Chinese Medicinal Herbs)

Cultivation and Processing of Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi)
Source
The dried flower buds of Magnoliaceae plants such as Wangchun Yulan, Yulan, and Wudang Yulan. From January to March, the unopen buds are cut off at the flower stalks; during the day they are sun-dried, and at night stacked to sweat so that the inside and outside have uniform moisture. When dried to about fifty percent, they are piled for 1–2 days and then further sun-dried until completely dry. If it rains, they may be dried by heat.
Properties and Flavor
Taste: pungent; Nature: warm
Processing
Pick out and clean away stem and debris, crush for use; for medicinal use slightly roast; those already opened are inferior, those withered are not good.
Physical Characteristics
(1) Wangchun Yulan
Flower buds are oblong-ovoid, like a brush tip, 1.2–2.5 cm long, 0.8–1.5 cm in diameter; the base often has a short woody stalk about 5 mm long, with whitish dot-like lenticels on the stalk. Bracts 2–3 layers, two per layer, with small scale buds between two layers of bracts; outer surface of bracts densely covered with gray-white or gray-green long pubescence, inner surface brownish without hairs. Perianth segments 9 in 3 whorls, brownish; outer whorl perianth segments strap-shaped, about one quarter the length of the inner two whorls, resembling sepals; stamens numerous, arranged spirally on the lower part of the receptacle, filaments flattened, anthers linear; pistils numerous, spirally arranged on the upper part of the receptacle. Light in weight, brittle in texture. Fragrant aroma, taste pungent and cool with a slight bitterness.
(2) Yulan
Flower buds 1.5–3 cm long, 1–1.5 cm in diameter, with relatively stout basal stalks and light brown lenticels. Bracts outer surface densely covered with gray-white or gray-green pubescence. Perianth segments 9, without marked difference between inner and outer whorls.
(3) Wudang Yulan
Flower buds 3–4 cm long, 1–2 cm in diameter, with stout stalks and reddish-brown lenticels. Bracts outer surface densely covered with pale yellow or pale yellow-green pubescence; in some specimens the outer layer bract pubescence has fallen off, appearing dark brown. Perianth segments 10–15, without marked difference between inner and outer whorls.
Among the three medicinal materials, those with large, unopened, yellow-green buds without stalks are best.
Effects of Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi)
Functions
The dried flower buds of Magnoliaceae plants such as Wangchun Yulan, Yulan, and Wudang Yulan.
Treats headache, nasal congestion and discharges, nasal obstruction, and toothache.
Channels Entered
Lung channel; Stomach channel
Indications
Expels wind and opens the orifices. Treats headache, rhinitis or sinusitis, nasal obstruction, and toothache.
① Ben Jing (Classic Materia Medica): Acts on the five viscera and the body’s cold and heat, wind-induced head pain, facial numbness.
② Bei Lu (Alternate Records): Warms the center and releases the muscles, unblocks the nine orifices, clears nasal obstruction and causes flowing nasal discharge, treats facial swelling radiating to the teeth causing toothache, dizziness and a sensation as if on a carriage or boat. Promotes hair growth, expels white parasites.
③ Yao Xing Lun (Treatise on Medicinal Properties): Can treat facial oiliness. Used for facial luster, promotes brightness.
④ Ri Hua Zi Ben Cao (Daily Flower’s Materia Medica): Unblocks channels and vessels, brightens the eyes. Treats headache, aversion to cold, bodily stiffness, and itching.
⑤ Dian Nan Ben Cao (Southwest Materia Medica): Treats cerebral leakage and nasal sinus issues, expels wind; can be roasted on new tile into powder. Treats facial cold pain, gastric qi pain; take with warm wine.
⑥ Ben Cao Gang Mu (Compendium of Materia Medica): For rhinitis, nasal catarrh, nasal blockage, nasal sores, and post-measles nasal sores, grind into fine powder, add a little musk, dip scallion white into it and insert several times.
⑦ Yu Qiu Yao Jie (Yu Qiu’s Pharmacological Explanation): Drains the lung and descends rebellious qi, facilitates qi and disperses accumulations.
⑧ Jiangxi Zhong Yao (Jiangxi Province Medicinal Materials): Externally can promote uterine contraction and has oxytocic effects.
Dosage and Administration
Internal: Decoction, 3–10 g, preferably decocted in a bag; or used in pills and powders.
External: Appropriate amount, powdered and snuffed into the nostrils; or use its distilled aromatic water and drop into the nostrils.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated for those with yin deficiency and vigorous fire.
① Ben Cao Jing Ji Zhu (Collected Annotations on Materia Medica): Chuanxiong (Chuan Xiong) is its envoy. Combines badly with five types of stone resin. Averse to Acorus (Chang Pu), Puhuang (Pollen of Typha), Coptis (Huang Lian), gypsum (Shi Gao), and Huang Huan (Huang Huan).
② Ben Cao Jing Kui (Collected Defects of Materia Medica): Persons with qi deficiency should avoid it; those whose headache is due to blood deficiency with blazing fire should not take it; toothache due to stomach fire is contraindicated.
③ Ben Cao Hui Yan (Collected Sayings on Materia Medica): People with qi deficiency, who only occasionally catch wind-cold causing orifices to be blocked, should not use it.
Formulas Using Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi)
① For rhinitis: Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) half liang (about 9 g), Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 2 qian 5 fen (about 7.5 g), Dahurian Angelica Root (Bai Zhi) one liang (about 15 g), Mint (Bo He) leaf half qian (about 1.25 g). Dry all in the sun and grind into a fine powder. Each dose two qian (about 5 g), take with scallion and clear tea after meals. (Ji Sheng Fang: Cang Er Powder)
② For rhinitis and sinusitis:
(1) Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) 3 qian (about 7.5 g), three chicken eggs. Cook together; eat the eggs and drink the decoction. (Selected Simple and Effective Prescriptions)
(2) Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) four parts, Goose-Does-Not-Eat-Grass (literally; E bu shi cao) one part. Soak in water 4–8 hours then distill to obtain aromatic water; use as nasal drops. (Guangdong Selected Herbal Prescriptions)
③ For nasal discharge where a mass grows inside the nostril: Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) (dehaired) four liang, Mulberry Root-bark (Sang Bai Pi) (honey-fried) four liang, Gardenia Fruit (Zhi Zi) one liang, Immature Bitter Orange (Zhi Shi), Platycodon Root (Jie Geng), Dahurian Angelica Root (Bai Zhi) each two liang. Grind all into fine powder. Each dose two qian, take with mild radish soup. (Yao Yi Da Quan)
④ For severe nasal blockage preventing breathing: Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) and Chuanxiong (Chuan Xiong) each one liang, Asarum (Xi Xin) (with sprouts removed) seven qian and a half, Akebia or Mu Tong (Mu Tong) half liang. Grind into fine powder. Use a small amount wrapped in cotton and insert into the nostrils, replace when wet. Cures in five to seven days. (Zheng Zhi Zhun Sheng: Chuanxiong Powder)
⑤ For inability to smell fragrances: Soap Pod (Zao Jiao, also called Pig-Tooth Soap), Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi), Acorus Rhizome (Shi Chang Pu) in equal parts. Grind into powder. Wrap in cotton and insert into nostrils. (Mei’s Newly Compiled Effective Prescriptions)
⑥ For nasal swelling or sores in the nose (often due to alcoholic toxin): Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) one liang, Sichuan Coptis (Chuan Huang Lian) five qian, Forsythia Fruit (Lian Qiao) two liang. Lightly fry all, grind into powder. Take three qian after each meal with plain water. (Miao’s Selected Prescriptions)
⑦ For toothache, swelling, or ulcerated gums: Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) one liang, Cnidium Fruit (She Chuang Zi) two liang, Qing Salt (Qing Yan) five qian. Grind together into powder and apply. (Ben Cao Hui Yan)
⑧ For head and facial swelling and itching as if insects crawling (wind-phlegm type): Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) one liang, Processed Aconite (White Fu Zi), Pinellia Rhizome (Ban Xia), Trichosanthes Root (Tian Hua Fen), Dahurian Angelica Root (Bai Zhi), Stiff Silkworm (Jiang Can), Scrophularia Root (Xuan Shen), Red Peony Root (Chi Shao) each five qian, Mint (Bo He) eight qian. Divide into ten doses and take. (Gu Jin Yi Zhun)
⑨ For dizziness, faintness and nausea (cold-phlegm type): Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) one liang, prepared Pinellia (Zhi Ban Xia), Bile-processed Arisaema (Dan Nan Xing), Gastrodia Rhizome (Tian Ma), Dried Ginger (Gan Jiang), Szechuan Lovage Root (Chuan Xiong) each eight qian. Grind into powder, make into pills with water. Take three qian nightly with plain water. (Ben Cao Hui Yan)
⑩ For rhinitis, nasal catarrh, nasal blockage, nasal sores and post-measles nasal sores: Grind Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) into fine powder, add a little Musk (She Xiang), dip scallion white and apply several times; very effective. (Compendium of Materia Medica)
⑾ For slight redness of the nasal tip and sores inside the nose: Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) powdered, add a little Bing Pian (borneol) and Musk (She Xiang), wrap in cotton and insert. (Danxi Xin Fa)
⑿ For inability to smell fragrances: Soap Pod (Zao Jiao), Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi), Acorus Rhizome (Shi Chang Pu) in equal parts. Grind into powder and wrap in cotton to insert into the nostrils. (Mei’s Newly Compiled Effective Prescriptions)
⒀ Mint, Cocklebur, Magnolia, Dahurian Angelica Tea:
Mint (Bo He) 6 g, Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 12 g, Magnolia Flower (Xin Yi) 6 g, Dahurian Angelica Root (Bai Zhi) 6 g, Scallion white (Cong Bai) 3 stalks, Tea leaves 2 g. Put all the above into a pot, decoct, discard dregs and take the liquid. Use as a tea substitute. Efficacy: disperses wind and unblocks the orifices. Indications: treats rhinitis, sinusitis and related disorders.

Mahonia (Gong Lao Mu)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E5%8A%9F%E5%8A%B3%E6%9C%A8
Names
Earth Yellow-Cypress (Tu Huangbai), Yellow Heaven Bamboo (Huang Tianzhu), Mouse Does Not Climb (Shu bu pa), Mountain Yellow-Cypress (Shan Huangbai), Large-leaved Huanglian (Da ye Huanglian), Ten Big Merits (Shi da Gonglao), Umbrella-handle Huanglian (San ba Huanglian), Large Mouse Yellow (Da lao shu huang), Mouse Yellow (Lao shu huang), Mouse Thorn (Lao shu ci), Thorn Huanglian (Ci Huanglian), Boxwood (Huangyang mu), Goat-horn Lily (Yangjiao lian), Earth Huangqin (Tu Huangqin), Goat-horn Huanglian (Yangjiao Huanglian), Eight-corner Goat (Ba jiao yang), Earth Huanglian (Tu Huanglian).
Morphology
1. Broad-leaved Shi Da Gonglao: evergreen shrub, 1–4 m high. Stem surface earth-yellow or brown, rough, cross-section yellow. Leaves alternate, thickly leathery, petiolate, base expanded and clasping the stem; odd-pinnate leaves, 25–40 cm long, 7–15 leaflets, lateral leaflets sessile, broadly ovate, unequal in size, 4–12 cm long, 2.5–4.5 cm wide, terminal leaflet larger and petiolated, apex gradually acuminate, base broadly cuneate or nearly rounded, margins revolute, with 2–8 large spine-like serrations per side, upper surface dark green and glossy, lower surface yellow-green. Racemose inflorescences at stem apex, erect, 5–10 cm long, 6–9 fascicled clusters, 1 small bract; sepals 9, arranged in three rows; flowers yellow-brown, petals 6, oblong, apex with two shallow lobes, base with two dense glands; stamens 6; pistil 1. Berries ovoid, about 5 mm in diameter, bluish-black when mature, covered with bloom. Flowering August–October, fruiting October–December.
2. Narrow-leaved Shi Da Gonglao: evergreen shrub, 1–2 m high. Stem erect, bark gray, much branched. Leaves alternate; odd-pinnate; petiole base swollen; leaves coriaceous, 5–13 leaflets, narrowly oblanceolate to lanceolate, 6–12 cm long, 0.7–1.5 cm wide, apex long acuminate with a sharp spine, base cuneate, margins with 6–13 spine-like serrations per side, upper surface fresh dark green and glossy, veins inconspicuous, lower surface yellow-green; veins 3-forking from the base. Racemose inflorescences arise from the axils of terminal branch scales, 3–6 cm long, pedicel base with an involucre, bracts ovate-triangular; sepals 9, petal-like; petals 6, yellow, oblong, entire; stamens 6, filaments thread-like, anthers short-cleft; ovary ovoid, without a style, stigma capitate. Berries ovoid, mature fruit ovoid, bluish-black when ripe, covered with bloom. Flowering July–August, fruiting August–October.
Ecological environment
1. Grows in sunny hillside shrubs, also cultivated.
2. Grows in hillside shrubs and roadsides. Also cultivated in gardens.
Resource distribution
1. Distributed in Shaanxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Sichuan and other areas.
2. Distributed in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Hubei, Hunan, Guangdong and other areas.

Cultivation and processing of Mahonia (Gonglao mu)
Source
This product is the dried stems of Berberidaceae plants Broad-leaved Shi Da Gonglao Mahonia bealei (Fort.) Carr. or Narrow-leaved Shi Da Gonglao Mahonia fortunei (Lindl.) Fedde.
Processing
Remove impurities from the crude drug, grade, wash clean, moisten thoroughly, slice thinly, dry, and sieve off dust.
Appearance
This product consists of nearly circular slices, 1–2.5 cm in diameter. Surface gray-yellow to brown, rough, soft, slightly elastic, outer bark easily peels off. Cross-section shows narrow bark, brown, wide wood, bright yellow, several concentric rings and closely arranged radiating striations visible, pith darker in color. Texture hard. Slight odor, bitter taste.
Properties and meridian tropism
Bitter, cold. Enters the liver, stomach, and large intestine meridians.
Functions and indications
Clears heat and dries dampness, drains fire and relieves toxicity. Used for damp-heat diarrhea and dysentery, jaundice, red swollen painful eyes, stomach-fire toothache, sores and boils, abscesses, dysentery; jaundice-type hepatitis.
Effects of Mahonia (Gonglao mu)
Efficacy
This product is the dried stems of the Berberidaceae plants Broad-leaved Shi Da Gonglao or Narrow-leaved Shi Da Gonglao. Used for damp-heat diarrhea and dysentery, jaundice, red swollen painful eyes, stomach-fire toothache, sores and boils, abscesses, dysentery; jaundice-type hepatitis.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoct as a decoction, 5–10 g.
External use: appropriate amount, decoct for washing; or grind to powder and apply as a paste.
Precautions and contraindications
Those with a cold-deficient constitution should avoid use.

Mahonia Leaf (Shi Da Gong Lao Ye)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E5%8D%81%E5%A4%A7%E5%8A%9F%E5%8A%B3%E5%8F%B6
Name
Chinese Mahonia Leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè)
Gougu Thorn (Gǒu Gǔ Cì)
Mahonia (Shí Dà Gōng Láo)
Cat-ear Thorn (Māo ěr Cì)
Ram-horn Thorn (Yáng Jiǎo Cì)
Ganggu Tree (Gàng Gǔ Shù)
Mahonia Leaf (Gōng Láo Yè)
Gougu (Gǒu Gǔ)
Cultivation and Processing of Chinese Mahonia Leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè)
Source
Leaves of Berberidaceae plants: broad-leaved Mahonia, narrow-leaved Mahonia or South China Mahonia; collected in autumn.
Taste and Properties
Yin Pian Xin Can: bitter, cold.
Characteristics
① Broad-leaved Mahonia leaf: obovate-elliptic, apex gradually acute with a sharp spine, base cordate or nearly truncate and oblique, margins with 2–8 spinous teeth on each side, tooth apices slightly bent toward the underside; upper surface purple-green and glossy, lower surface yellow-green. Texture hard and brittle. Odor faint, taste mild. Produced in Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi and other regions.
② Narrow-leaved Mahonia leaf: narrowly lanceolate, margins with 6–13 spinous teeth on each side; otherwise same as above. Produced in Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi and other regions.
③ South China Mahonia leaf: medicinal character same as broad-leaved Mahonia leaf. Used in Fujian and Yunnan.
According to the Illustrated Examination of Plant Names and Realities, the Shida Gonglao refers to the Berberidaceae plants mentioned above. However, at present medicinal material is only found in a few areas such as Zhejiang and Jiangxi; folk use also occurs in Fujian, Guangdong and Guangxi. The Mahonia leaf used in Tibet is the leaf of Tibetan Mahonia. As for the Mahonia leaves widely used in the market, they are the leaves of the evergreen species Gougu. See the entry for Gougu leaf.
Effects of Chinese Mahonia Leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè)
Actions
Leaves of Berberidaceae plants: broad-leaved Mahonia, narrow-leaved Mahonia or South China Mahonia.
Main indications: pulmonary tuberculosis with hemoptysis, steaming bone tidal fever, dizziness and tinnitus, low back soreness and weak legs, irritability, red eyes.
Channels
Ben Cao Zai Xin: enters the Lung meridian.
Indications
Clears heat and tonifies deficiency, stops cough and transforms phlegm, dries dampness and detoxifies. Treats pulmonary tuberculosis with hemoptysis, steaming bone tidal fever, dizziness and tinnitus, low back soreness and weak legs, irritability, red eyes.
① Ben Cao Zai Xin: treats consumptive cough due to deficiency.
② Illustrated Examination of Plant Names and Realities: treats hematemesis (vomiting blood).
③ Yin Pian Xin Can: treats pulmonary consumption, stops cough and transforms phlegm, reduces deficiency-heat, kills parasites.
④ Modern Practical Chinese Materia Medica: a cooling nourishing tonic. Efficacy similar to Ligustrum fruit (Nǚzhēn Zǐ); suitable for tidal fever, steaming bone, low back soreness, weak knees, dizziness, tinnitus and similar syndromes.
⑤ Lu Chuan Ben Cao: drains fire and reduces fever. Treats febrile disease with fever, vexation, diarrhea, red eyes.
⑥ Common Tibetan Medicinal Herbs: treats damp-heat dysentery, red swollen painful eyes, carbuncles and sores.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 6–9 g.
External use: appropriate amount; grind to powder and apply as a paste.
Precautions and Contraindications
Use with caution in patients with spleen and stomach deficiency-cold.
Formulas Using Chinese Mahonia Leaf
For wind-fire toothache: Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 3 qian. Decoction, take immediately. One dose daily; if pain is severe, take two doses. (Jiangxi Materia Medica)
Clinical Applications
① Treatment of Pulmonary Tuberculosis
Qinggu San was used to treat 34 cases of pulmonary tuberculosis of the tidal-fever type that were unresponsive to anti-tuberculosis drugs.
Method: Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 20 g, Guobo leaf (Guǒ Bǔ Yè) 20 g,
Bletilla rhizome (Bái Jí) 30 g, Yuanshen (Xuán Shēn, Scrophularia root) 10 g, Digu Pi (Dì Gǔ Pí) 10 g, Qinjiao (Qín Jiāo, Gentiana macrophylla) 10 g,
Licorice (Gān Cǎo) 6 g; one dose daily, decocted and taken in three divided doses.
Modifications: for severe hemoptysis add raw Rehmannia (Shēng Dì Huáng) 30 g, soaked in boiling water and taken as a drink; for thirst add Ophiopogon (Mài Dōng) 20 g; for severe coughing with dyspnea add reed root (Lú Gēn) 20 g. One dose daily; one course lasts three months. Before treatment chest X-rays were taken; of the 34 cases all were in the infiltrative stage of pulmonary tuberculosis, three had thin-walled cavities, five were sputum positive for tubercle bacilli, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate was generally elevated.
Results: markedly effective in 24 cases (symptoms disappeared, pulmonary lesions absorbed, cavities closed, ESR returned to normal); improved in 9 cases (symptoms improved, pulmonary lesions partially absorbed, cavities reduced, ESR decreased); ineffective in 1 case (no symptom reduction, pulmonary lesions aggravated and transferred to other therapies).
② Cancer treatment — Formula for Liver Cancer
Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 30 g,
Black nightshade (Lóng Kuí) 20 g, Baiying (Bái Yīng) 20 g, eucalyptus leaf (Ān Shù Yè) 20 g, verbena (Mǎ Biān Cǎo) 20 g, Hedyotis diffusa / Oldenlandia (Bái Huā Shé Shé Cǎo) 20 g,
Scutellaria barbata (Bàn Zhī Lián) 10 g, licorice (Gān Cǎo) 10 g. Modifications: for severe hepatic pain add Qiye Lian (Qī Yè Lián) 20 g; for true deficiency add Baishen (Bái Shēn) 5 g; grind and mix into juice. One dose daily, decocted and taken in three divided doses. This formula is suitable for early-stage liver cancer.
Lung cancer formula: Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 20 g, Scutellaria barbata (Bàn Zhī Lián) 20 g, common ivy (Cháng Chūn Téng) 20 g, Ji Shiteng (Jī Shǐ Téng) 20 g, Prunella (Xià Kū Cǎo) 20 g,
Houttuynia (Yú Xīng Cǎo) 30 g, Liaogewang (Liǎo Gē Wáng) 10 g,
pomegranate peel (Shí Liú Pí) 15 g, Notoginseng (Tián Qī / Sān Qī) 6 g (ground and mixed); one dose daily, decocted and taken in three divided doses. Modifications: for hemoptysis add charred Puhuang (Pú Huáng Tàn) 10 g and Imperata root (Bái Máo Gēn) 30 g; for dyspnea add mulberry bark (Sāng Bái Pí) and Tingli Zi (Tíng Lì Zǐ) 10 g each. If this formula is taken continuously for three months it can gradually reduce lesions and resolve clinical symptoms.
③ Treatment of Respiratory Tract Inflammation — Bronchitis Formula
Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 20 g, knotweed (Hǔ Zhàng) 20 g, Feijingcao (Fèi Jīng Cǎo) 20 g, short earth tea (Ǎi Dì Chá) 20 g; loquat leaf (Pípá Yè) de-haired 15 g, Teng Bai Wei (Téng Bái Wēi) 15 g,
licorice (Gān Cǎo) 6 g; one dose daily, decocted and taken in three divided doses.
Modifications: for abundant white phlegm add Pinellia (Bàn Xià) 8 g; for abundant yellow phlegm add Jinxingcao (Jīn Xīng Cǎo) 20 g. This formula is suitable for acute bronchitis.
Pneumonia formula:
Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 12 g; Tu Fuling (Tǔ Fú Líng) 20 g, Ǎi Dì Chá 20 g, Jīn Xīng Cǎo 20 g, E Bu Shi Cao 20 g, Fèng Wěi Cǎo 20 g; licorice (Gān Cǎo) 10 g; one dose daily, decocted and taken in three divided doses.
Modifications: for cough with rusty sputum add Zhimu leaf (Zhì Mù Yè) and Imperata root (Bái Máo Gēn) 20 g each; for high fever not abating add raw gypsum (Shēng Shí Gāo) 20 g; for dyspnea add fine tea leaves 20 g and mulberry bark (Sāng Pí) 15 g. This formula, combined with Western medicine, shows remarkable efficacy.
④ Treatment of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
Some have used Chinese Mahonia leaf to treat nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Method: Chinese Mahonia leaf (Shí Dà Gōng Láo Yè) 30 g; Prunella (Xià Kū Cǎo) and fresh pomegranate peel (Xiān Shí Liú Pí) 20 g each; licorice (Gān Cǎo) 5 g; one dose daily.

Cultivation and processing of Mint (bohe)
Source
This product is the dried aerial parts of the Lamiaceae family Mentha genus plant Mint (bohe, Mentha haplocalyx Briq.). In the summer and autumn seasons when stems and leaves are luxuriant or when flowers have opened to the third whorl, choose sunny days, harvest in successive cuts, and dry in the sun or in the shade.
Properties and flavor
Acrid, cool.
Processing
Pick out impurities, remove remaining roots; first shake off the leaves and set them aside, then spray the stems with clean water until thoroughly moistened, cut into sections, sun-dry, and finally mix evenly with the leaves.
Description
The whole dried herb: stems are quadrangular-cylindrical, 15–35 cm long, 2–4 mm in diameter, yellow-brown with purple or green, with nodes; internodes 3–7 cm long; upper parts have opposite branches; surfaces covered with white pubescence, denser on the ridges; texture brittle, easily broken, fracture surface whitish, hollow. Leaves opposite, often curled and wrinkled, mostly broken; upper surface dark green, lower surface light green, with white pubescence; brittle. Branch tips often bear verticillaster inflorescences, yellow-brown, many corollas remaining. Aromatic smell, spicy-cool taste. The best are whole-dried, rootless, leaf-abundant, green in color, and strongly aromatic.
Actions of Mint (bohe)
Functions and indications
This product is the dried aerial parts of the Lamiaceae family Mentha genus plant Mint (bohe).
Used for wind-heat common cold, early-stage warm-epidemic febrile disease, headache, red eyes, sore throat with obstruction, mouth ulcers, urticaria, measles, and chest and hypochondriac distention.
Channels entered
Lung channel, Liver channel.
Main indications
Disperse wind-heat; clear the head and eyes; release rashes. Used for wind-heat common cold, early-stage warm-epidemic febrile disease, headache, red eyes, sore throat with obstruction, mouth ulcers, urticaria, measles, and chest and hypochondriac distention.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoction, 3–6 g, should not be boiled for long, add near the end of decoction; or used in pills and powders.
External use: appropriate amount, decocted water applied first or crushed juice applied as a topical dressing.
Precautions and contraindications
Contraindicated in yin deficiency with blood dryness, exuberant liver yang, or exterior deficiency with profuse sweating.
1. From Yao Xing Lun: Newly ill convalescents should not eat; it causes continuous deficient sweating.
2. From Qianjin·Food Therapy: Promotes emaciation and thirst disease.
3. From Benjing Fengyuan: Excessive or prolonged use causes deficient cold; do not use in yin-deficiency fever, cough, spontaneous sweating.
4. From Bencao Congxin: Its acrid aroma diffuses qi; excessive use harms the lungs and injures the heart; the deficient should avoid it.
Formulas using Mint (bohe)
① Clear the upper burner and transform phlegm, benefit the throat and diaphragm, treat wind-heat: powdered mint refined with honey into pills the size of gorgon seed; take one pill at a time. White sugar may also be used. (Jianbian Danfang)
② Treat red, painful, suppurating eyes: mint soaked overnight in fresh ginger juice, sun-dried and powdered, use one qian each time, soak in boiling water to wash. (Mingmu Jingyan Fang)
③ Treat scrofulous swellings that have formed lumps, are painful, ulcerate, with continuous pus discharge irrespective of distance: one bundle of mint about bowl-sized (shade-dried), ten strips of Gleditsia pods (zaojia; each one chi two cun long and not worm-eaten, remove black skin, coat with vinegar, roast until golden). Crush, soak in one hu of wine for three nights, take out and sun-dry, then soak three more nights; continue until all wine is used up, bake dry, grind into powder, mix with cooked rice to form pills the size of wutongzi. Before meals take twenty pills with Astragalus (huangqi) decoction; halve the dose for children. (Shenghuifang: Mint pills)
④ Treat wind-induced itching: large mint, cicada slough equally powdered, take one qian with warm wine. (Yonglei Qianfang)
⑤ Treat bloody dysentery: decoction of mint leaves taken alone. (Puji Fang)
⑥ Treat continuous nosebleed: drop mint juice into nostril; or boil dry mint in water, wrap with cotton and pack into the nose. (Benshi Fang)
⑦ Treat bee and wasp stings: apply mint plaster. (Meng Shen, Bixiao Fang)
⑧ Treat fire toxin sores like cauterization, internal fire-toxin causing sores on the buttocks with oozing juices: frequently apply decocted mint. (Yishuo)
⑨ Treat earache: drop fresh mint crushed juice into the ear. (Mindong Bencao)
⑩ Treat men and women with wind-cold cough and nasal congestion with heavy voice: wild mint (ye bohe) 2 qian, aged tangerine peel (chenpi) 2 qian, apricot kernel (bitter apricot kernel, kuxingren) 2 qian (skin and tips removed); add bamboo leaves (danzhuye) 15 pieces, decoct in water and take. (Diannan Bencao)
⑾ Treat conjunctivitis: wash mint leaves with cold boiled water and then soak in breast milk for 10–30 minutes. Rinse affected eye with 5% saline warm water, then place mint leaf over the affected eye for 10 minutes and replace as needed, several times daily. (Fujian Yaowuzi)
⑿ Treat cerebrospinal leak, nasal fetid discharge: wild mint in any amount, decoct in water, take with rice wine dropwise. (Diannan Bencao)
⒀ Treat dry or moist scabies arising from damp-heat causing severe persistent itching: mint 1 liang, Stemona (baibu) 1 liang, Kochia seed (difuzi) 1 liang. Decoction used to wash one to two times daily. (Jiren Jiyan Fang)
⒁ Treat hidden skin rash that does not surface with itching: mint leaves 10 g (bohe), Schizonepeta (jingjie) 10 g, Saposhnikovia (fangfeng) 10 g, cicada slough (chantui) 6 g. Decoction taken orally. (Sichuan Zhongyao Zhi 1980)
Dietary therapy recipes
1. Chrysanthemum-Mulberry-Mint-Bamboo Leaf Tea
Chrysanthemum (juhua) 5 g, Mulberry leaf (sangye) 5 g, Mint (bohe) 3 g, Lophatherum leaf (danzhuye) 30 g, Imperata root (baimaogen) 30 g. Put all ingredients in a teapot, pour boiling water and steep for 10 minutes. Use as a tea and drink as desired.
Functions: Acrid and cool to release the exterior, clears and benefits the throat. Indications: wind-heat common cold, fever and headache, spontaneous sweating and nasal congestion, swollen painful throat, cough with viscous sputum.
2. Mint-Xanthium-Magnolia-Angelica Tea
Mint (bohe) 6 g, Xanthium fruit (cangerzi) 12 g, Magnolia flower (xinyi) 6 g, Angelica dahurica (baizhi) 6 g, white part of scallion (congbai) 3 stalks, tea leaves (chaye) 2 g. Put the above medicines into a pot, decoct in water, remove dregs and take the decoction. Drink as tea.
Functions: Disperse wind and open the orifices. Indications: rhinitis, sinusitis and related disorders.
3. Mint with Brown Sugar Drink
Mint (bohe) 15 g, brown sugar (hongtang) 60 g. Decoction and sweeten with sugar, can be used as a tea.
Functions: Dietary therapy for liver cancer — this medicinal diet clears heat, benefits diuresis and reduces jaundice; may be selected for jaundice and ascites.
4. Apricot Kernel and Mint Porridge
Apricot kernel (bitter apricot kernel, kuxingren) 30 g (peel and tips removed), fresh mint (bohe) 10 g, hulled rice (gengmi) 50 g. Boil the apricot kernels in boiling water until 70% cooked, add the hulled rice and continue to cook; when nearly done add the mint and cook until finished.
Functions: Acrid dispersing to release the exterior, warms the lungs and stops wheezing.
5. Mint Porridge
Fresh mint (bohe) 30 g, japonica rice 60 g. Decoction of mint is prepared and strained for the liquid; cook the japonica rice into porridge, when cooked add the mint decoction and simmer briefly. One dose daily, divide into morning and evening portions.
Functions: Unblock the diaphragm and benefit the throat, disperse wind-heat. Indications: early-stage measles, exterior wind-heat.
6. Mulberry Leaf-Mint-Loquat Tea
Mulberry leaf (sangye) 500 g, yellow chrysanthemum (juhua) 250 g, loquat leaf (pipaye) 250 g, mint (bohe) 250 g. Grind the above into a coarse powder, pack into clean gauze bags, each bag 10–15 g. Take one bag per cup, pour boiling water and steep, cover and let sit for 10 minutes. Drink as a tea frequently.
Functions: Disperse wind and clear heat, release the exterior and clear the lungs. Indications: early-stage wind-heat common cold.

Mulberry leaf (Sang Ye)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%A1%91%E5%8F%B6
Name
Mulberry Leaf (Sang Ye)
Iron Fan (Tie Shan Zi), Silkworm Leaf (Can Ye)
Silkworm Leaf (Can Ye)
Frosted Leaf (Shuang Ye)
Double Leaf (Shuang Ye)
Winter Mulberry Leaf (Dong Sang Ye)
Immortal Herb (Shen Xian Cao)
Roasted Mulberry Leaf (Zhi Sang Ye)
Cultivation and Processing of Mulberry Leaf
Source
From the leaves of the mulberry (Morus) of the Moraceae family. Leaves are harvested after frost in October to November; remove fine branches and impurities, then sun-dry.
Morphology
A deciduous shrub or small tree, 3–15 m tall. Bark gray-white with linear shallow fissures; root bark yellow-brown or reddish-yellow, strongly fibrous.
Simple leaves alternate; petiole 1–2.5 cm long; leaf blade ovate or broadly ovate, 5–20 cm long, 4–10 cm wide, apex acute or acuminate, base rounded or nearly cordate, margin with coarse or rounded teeth, sometimes irregularly lobed, glabrous and shiny above, with short hairs along veins beneath and hair in the axils; three basal veins arising and interlacing with finer veins into a reticulate pattern, more distinct on the underside; stipules lanceolate, falling early.
Flowers unisexual, dioecious; male and female inflorescences arranged in spike-like catkin inflorescences, axillary; female spikes 1–2 cm long, pubescent, peduncle 5–10 mm; male spikes 1–2.5 cm long, pendulous, slightly pubescent; male flowers with 4 perianth segments and 4 stamens, with a sterile pistil in the center; female flowers with 4 perianth segments fused at the base, stigma 2-lobed.
The achenes are aggregated into many clustered ovoid or oblong multiple fruits, 1–2.5 cm long, green at first and becoming fleshy, dark purple or red when ripe. Seeds small. Flowering April–May, fruiting May–June.
Habitat and Distribution
Ecology: grows on hills, slopes, beside villages, in fields, etc.; mostly cultivated.
Resource distribution: distributed throughout the country.
Taste and Properties
Taste: bitter and sweet; nature: cold.
Processing
Mulberry Leaf (Sang Ye): pick out impurities, rub or crumble, remove stems, and sieve off dirt.
Honey-fried Mulberry Leaf (Mi Sang Ye): take clean mulberry leaves, mix with refined cooked honey and a little boiling water, combine and let sit briefly, then place in a pan and stir-fry over low heat until no longer sticky to the touch; remove and cool. (Per 100 jin of mulberry leaves use 20–25 jin of refined honey)
Characteristics
Leaves often wrinkled and broken. Intact leaves have petioles 1–2.5 cm long; when flattened leaf blades are ovate or broadly ovate, 8–15 cm long, 7–13 cm wide, apex gradually acute, base truncate, rounded or cordate, margin serrate or with blunt teeth, some irregularly divided.
Upper surface yellow-green or pale yellow-brown, some with small wart-like projections; lower surface slightly lighter, veins prominent, fine veins reticulate, veins sparsely pubescent, vein bases with tufted hairs. Brittle texture. Slight aroma, taste mild and slightly bitter and astringent. Best when leaves are large and yellow-green in color.
Therapeutic Effects of Mulberry Leaf
Functions
From the leaves of the mulberry (Morus) of the Moraceae family.
Treats wind-warm febrile conditions with fever, headache, red eyes, thirst, lung-heat cough, wind-bi (wind-damp obstruction), urticaria, and elephantiasis of the lower limbs.
Channels Entered
Enters the Lung channel
Liver channel
Indications
Expels wind and clears heat, cools the blood and brightens the eyes. Treats wind-warm febrile disease with fever, headache, red eyes, thirst, lung-heat cough, wind-bi, urticaria, and lower limb elephantiasis.
1. Shennong Bencao Jing: dispels cold and heat, induces sweating.
2. Tang Bencao: decoct to a concentrated juice; treats beriberi and edema, benefits the large and small intestines.
3. Meng Shen: roast and fry and drink as a tea to stop thirst.
4. Bencao Shiyi: treats cholera with abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea; in winter use dried leaves cooked strongly. Finely scrape and boil in a large pot until reduced to the color of brown sugar to remove chronic wind and lingering blood stasis.
5. Rihuazi Bencao: benefits the five viscera, unblocks the joints, descends qi when decocted and taken; expels wind-pain and induces sweating; used for traumatic bleeding; for snake or centipede bites, mash with salt and apply.
6. Bencao Tujing: boil into a decoction and pour over hands and feet to relieve wind-bi.
7. Danxi Xinfa: bake dry into powder, take with rice soup on an empty stomach to stop night sweating.
8. Bencao Mengquan: decoct and wash the eyes to remove wind-tears, reduce edema and foot swelling, descend qi, and benefit the joints.
9. Compendium of Materia Medica: treats consumptive low fever and cough, brightens the eyes, promotes hair growth.
10. Bencao Congxin: nourishes dryness, cools the blood, and stops bleeding.
11. Baicao Jing: treats intestinal wind.
12. Bencao Qiuzhen: clears the lungs and purges the stomach, cools the blood and dries dampness.
13. Bencao Qiuyuan: stops hematemesis and bleeding from traumatic wounds.
14. Shandong Chinese Materia Medica: treats sore throat, swollen painful gums, and facial edema.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 4.5–9 g; or incorporated into pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, decoct for washing or pound and apply as a poultice.
Formulas Containing Mulberry Leaf
1. For Taiyin wind-warm (mild) febrile disorder with cough, not very hot body, slight thirst: Bitter Apricot Kernel (Ku Xing Ren) 2 qian, Forsythia (Lian Qiao) 1.5 qian, Mint (Bo He) 0.8 qian, Mulberry Leaf (Sang Ye) 2.5 qian, Chrysanthemum Flower (Ju Hua) 1 qian, Platycodon Root (Jie Geng) 2 qian, Licorice (Gan Cao) 0.8 qian (raw), Reed Root (Wei Gen) 2 qian. Two cups of water, decoct to one cup, take twice daily. (Wenbing Tiaobian: Sang Ju Yin)
2. For wind-tearing eyes with lacrimation: mulberry leaves that have not fallen in the twelfth lunar month, decoct and wash warm daily, or add Mirabilite (Mang Xiao). (Binhu Ji Jian Fang)
3. For wind-heat swollen painful eyes with dryness, blurred and red vision: two Iron Fan leaves (Tie Shan Zi), pour half a cup of boiling water over them, cover and wait until warm; when the color is yellow-green like strong tea, wash the eyes and dry; after one or two hours reheat the decoction in a bowl over water and wash again. Wash 3–5 times daily. (Yang Su Yuan Chuan Xin Fang)
4. For liver-yin deficiency with blurred vision, chronic cough, skin and nail malformations, numbness: young mulberry leaves (remove stalks, wash, sun-dry, grind to powder) 1 jin, Black Sesame Seed (Hei Zhi Ma) (cleaned) 4 liang; grind the sesame and boil down to a thick syrup, mix with 1 jin white honey and cook until it forms droplets, then add mulberry leaf powder to form pills the size of paulownia seeds. Take 3 qian per dose, take with salted broth on an empty stomach and with warm wine before bed. (Yi Ji: Sang Ma Wan)
5. For hematemesis: evening-harvested mulberry leaves, lightly roasted, an unspecified amount, pounded and sieved into a fine powder. Each dose 3 qian, mixed with cooled preserved tea into a paste, add a little musk (She Xiang), at night hold in the mouth to dissolve and swallow saliva. One dose stops bleeding; follow with lung-tonifying medicines. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Du Sheng San)
6. After cholera with vomiting and diarrhea and persistent thirst: a handful of mulberry leaves, chopped, with one large cup of water, decoct to half volume, strain, and take warm as needed. (Sheng Hui Fang)
7. For pediatric thirst: mulberry leaves in any amount, coat each leaf with raw honey, tie by the petiole with thread and shade-dry, finely cut, decoct the juice and administer. (Sheng Jin Fang)
8. For rectal prolapse: three sheng of yellow-barked mulberry leaves, decoct in water and apply warm as a compress to reduce the prolapse. (Ren Zhai Zhi Zhi Fang)
9. For toxic swelling of the palm: crush fresh mulberry leaves into a pulp and apply. (Tong Xuan Lun)
10. For suppurating ulcers that will not close: frost-bitten yellow mulberry leaves, powdered and applied topically. (Ren Zhai Zhi Zhi Fang)
11. For burns and scalds: frost-bitten mulberry leaves, baked dry, burned to preserve properties, powdered finely, mixed with sesame oil and applied, or applied dry. (Yi Xue Zheng Zhuan)
12. For red swollen throat and toothache: mulberry leaf 3–5 qian, decoct and take. (Shanghai Commonly Used Chinese Herbs)
13. For dizziness of the head and eyes: mulberry leaf 3 qian, Chrysanthemum Flower (Ju Hua) 3 qian, Goji Berry (Gou Qi Zi) 3 qian, Cassia Seed (Jue Ming Zi) 2 qian. Decoction made and drunk as tea. (Shandong Chinese Materia Medica Manual)
14. For shaking-head syndrome (tongue protrusion, watery drooling, continuous head shaking): mulberry leaf 1–2 qian, decoct and take. (Jiangxi Herbal Manual)
15. For profuse whole-body sweating that will not stop: fresh mulberry leaves picked while covered in dew, squeeze dry and grind into powder. Dose 2 qian, take with rice soup on an empty stomach. (Zhong Xing Xian Fang)
16. For hiccup, vomiting, inability to retain food: mulberry leaf powder 2 liang, Pinellia Rhizome (Ban Xia) 1 liang (washed seven times to remove slipperiness). Pound finely and sieve into powder. Dose 1 qian; take with about a medium cup of vinegar-water decoction reduced to 60% volume, add a little fresh ginger juice, take warm with sediment. (Sheng Hui Fang)
17. For numbness of hands and feet with loss of sensation to pain and itch: after the frost, decoct mulberry leaves and frequently wash. (Emergency Remedies)
18. For painful breast nodules: young mulberry leaves picked fresh and ground, mixed with rice beverage (rice water), spread on paper and applied to the affected area. (Good Formulas for Women)
Dietary/Therapeutic Recipes
1. Chrysanthemum-Mulberry-Mint-Bamboo Leaf Tea
Chrysanthemum Flower (Ju Hua) 5 g, Mulberry Leaf (Sang Ye) 5 g, Mint (Bo He) 3 g, Lophatherum/Bamboo Leaf (Dan Zhu Ye) 30 g, Imperata Root (Bai Mao Gen) 30 g. Place all ingredients in a teapot, pour boiling water over and steep for 10 minutes. Drink as a tea substitute as desired.
Function: acrid-cool release of the exterior, clears and benefits the throat. Indications: wind-heat common cold, fever and headache, spontaneous sweating, nasal congestion, sore and swollen throat, cough with thick phlegm.
2. Mulberry Leaf and Fu Xiao Mai Tea
Mulberry Leaf (preferably frost-bitten) 10 g, Floating Wheat (Fu Xiao Mai) 30 g. Rub the mulberry leaves to break them up and place in a large teacup. Boil the Fu Xiao Mai in a pot and strain to obtain the juice; use the Fu Xiao Mai juice to infuse the mulberry leaves, cover and steep for 10 minutes. Drink as a tea frequently.
Function: clears heat and stops sweating. Indications: low-grade fever and night sweats in pulmonary tuberculosis.
3. Mulberry-Chrysanthemum-Cicada Slough Decoction
Mulberry Leaf 10 g, Chrysanthemum Flower (Ju Hua) 10 g, Cicada Slough (Chan Yi) 6 g, white sugar as needed. Select and clean the mulberry leaves and chrysanthemum, remove the head and feet of the cicada slough, place all in a pot with appropriate water, bring to a boil over high heat then simmer for 15 minutes, strain and add sugar to taste. Drink regularly.
Function: disperse wind and clear heat, calm convulsions. Indications: pediatric convulsions with fever, headache, cough, and nasal discharge.
4. Safflower-Mulberry-Chrysanthemum Decoction
Safflower (Hong Hua) 3 g, Mulberry Leaf (Sang Ye) 10 g, Chrysanthemum Flower (Ju Hua) 10 g. Place the mulberry leaf, chrysanthemum and safflower in a cup and pour boiling water over, cover and steep briefly. First use to fumigate the affected eye, then drink when warm. Twice daily for 3 days.
Function: disperse heat, reduce swelling, relieve pain and brighten the eyes. Indications: acute infectious conjunctivitis.
5. Mulberry-Mint-Chrysanthemum-Loquat Leaf Tea
Ingredients: Mulberry Leaf 500 g, Chrysanthemum Flower 250 g, Loquat Leaf (Pi Pa Ye) 250 g, Mint (Bo He) 250 g.
Preparation: coarsely powder the above herbs and place in clean gauze bags, each bag 10–15 g. Take one bag, place in a teacup and pour boiling water over, cover and steep for 10 minutes. Drink as a tea frequently.
Function: dispel wind and clear heat, release the exterior and clear the lungs. Indication: early wind-heat common cold.

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%BE%8C%E6%B4%BB
Name
Incised Notopterygium
Qiangqing (Qiangqing), Protector-of-Qiang Envoy (Huqiang Shizhe), Hu King Envoy (Hu Wang Shizhe), Qianghua (Qianghua), Wind-Dispelling Envoy (Tuifeng Shizhe), Black Medicine (He Yao)

Cultivation and Processing of Incised Notopterygium (Qianghuo)
Source
The rhizome and root of plants of the Apiaceae family: Notopterygium incisum (Qianghuo) or Notopterygium forbesii (broad-leaved Qianghuo). Cultivated plants are dug 3 to 4 years after planting in the autumn after leaning out the seedlings and before sprouting in early spring by cutting off the aboveground parts, excavating the rhizomes, shaking off mud and sand, chopping off the leaf bases, removing the fine roots, cutting into short sections 10 to 13 cm long, and sun-drying or oven-drying.
Properties and Taste
Pungent and bitter, warm in nature.
Appearance
(1) Qianghuo
The rhizome is cylindrical, slightly curved, 4 to 13 cm long, 0.6 to 2.5 cm in diameter. The top has stem scars. The surface is brownish to dark brown, with yellow where the peel has flaked off. Internodes are shortened and form tightly raised rings, resembling silkworms (commonly called Can Qiang); or the nodes are elongated, bamboo-joint like (commonly called Zhujie Qiang). On the nodes there are many punctate or nodular root scars and broken scale remnants. The body is light, brittle, and breaks easily. The fracture surface is uneven with many fissures; the periderm is yellow-brown to dark brown, oily, with brown oil spots; the wood is yellow-white with distinct rays; the pith is yellow to yellow-brown. Aromatic odor, slightly bitter and pungent taste.
(2) Broad-leaved Qianghuo
Rhizomes and roots cylindrical; the top has remnants of stem and leaf sheaths; the root is conical with longitudinal wrinkles and lenticels; the surface is brownish, with denser annular rings near the rhizome, 8 to 15 cm long, 1 to 3 cm in diameter (commonly called Tiao Qiang). Some rhizomes are large and irregularly nodular with several stem bases at the top and finer roots (commonly called Da Tou Qiang). Texture is loose and brittle, breaks easily. The fracture surface is relatively flat; periderm light brown; wood yellow-white. Odor is milder.
The best quality is from thick rhizomes with transverse nodes like silkworm-segments, brown surface, dense fracture texture, many cinnabar-like oil points, and strong aroma.
Effects of Qianghuo
Efficacy
The rhizome and root of plants of the Apiaceae family: Notopterygium incisum (Qianghuo) or Notopterygium forbesii (broad-leaved Qianghuo).
Used for impotence and spermatorrhea, enuresis and frequent urination, cold pain in the lower back and knees, wheezing due to kidney deficiency, early morning diarrhea; externally for vitiligo and alopecia areata. Releases the exterior and disperses cold, expels wind and overcomes dampness, relieves pain.
Meridians Entered
Enters the Bladder meridian; the Kidney meridian.
Main Indications
Disperses exterior cold, expels wind-dampness, and benefits the joints. Treats wind-cold common cold, headache without sweating, wind-cold-damp bi painful obstruction, stiff neck with contracted sinews, soreness and aching of bones and joints, wind-water edema, boils and sores with toxic swelling. Used for impotence and spermatorrhea, enuresis and frequent urination, cold pain in the lower back and knees, wheezing due to kidney deficiency, early morning diarrhea; externally treats vitiligo and alopecia areata.
1. For externally-contracted wind-cold with aversion to cold, fever, headache, body aches and other symptoms. This herb has a strong dispersing effect on wind-cold and analgesic effect. Often used with Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Angelica dahurica root (Baizhi), Asarum (Xixin), etc., such as in Nine-Ingredient Qianghuo Decoction (Jiuwei Qianghuo Tang).
2. For limb and joint pain, shoulder and back soreness due to invasion of wind-cold-dampness, especially suitable for upper-body pain. This herb expels wind and overcomes dampness, disperses cold and relieves pain. Often used with Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), as in Quanbi Decoction (Juanbi Tang).
① From Yaoxing Lun: Treats pernicious wind, loss of voice and muteness, many itchings and blood scaly eruptions, paralysis of hands and feet, facial deviation, obstinate bi pain all over the body.
② From Rihuazi Bencao: Treats all wind disorders and qi disorders, sinew and bone contracture, emaciation of limbs, vertigo, red painful eyes and submerged-fluid disorders, overexertion injuries, deficiency and cold qi, soreness and pain of bones and joints, and unblocks and benefits the five zang.
③ From Zhenzhu Nang: For Taiyang meridian headache, removes various bone and joint pains, also warms the gallbladder.
④ From Pinhui Jingyao: Main for pain all over the body and in all joints, exterior eight-wind pernicious influences, removes new and old wind-dampness, discharges rotten flesh abscesses and sores.
⑤ From Bencao Beiyao: Drains liver qi, searches liver wind, treats wind-damp complex, Taiyang meridian headache, diseases of the Governing Vessel, stiff spine and collapse, rigid or flexible spasms, windstroke with muteness, vertigo and red painful eyes.
⑥ From Huiyue Yijing: Treats evil constriction and aversion to cold, robust fever without sweat.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 3 to 10 g; or used in pills and powders.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated for bi pain due to blood deficiency.
Formulas Containing Qianghuo
① For common cold with fever and tonsillitis: Qianghuo (Qianghuo) four to five qian, Isatis root (Banlangen), Dandelion (Pugongying) each one liang. Decoction, one dose per day, take in two divided doses. (Affiliated Longhua Hospital, Shanghai College of Traditional Chinese Medicine)
② For releasing and treating cold disease: Qianghuo one and a half liang, Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng) one and a half liang, Atractylodes rhizome (Cangzhu) one and a half liang, Asarum (Xixin) five fen, Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong) one liang, Angelica dahurica root (Baizhi) one liang, Rehmannia root raw (Sheng Dihuang) one liang, Baical skullcap root (Huangqin) one liang, Licorice root (Gancao) one liang. Grind the above into powder, decoct with water and take. If there is urgent sweating, take with hot gruel; if sweating is slow, take warm but not with soup. (From Cishi Nanzhi: Nine-Ingredient Qianghuo Decoction)
③ For relieving acute dental-cold: Qianghuo, Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Atractylodes rhizome (Cangzhu), Asarum (Xixin), Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong), Angelica dahurica root (Baizhi), Rehmannia root raw (Sheng Dihuang), Baical skullcap root (Huangqin), Licorice root (Gancao). Decoction; for rapid sweating take with hot gruel, for slow sweating take warm and not with soup. (Zhang Yuansu Nine-Ingredient Qianghuo Decoction)
④ For Taiyang meridian headache: Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng) 2 fen, Qianghuo 3 fen, Adzuki beans (Hongdou, Chixiaodou) two pieces. Grind to powder and insert into the nose. (From Yuji Weiyi)
⑤ For invading cold affecting the head causing toothache, cold extremities and coldness of mouth and nose: Qianghuo one qian, Prepared aconite (Fuzi) and Dried ginger (Ganjiang) each five fen, honey-fried Licorice root (Gancao) eight fen. Decoction. (From Yixue Xinwu: Qianghuo Fuzi Decoction)
⑥ For wind-damp complex causing body pain, pulling pain preventing flexion and extension, or slight swelling and numbness of the body: Qianghuo (remove leaf bases), Prepared aconite (Pao Fuzi, peeled and cored), Atractylodes rhizome (Baizhu), Licorice root (Gancao, honey-fried) in equal parts. Each dose four qian, water one and a half cup, fresh ginger five slices, boil down to seven tenths, strain, take warm at any time. (From Jisheng Fang: Qiang-Fuzi Decoction)
⑦ For shoulder and back pain preventing turning the head, spinal pain and stiff neck, waist like broken, neck as if pulled out: Qianghuo and Angelica pubescens root (Duhuo) each one qian, Ligusticum (Gaoben), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Licorice root (Gancao, honey-fried), Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong) each five fen, Vitex seed (Manjingzi) three fen. Make one dose, two cups water, reduce to one cup, strain, take very warm on an empty stomach before meals. (From Nei Wai Shang Bian: Qianghuo Victory Dampness Decoction)
⑧ For pediatric common cold: Qianghuo one qian, Ginseng (Renshen) one qian, Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng) one qian, Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong) one qian. Grind as one dose, fresh ginger three slices, Mint (Bohe) seven leaves, one cup water, reduce to seven tenths, take at any time. (From Yingtong Baiwen: Qianghuo Decoction for Children)
⑨ For postpartum cold disease: Qianghuo, Cyperus (Xiangfu), Perilla leaf (Zisuye) each one qian five fen, Angelica sinensis root (Danggui) one qian, White peony root (Baishao), Bupleurum root (Chaihu), Aged tangerine peel (Chenpi) each one qian two fen. Add three green onion whites, decoct and take at any time. (From Dantai Yu'an: Qiang-Su Drink)
⑩ For unbearable brow-bone pain: honey-fried Licorice root (use raw in summer), Qianghuo and Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng) each three qian, wine Baical skullcap root (Huangqin) one qian (omit Huangqin in winter; if the pain is aggravated by eating and heat, double this herb). Grind and mix; each dose five qian, two cups water, reduce to one cup, strain, take after meals. (From Lanshi Mancang: Xuanqi Decoction)
⑾ For headache with dizziness and faintness on rising: Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong), Qianghuo, Vitex seed (Manjingzi), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Angelica dahurica root (Baizhi), Asarum (Xixin), Ligusticum (Gaoben), Gypsum (Shigao) in equal parts. Decoction. (From Yixue Qimeng: Chuanxiong-Qianghuo Powder)
⑿ For stagnation of Taiyang qi in the hands causing shoulder and back pain preventing turning the head; stagnation in the foot Taiyang causing spinal pain and stiff neck, waist like broken, neck as if pulled out: Qianghuo and Angelica pubescens root (Duhuo) each one qian, Ligusticum (Gaoben), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Licorice root (Gancao, honey-fried), Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong) each five fen, Vitex seed (Manjingzi) three fen. Prepare one dose with two cups water, reduce to one cup, strain, take very warm on an empty stomach before meals. (From Nei Wai Shang Bianhuo Lun: Qianghuo Victory Dampness Decoction)
⒀ For wind-damp complex with body soreness, neck and arm heaviness, difficulty moving, cold numbness of hands and feet, heavy knees and legs, weak tendons and vessels: Angelica sinensis root (Danggui, soak in wine and remove earth, soak overnight), Qianghuo (remove leaf bases), Curcuma (Jianghuang), White peony root (Baishao), Astragalus (Huangqi, honey-fried), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng, remove leaf bases) each one liang and a half, Licorice root (Gancao, honey-fried) half liang. Grind and mix; each dose half liang, two cups water, fresh ginger five slices, boil to one cup, strain, warm take at any time. (From Yang Family Collection: Juanbi Decoction)
⒁ For dampness wandering into the four limbs with swollen painful joints: Qianghuo and Cimicifuga (Shengma) each one qian, Angelica pubescens root (Duhuo) seven fen, Atractylodes rhizome (Cangzhu), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng, remove leaf bases), Clematis root (Weilingxian, remove leaf bases), Atractylodes macrocephala rhizome (Baizhu), Angelica sinensis root (Danggui), Poria (Fuling, peeled), Alisma rhizome (Zexie) each half qian. Grind and make one dose, two cups water, reduce to one cup, strain, warm take one dose before meals and one after meals. (From Weisheng Baojian: Da Qianghuo Decoction)
⒂ For wind-cold-damp lingering in the muscles causing weak, numb hands and feet, or qi-blood disharmony with numb obstruction: Sliced Curcuma (cleaned of dirt), Qianghuo, Atractylodes macrocephala rhizome (Baizhu), Stephania root (Fangji) each one liang, Licorice root (Gancao, lightly honey-fried) half liang. Each dose four qian, water one and a half cup, add fresh ginger ten slices, boil to eight tenths, strain. If disease is in the upper body take after meals; if in the lower body take before meals. (From Ju Fang: Wu Bi Decoction)
⒃ For tinea with swelling and pain of the feet: Qianghuo one and a half qian, Angelica sinensis body (Danggui shen) one qian, Bitter orange (Zhishi) and Rhubarb (Dahuang) each five fen. Grind into pieces the size of sesame beans, make one dose, two and a half large cups water, reduce to one cup, strain, take warm on an empty stomach; induce one liang of diarrhea, pain stops. (From Yixue Faming: Yiqi Exorcise Dampness Decoction)
⒄ For watery edema: Qianghuo and Radish seed (Laifuzi, stir-fried) each one liang. Grind to powder, take with wine. (From Shiyi De Xiao Fang: Chuanhuo Powder)
⒅ For throat obstruction and trismus: Qianghuo three liang (finely grated), Burdock seed (Niubangzi) one liang (pounded to powder). First decoct the Qianghuo in three large cups of water and take one and a half large cups, strain. Add one fen of alum (white vitriol), mix evenly; each dose one small cup, add two qian of burdock powder to the decoction. When administering, use a wooden spatula to pry open the mouth and pour in; success is when the patient vomits. (From Shenghui Fang)
⒆ For postpartum wind-stroke with trismus, obstinate numbness of the limbs, or limbs like bowstrings: Qianghuo and Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng) each three liang, soybeans one sheng (stir-fry until skins crack). Soak the two herbs in wine, then after a night stir in the fried beans hot into the wine, mix, seal for one day, then steep and cook down in a jar for a long time; take eight he (measures), cover and extract the juice quickly; administer by bean dribbling; take Qianghuo and Fangfeng to good effect. (From Jingxiao Chanbao)
⒇ For tetanus after taking Zuo Long Pill or after purgation with continued convulsions: Qianghuo, Angelica pubescens root (Duhuo), Saposhnikovia root (Fangfeng), Sanguisorba root (Diyu) each one liang. Grind and make one dose; each dose five qian, water one and a half cup, reduce to one cup, strain, take warm. If fever add Baical skullcap root (Huangqin); if excess saliva add Pinellia (Banxia). (From Baoming Ji: Qianghuo Decoction)
(21) For liver constraint with fullness, red and dim eyes, continual hot tears, tight and painful tendons, shoulder and back fatigue, and dizziness with stiff and painful neck: Qianghuo, Chrysanthemum (Juhua), Vitex seed (Manjingzi), Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong) each one fen. Grind to fine powder; each dose two qian, one medium cup of water, add Sour Jujube seed (Suanzaoren) and Burdock seed (Niubangzi) each fifty grains, ground, decoct to seven tenths, strain, take at any time. (From Jifeng Puji Fang: Qianghuo Powder)
(22) For wind-heat toxin forming scrofula and lymph node swellings: Qianghuo (remove leaf bases) one and a half liang, Stiff silkworm (Jiangcan, stir-fried) one liang. Pound the two into a powder. Each morning on an empty stomach take four qian with honey-wine, repeat at night. (From Shengji Zonglu: Internal-Reducing Qianghuo Powder)
(23) For purulent otorrhea: Typhonium rhizome (Baifuzi, prepared), Qianghuo (remove leaf bases) each one liang. Grind to fine powder. Take one pig or sheep kidney, cut open, put half a qian of the powder into each kidney, do not add salt, wrap in damp paper and roast until cooked, at dawn take warm and swallow, then continue with porridge to suppress. (From Shengji Zonglu: Two-Sage Powder)
(25) Two-Huo Chuanxiong Wine: Qianghuo 15 g, Angelica pubescens root (Duhuo) 15 g, Ligusticum chuanxiong rhizome (Chuanxiong) 20 g, black beans 30 g, hemp seed (Huomaren) 30 g, rice wine 200 ml. Precisely process the above, crush to powder, place in a clean bottle, add wine to soak, seal for 21 days, then open and filter to remove residue and retain the infusion.
Take twice daily, morning and evening, 10 to 25 ml each time.
Efficacy: expels wind, promotes blood circulation, relieves spasms. For early-stage stroke with neck and nape rigidity, shoulder and back soreness, limb stiffness, occasional aversion to wind and fever.
