Open-mouthed Arrow (Kai Kou Jian)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%A3%E7%AE%AD
Bamboo-root Seven (Zhu gen qi)
Cultivation and Processing of Arisaema (Kai kou jian)
Source
The rhizomes of Arisaema (Kai kou jian) and Sword-leaf Arisaema (Jian ye kai kou jian) of the Liliaceae family. Can be harvested year-round; remove leaves and fibrous roots, wash clean, use fresh or slice and sun-dry.
Morphology
1. Arisaema (Kai kou jian) is a perennial herb. Rhizome elongate-cylindrical, diameter 1–1.5 cm, many-noded, green to yellow. Leaves basal, 4–8; leaf blades obovate-lanceolate, linear-lanceolate or strap-shaped, 15–65 cm long, 1.5–9.5 cm wide, apex gradually acuminate, base gradually narrowed; two cataphylls. Spike-like inflorescence lateral, erect, densely many-flowered, 2.5–9 cm long; bracts ovate-lanceolate to subulate, with several sterile bracts clustered at the inflorescence apex; perianth short campanulate, 5–7 mm long; segments 6, ovate, 3–5 mm long, 2–4 mm wide, yellow or yellow-green, fleshy; stamens 6, filaments dilated at the base, sometimes fused with each other, free above, incurved, anthers ovoid; ovary globose, 3-loculed, style indistinct, stigma blunt triangular, apex 3-cleft. Berry globose, 8–10 mm in diameter, purple-red when ripe, with 1–3 seeds. Flowering April–June, fruiting September–November.
2. Sword-leaf Arisaema (Jian ye kai kou jian) is a perennial herb. Rhizome cylindrical, brown or green, stems up to 10 cm long, many-noded. Leaves numerous, distinctly two-ranked, strap-shaped, 35–50 cm long, 5–12 mm wide, apex long-acuminate, base enlarged and clasping the stem, margins slightly revolute when dry. Spike-like inflorescence lateral, densely many-flowered, 4–5.5 cm long; bracts subulate or triangular-subulate, longer than the flowers, with several sterile bracts clustered at the inflorescence apex; perianth simple campanulate, 5–5.5 mm long; segments 6, ovate, spreading, 2–2.5 mm long, 1.5–2 mm wide, fleshy, brown or green, margins white-membranous and eroded-looking; stamens 6, filaments thick, dilated and wrinkled at the base, adnate to the perianth tube, free above, shorter than the anthers, anthers ovoid; ovary ovoid, 3-loculed, style indistinct, stigma blunt triangular, apex 3-cleft. Berries 5–8 mm in diameter, red-black, with 1–3 seeds. Flowering in June, fruiting in October.
Ecological Habitat
1. Arisaema (Kai kou jian) grows in shaded moist places under forests, by streams, or beside roads.
2. Sword-leaf Arisaema (Jian ye kai kou jian) grows under forests at altitudes of 1100–3200 m.
Distribution
1. Arisaema (Kai kou jian) is distributed in central and southern China and in Shaanxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Sichuan, Yunnan, etc.
2. Sword-leaf Arisaema (Jian ye kai kou jian) is distributed in Yunnan.
Properties and Taste
Bitter; pungent; cold; toxic
Characteristics
The rhizome of Arisaema (Kai kou jian) is flattened-cylindrical, slightly twisted, 10–15 cm long, about 1 cm in diameter. Nodes distinct, slightly swollen, with buds and membranous scale-like leaves at the nodes; internodes short. Surface yellow-brown to yellow-green, wrinkled. Transverse section pale yellow-white, fine granular. Odor absent, taste bitter and astringent.
Effects of Arisaema (Kai kou jian)
Efficacy
The rhizomes of Arisaema (Kai kou jian) and Sword-leaf Arisaema (Jian ye kai kou jian) of the Liliaceae family. Used for diphtheria, throat swelling and pain, rheumatic painful obstruction, traumatic injuries from falls and blows, stomach pain, carbuncles and ulcers, poisonous snakebites, and rabid dog bites.
Main Indications
Clears heat and detoxifies, dispels wind and eliminates dampness, disperses stasis and relieves pain. Indicated chiefly for diphtheria, throat swelling and pain, rheumatic pain, traumatic injuries from falls and blows, stomach pain, carbuncles and ulcers, poisonous snakebites, and rabid dog bites.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 1.5–3 g; powdered, 0.6–0.9 g.
External use: appropriate amount, pounded and applied.
Precautions
Contraindicated in pregnancy.
Notes
This substance is toxic; there have been reports of poisoning when up to 3 qian were used, therefore the dosage must not be excessive. In poisoning, symptoms such as headache, dizziness, nausea and vomiting may be observed; stop the medicine immediately and provide timely rescue.

Ox-ear Rhubarb (Niu Er Da Huang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%89%9B%E8%80%B3%E5%A4%A7%E9%BB%84
Cultivation and Processing of Curly Dock (Niu'er Dahuang)
Source
From the root of the Polygonaceae plant Curly Dock (Rumex crispus). The roots are harvested in April–May, washed clean, sun-dried or used fresh.
Morphology
Perennial herb, 50–100 cm tall. Roots are thick, yellow, with a sour taste. Stems erect, usually unbranched, with shallow grooves. Leaves alternate; stipule sheaths membranous, tubular, often rupturing; leaf blades lanceolate or narrowly oblong-lanceolate, 12–18 cm long, 2–4.5 cm wide, apex short-acuminate, base gradually narrowed, margins with wavy folds, glabrous on both surfaces. Many flowers cluster in leaf axils or form short racemes, composing a narrow, elongated panicle; perianth segments 6 in 2 whorls, persistent; stamens 6; styles 3, brush-like. Achenes trigonous with sharp ridges, about 2 mm long, brown and shiny. Flowering and fruiting period June–August.
Habitat and Distribution
Ecological environment: grows in wet places by ditches, riverbanks and beside marshy meadows.
Distribution: occurs in Northeast China, North China and in Shaanxi, Gansu, Qinghai, Fujian, Taiwan, Guangxi, Guizhou and other regions.
Taste and Nature
Bitter; cold in nature
Characteristics
Roots are irregularly conical and cylindrical, 10–20 cm long, up to 2.5 cm thick, solitary or with several branches at the middle. The root crown bears a dried stem base surrounded by many brown, flattened dried leaf bases. Surface brown to dark brown with irregular longitudinal wrinkles and many nearly round rootlet scars. Hard texture; fracture yellow-brown and fibrous.
Slight odor, bitter taste.
Pharmacological Actions
1. Antitussive, expectorant and antiasthmatic effects
Decoctions of the root and decoctions after deproteinization, administered orally to mice, showed significant antitussive effects (ammonia aerosol cough model), although mice exhibited abdominal distension, diarrhea and piloerection. Emodin and chrysophanol isolated from the root both showed marked antitussive effects, with emodin stronger than chrysophanol; total anthraquinones had mild antitussive effect, while rhein showed no antitussive effect. Decoctions and deproteinized decoctions had expectorant effects (phenol red method in mice), while total anthraquinones showed no obvious effect. Total anthraquinones given orally to guinea pigs produced a marked antiasthmatic effect (histamine aerosol method), but emodin, rhein and chrysophanol were ineffective. A mixture of chrysophanol with the residue remaining after extraction of the above components produced an antiasthmatic effect in guinea pigs.
2. Antibacterial effects
Rhein, emodin and chrysophanol isolated from the root exhibited varying degrees of inhibition in vitro against Group A streptococcus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis. Whole-plant extracts inhibited Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. A root tincture showed significant inhibitory activity against Microsporum canis on Sabouraud agar, with a minimum effective concentration of 1.56–3.12%.
3. Antitumor effects
Six days after inoculation of mice thigh muscle with Sarcoma-37, a single subcutaneous injection of an alcoholic extract of Rumex crispus root produced observable tumor damage at 6–48 hours after dosing; the acidic extract may be more potent.
4. Other effects
The roots and rhizomes contain emodin and other anthraquinone derivatives, hence a laxative effect; they also contain a fairly high tannin content (3.62–6.42%), hence an astringent action; roots and rhizomes also contain vitamin B1 (up to 10.26 µg/g), and can be used as a stomachic and tonic. They also contain an irritant substance named rumicin (molecular formula C14H10O4), which acts as a rubefacient and dispersant and can kill skin parasites; however it can cause dermatitis and gastrointestinal disturbances in animals (sheep, horses).
Therapeutic Effects of Curly Dock (Niu'er Dahuang)
Actions
From the root of the Polygonaceae plant Curly Dock (Rumex crispus). Primarily treats acute and chronic hepatitis, enteritis, dysentery, chronic bronchitis, hematemesis, epistaxis, hematochezia, metrorrhagia, heat-bound constipation, carbuncles and toxic swellings, scabies, and alopecia.
Channels Entered
Heart; Liver; Large Intestine
Indications
Clears heat and detoxifies, cools the blood and stops bleeding, purges and kills parasites. Indicated for acute and chronic hepatitis, enteritis, dysentery, chronic bronchitis, hematemesis, epistaxis, hematochezia, metrorrhagia, heat-bound constipation, carbuncles and toxic swellings, scabies, and alopecia.
Dosage and Administration
Internal: decoction, 10–15 g.
External: appropriate amount, pounded and applied; or ground to powder and applied topically.
Precautions and Contraindications
Sichuan Materia Medica: contraindicated in diarrhea due to spleen deficiency.
Prescriptions Using Curly Dock (Niu'er Dahuang)
1) For scabies: 4 liang Curly Dock (Niu'er Dahuang), 2 liang Laojunxu; stew with pork femur and take. (Chongchuang Materia Medica)
2) For hematemesis: fresh Curly Dock (Niu'er Dahuang), stew with shakou meat and take. (Chongqing Materia Medica)
Remarks by Various Sources
1. Caomu Bianfang: invigorates blood, replenishes essence, strengthens vigor. Can release the exterior. Pound into a paste and mix with thick indigo vat water to apply for scabies, tinea and alopecia.
2. Sichuan Materia Medica: detoxifies, clears heat, heals sores and tinea. Treats dry, hard stools.
3. Chongqing Materia Medica: clears fire, detoxifies, clears blood-heat, promotes bowel movement. Treats conditions of hematemesis. Stir-frying with wine can regulate qi and restrain bleeding, treating excessive uterine bleeding.
4. Mindong Materia Medica: eliminates heat, kills parasites, drains pus and expels toxins. Treats patchy alopecia, tinea, carbuncles and boils.
5. Qiqihar Chinese Herbal Medicine: treats hemorrhagic purpura, thrombocytopenia and internal bleeding.
6. Plateau Herbal Treatment Manual: clears heat and cools the blood, moistens the intestines and relieves constipation. Treats acute hepatitis, amenorrhea with abdominal distention, and unspecified toxic swellings.
7. Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia-Qinghai Herbal Selection: clears heat and detoxifies, reduces inflammation and swelling, stops bleeding.

Perilla leaf (Zi Su Ye)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%B4%AB%E8%8B%8F%E5%8F%B6
Name
Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye)
Red Perilla Leaf (Chi Su Ye), Fragrant Perilla Leaf (Xiang Su Ye), Red Perilla Leaf (Hong Su Ye), Cinnamon Perilla Leaf (Gui Su Ye), Perilla Leaf (Su Ye)
Red Perilla Leaf (Chi Su Ye)
Fragrant Perilla Leaf (Xiang Su Ye)
Red Perilla Leaf (Hong Su Ye)
Cinnamon Perilla Leaf (Gui Su Ye)
Perilla Leaf (Su Ye)
Perilla (Zi Su)
Cultivation and Preparation of Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye)
Source
This product is the dried leaves (or with young shoots) of the Lamiaceae plant Perilla frutescens (L.) Britt. Harvest when branches and leaves are luxuriant in summer, remove impurities, and sun-dry.
Property and Taste
Pungent, warm.
Processing
Remove impurities and old stems; or spray with clean water, chop, and dry.
Character
The leaves of this product are often wrinkled, rolled, or broken; intact leaves when flattened are ovate, 4–11 cm long and 2.5–9 cm wide. Apex long-acuminate or acute, base rounded or broadly cuneate, margin with rounded serrations. Both surfaces purple or upper surface green and lower surface purple, sparsely covered with gray-white hairs; lower surface has numerous depressed glandular scales. Petiole 2–7 cm long, purple or purplish green. Texture brittle. If with young shoots, branch diameter 2–5 mm, purplish green, with pith in the center of the cross section. Fragrant aroma, taste slightly pungent.
Effects of Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye)
Efficacy
This product is the dried leaves (or with young shoots) of Perilla of the Lamiaceae family.
Main Indications: wind-cold common cold, aversion to cold with fever, cough, wheeze, chest and abdominal distention and fullness, restless fetal movement. Also able to relieve fish and crab poisoning.
Channels Entered
Enters the Lung Channel (Fei Jing), and Spleen Channel (Pi Jing).
Indications
Used for wind-cold common cold with fever and aversion to cold, headache and nasal congestion, accompanied by cough or chest oppression. This product can disperse exterior cold and open and promote Lung qi; it can be used together with Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang). If cough is present, it is often paired with Apricot Kernel (Xing Ren) and Peucedanum (Qian Hu), as in Apricot-Perilla Powder (Xing Su San); if there is qi stagnation with chest oppression, it is often combined with Nutgrass (Xiang Fu) and Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi), as in Su San.
Used for Spleen and Stomach qi stagnation with chest fullness and vomiting. This product moves qi, widens the middle, harmonizes the stomach and stops vomiting. For cold-dominant cases, it is often used with Agastache (Huo Xiang); for heat-dominant cases, it may be used with Coptis (Huang Lian). For qi stagnation with phlegm accumulation, it is often combined with Pinellia (Ban Xia) and Magnolia Bark (Hou Po).
Used for morning sickness in pregnancy with chest and abdominal fullness; often combined with Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi) and Amomum (Sha Ren) to strengthen antiemetic and fetal-stabilizing effects.
Used for abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea caused by eating fish or crab; used alone or with Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) and Angelica Dahurica (Bai Zhi) decocted and taken.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decocted, 5–10 g.
External use: appropriate amount, pounded and applied, ground into powder and mixed in, or decocted for washing.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated in warm diseases and those with deficient qi.
1. "Ben Cao Jing Shu": If the disease belongs to yin deficiency and manifests as fever from deficiency or aversion to cold and headache, use with caution or do not administer, because the disease requires contraction and tonification. Also not suitable when fire rising causes vomiting.
2. "Ben Cao Tong Xuan": Prolonged use can deplete true qi.
Formulas Using Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye)
1) For wind-cold with fever: Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye), Saposhnikovia (Fangfeng), Ligusticum chuanxiong (Chuanxiong) each 1 qian 5 fen, Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi) 1 qian, Licorice (Gan Cao) 6 fen. Add two slices of Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) and decoct. (From Bu Zhi Yi Bi Yao: Su Ye Tang)
2) For sudden cold-induced shortness of breath: Dried Perilla Leaf (gan Su Ye) 3 liang, Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi) 4 liang, wine 4 sheng, boil down to 1.5 sheng, divide into two doses and take. (From Bu Que Zhou Hou Fang)
3) For cough with dyspnea: Perilla stem and leaves (chopped) 1 liang, Ginseng (Ren Shen) 0.5 liang. Coarsely pound and sift the two herbs; each dose 3 qian, water one cup, decoct to 70%, remove dregs, take warm, twice daily. (From Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Zi Su Tang)
4) For persistent hiccups after cold damage: Red Perilla (Chi Su) a handful, water 3 sheng, boil down to 2 sheng, sip slowly. (From Bu Que Zhou Hou Fang)
5) For disharmony of fetal qi with distention and pain in the upper abdomen called "suspended fetus": Areca Peel (Da Fu Pi), Ligusticum chuanxiong (Chuanxiong), White Peony (Bai Shao), Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi, peel removed), Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye), Angelica sinensis (Dang Gui, stalk removed and wine-soaked) each 1 liang; Ginseng (Ren Shen) and Licorice (Gan Cao, honey-fried) each 0.5 liang. Finely slice, each dose 4 qian, water 1.5 cups, add 5 slices Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang), scallion white 7 cun, decoct to 70%, take warm on empty stomach. (From Ji Sheng Fang: Zi Su Yin)
6) For breast abscess swelling and pain: frequently drink Perilla decoction and also pound and apply as a poultice. (From Hai Shang Xian Fang)
7) For bleeding from wounds: tender Perilla Leaves (young), Mulberry Leaves (Sang Ye), pound together and apply as a plaster. (From Yong Lei Qian Fang)
8) For contusions and bruises: pound Perilla and apply; wounds will close. (From Tan Ye Weng Shi Yan Fang)
9) For snake and poisonous reptile bites: drink crushed Perilla Leaf juice. (From Qian Jin Fang)
10) For crab poisoning: boil Perilla and drink the juice. (From Jin Kui Yao Lue)
11) For cold diarrhea: Perilla Leaf 15 g, decoct with water and add 6 g brown sugar and take.
12) To relieve poisoning from fish or soft-shelled turtle: Perilla Leaf 60 g, decoct to a concentrated decoction and drink as tea, or mix with 10 drops of ginger juice and take.
13) For uterine prolapse: Perilla Leaf 60 g, decoct and fumigate and wash.
14) For cough with copious phlegm, moistening the Lung: Perilla (Zi Su), Fritillaria (Chuan Bei Mu), Coltsfoot Flower (Kuan Dong Hua), Han Fangji (Han Fang Ji) each one fen. Grind into fine powder; each dose 1 qian, water one teacup, decoct to 70%, take warm. (From Bo Ji Fang: Zi Su Yin)
15) For vomiting of milk: Perilla, Licorice (Gan Cao), Talc (Hua Shi) in equal parts, decoct and take. (From Shen Zhai Yi Shu)
16) For globus hystericus with vomiting and poor appetite: Perilla Leaf 2 liang, white honey and ginger juice each 5 fen, mix evenly, simmer gently until boiling; each dose half a spoon, take on empty stomach in small sips. (From Shou Shi Qing Bian: Su Mi Jian)
17) For pregnant women with cold damage; primarily clear heat and harmonize the fetus; treat according to symptoms appearing in the six channels and do not treat as ordinary disease to avoid harming the fetus; use the following formula as principal: Perilla (Zi Su), Coptis (Huang Qin, stir-fried with wine), Atractylodes (Bai Zhu, earth-fried) each 1 qian 5 fen, Licorice (Gan Cao) 1 qian, scallion and ginger as guides. (From Yi Fang Yi Pan Zhu: Four-Ingredient Perilla Fetus-Harmonizing Decoction)
18) For beriberi with chaotic heart, delirium, vomiting and inability to ingest: Perilla stem and leaves 1 liang 5 qian, Evodia (Wu Zhu Yu, soaked and stir-fried till dry) and Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi, soaked to remove the white pith and roasted) each 1 fen. Pound and sift; each dose 3 qian, water one cup, decoct to 70%, add one he of young boy urine, take warm. (From Pu Ji Fang: Zi Su Tang)
19) For beriberi with persistent wheeze regardless of cold or heat: Perilla Leaf 1 liang 5 qian (chopped), White Poria (Fu Ling, peel removed) 1 liang, Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi, soaked to remove white, roasted) 10 liang. Grind into powder; each dose 1 qian, water one cup, add half a fen of Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) crushed, decoct to 70%, remove dregs, take warm on empty stomach, twice daily, morning and evening. (From Pu Ji Fang: Zi Su Tang)
20) For edema due to water-dampness with scanty, reddish urine: Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi, white pith removed) 1 liang, Radix Stephaniae (Fang Ji), Akebia (Mu Tong), Perilla Leaf each 5 qian. Grind into powder; each dose 2 qian, add three slices ginger, decoct in water and take before meals. (From Chi Shui Xuan Zhu: Xiang Su San)
21) For scrotal sores and ulceration with fragile skin and a tendency for the scrotum to sag, called fragility of the scrotum due to damp-heat: use Perilla Leaf powder; if wet mix with it, if dry mix with clarified oil and apply. (From Pian Yu Xin Shu)
22) For ulcerative sores and scabies: grind large Perilla leaves into fine powder and apply. (From Pu Ji Fang)
23) For chest fullness and qi stagnation after cold damage with poor appetite: Perilla stem (chopped) 1 liang, Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi, soaked to remove white, roasted) 2 liang, Red Poria (Chi Fu Ling, peel removed) 1 liang 5 qian, Areca Peel (Da Fu Pi, chopped), Inula Flower (Xuan Fu Hua) each 1 liang, Pinellia (Ban Xia, washed seven times and roasted) 0.5 liang. Finely cut to the size of broad beans. Each dose 5 qian, water 1.5 cups, add 1 fen fresh ginger (crushed) and 3 pieces of jujube (broken), decoct to 70%, remove dregs, take warm. (From Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Su Ju Tang)
24) For aftercare following cold damage or warm disease when early rising and excessive eating cause relapse: Perilla stem and leaves (chopped) 1 liang, Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang, sliced) 0.5 liang, fermented soybean paste 1–2 he. Use 2.5 cups water, decoct to one large cup, remove dregs, take warm before meals, twice daily. (From Pu Ji Fang: Zi Su Yin)
25) For violent coughing and wheezing: Perilla stem and leaves 2 sheng, soybeans 1 sheng. Boil soybeans in 4 sheng of water, then add Perilla and continue boiling until 1.5 sheng remains. Divide into three doses, two during the day and one at night. Avoid vinegar, fried, salty, sour, and greasy foods. (From Wai Tai)
26) For beriberi with persistent wheezing: Perilla stem and leaves 3 fen (2 liang), White Qian (Bai Qian) 1 liang, Mulberry Root Bark (Sang Bai Pi) 2 liang (chopped). Coarsely pound and sift into powder. Each dose 4 qian, water one medium cup, add half a fen fresh ginger, decoct to 60%, remove dregs, take warm at any time. (From Sheng Hui Fang)
27) For hematemesis and epistaxis: White Mao (Bai Mao) 3 qian, Perilla stem and leaves 2 qian. Powder. One bowl of fresh-drawn water, decoct to 70%, while hot mix with 2 qian Cattail Pollen (Pu Huang) and take immediately. Also roast two cloves of garlic, smash and apply to both soles; after a short while one feels garlic aroma in the chest and bleeding stops. If lower body bleeding, roast garlic and apply to both palms. (From Zhi Zhi Fang: Mao Su Tang)
28) For heat in the upper burner with blood-streaked sputum, vexation, thirst: Black soybeans 3 he, Perilla stem and leaves 2 liang, Mume (Wu Mei) 2 pieces. Boil together in a large bowl of water; near completion add 3 large spoons of ginger juice and take immediately before meals. (From Zhi Zhi Fang: Dou Su Tang)
29) Perilla Vinegar Powder: Perilla 30 g, appropriate amount of vinegar. Grind Perilla into fine powder, add 1500 ml water, boil and filter to obtain juice. Add equal amount of vinegar and boil down to dryness. Take 1.5 g each time, three times daily. Has throat-swelling-relieving and middle-widening effects; suitable for dysphagia in esophageal cancer.
30) Five-Spirit Tea: Schizonepeta (Jing Jie) 10 g, Perilla Leaf (Su Ye) 10 g, Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) 10 g, brown sugar 30 g, tea leaves 6 g. First simmer Schizonepeta, Perilla Leaf, Fresh Ginger, and tea leaves over low heat for about 15–20 minutes, then add brown sugar until dissolved and serve. Dosage: take twice daily as needed. Efficacy: disperse wind-cold and relieve pain. Indicated for wind-cold type headaches, aversion to cold, body aches, no sweating, etc.

Phellodendron (Huang Bai)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%BB%84%E6%9F%8F
Name
Phellodendron bark (Huang Bai)
Huangbo (Huangbo), Yuan Bai (Yuan Bai), Bo tree (Bo Mu)
Huangbo (Huangbo)
Yuan Bai (Yuan Bai)
Bo tree (Bo Mu)
Sichuan Phellodendron (Chuan Bai)
Tan Gui (Tan Gui)
Huangbo (Huangbo)
Sichuan Phellodendron bark (Chuan Bai Pi)
Phellodendron bark (Bo Pi)
Cultivation and processing of Phellodendron bark
Source
This item is the dried bark of plants of the Rutaceae family: Phellodendron species or the Huangpi tree. The former is commonly called Sichuan Phellodendron, the latter commonly called Guan Huang Bai. After peeling the bark, remove the rough outer bark and dry in the sun.
[Macroscopic morphology]
1. Phellodendron
Also called: Huangboluo, Huangbai li. A deciduous tree, 10–25 meters high; the outer layer of the bark is gray with a rather thick cork layer, the surface has longitudinal fissures, the inner bark is bright yellow. Twigs are usually gray-brown or light brown, rarely red-orange. Leaves opposite, imparipinnate, 5–13 leaflets; leaflet petioles short; leaflets oblong-lanceolate, oblong-ovate-lanceolate or nearly ovate, 5–11 cm long, 2–3.8 cm wide, apex gradually acuminate, base usually unequal broadly cuneate or nearly rounded, margins with fine rounded teeth or nearly entire, often ciliate; upper surface dark green, young leaves with soft hairs along the veins, older leaves glabrous. Lower surface pale, young leaves with soft hairs along the veins, older leaves only with long white hairs at the base of the midrib. Inflorescences paniculate, axis and branches hairy when young; flowers unisexual, dioecious, small; calyx 5, ovate; petals 5, oblong, yellow-green; male flowers with 5 stamens protruding beyond the petals, filaments hairy at the base; in female flowers the abortive stamens are scale-like, pistil 1, ovary superior, very short style, capitate stigma, 5-lobed. Drupes globose, about 8–10 mm in diameter, purple-black when ripe, usually 5-seeded. Flowering May–June. Fruiting September–October. Grows in mixed broadleaf forests on mountains or near mountain valleys and torrents. Distributed in Northeast China and North China.
2. Huangpi tree
Also called: Huipi bai, Hua Huang Bai. A deciduous tree, 10–12 meters high. Outer bark gray-brown, very thin, without a thickened cork layer, inner layer yellow; twigs usually dark red-brown or purple-brown, smooth and glabrous. Leaves opposite; imparipinnate, 7–15 leaflets with short petioles; leaflets oblong-lanceolate to oblong-ovate, 9–14 cm long, 3–5 cm wide, apex gradually acuminate, base broadly cuneate or nearly rounded, usually unequal on both sides, upper surface dark green with only the midrib hairy, lower surface light green with long soft hairs. Inflorescences paniculate, axis and branches densely short-hairy; flowers unisexual, dioecious; calyx 5, ovate; petals 6, oblong; male flowers with 6 stamens greatly exceeding the petals, filaments very long, base with long white soft hairs; abortive stamens in female flowers small, pistil 1, ovary superior, 5 chambers, style short; stigma 5-lobed. Drupes globose, 1–1.2 cm in diameter, densely clustered, purple-black when ripe, usually 5-seeded. Flowering May–June. Fruit ripens in October. Grows in mixed broadleaf forests on mountain slopes and ravines. Distributed in Sichuan, Hubei, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang and other regions.
Properties and flavor
Bitter, cold.
Character
1. Eastern Phellodendron
Also called: Guan Bai, Guan Huang Bai. The dried bark of the plant Phellodendron. Appears as slightly curved plate-like pieces, edges irregular, varying length and width, thickness about 2–4 mm. Cork layer may be retained or removed; cork relatively thick, surface grayish-white; where cork is removed, surface brown-yellow, flat or wrinkled with lenticels; inner surface gray-yellow. Texture relatively loose, brittle, fracture fibrous, pale yellow slightly greenish. Smell faint, taste bitter. Powder becomes sticky when mixed with water and stains the water yellow. Best quality when pieces are large and thick, fresh yellow, without cork. Main production areas: Liaoning, Jilin, Hebei. Also produced in Heilongjiang and Inner Mongolia. Liaoning produces the most.
2. Sichuan Phellodendron (from Depei Bencao)
Dried bark of the Huangpi tree and its variants. Slightly curved plate-like pieces, edges irregular, varying length and width, thickness about 3–5 mm, cork mostly removed. Outer surface deep yellow, relatively flat, with longitudinal ridges and brown lenticels; inner surface grayish-yellow or yellow. Texture hard and light, brittle, fracture fibrous, splits in flakes, fresh yellow. Smell faint, taste bitter, chewed it is mucilaginous and can stain water yellow. Best when pieces are large, thick, fresh yellow, without cork. Main production areas: Sichuan, Guizhou, Hubei, Yunnan. Also in Hunan, Gansu, Guangxi. Sichuan and Guizhou produce the most.
Effects of Phellodendron bark
Efficacy
This item is the dried bark of Phellodendron species of the Rutaceae family or the Huangpi tree. Main indications: dysenteric disorders from heat, diarrhea, excessive thirst (Xiaoke), jaundice, flaccid paralysis, nocturnal emission, turbid painful urination, hemorrhoids, bloody stools, leucorrhea, steaming bone disorders with night fever, red painful eyes, mouth and tongue sores, carbuncles and toxic swellings.
Channels entered
Enters the Kidney meridian and the Bladder meridian.
Main indications
Clears heat. Dries dampness, drains fire, detoxifies. Treats dysenteric disorders from heat, diarrhea, excessive thirst (Xiaoke), jaundice, flaccid paralysis, nocturnal emission, turbid painful urination, hemorrhoids, bloody stools, leucorrhea, steaming bone disorders with night fever, red painful eyes, mouth and tongue sores, carbuncles and toxic swellings.
1. Benjing: treats accumulative heat in the five zang and intestines and stomach, jaundice, intestinal hemorrhoids; stops dysenteric diarrhea, female abnormal uterine bleeding of red or white, sores of the genitals.
2. Bie Lu: cures fright qi between the skin, heat and redness of the flesh, red painful eyes, mouth sores.
3. Yaoxing Lun: treats male impotence. Treats rectal bleeding like pieces of duck or chicken liver; and sores on the male organ, apply powdered herb.
4. Bencao Shiyi: treats heat sores and eruptions, worm sores, dysentery, bleeding, kills insects; decocted for internal use treats excessive thirst.
5. Rihuazi Bencao: calms the heart and relieves fatigue, treats steaming bone disorders, cleanses the liver, brightens the eyes, excessive tearing, dry mouth, heart heat, kills pinworms, treats roundworm heart pain, scabies, when honey-fried treats nasal discharge, intestinal wind, hematochezia, acute swollen pain.
6. Zhenzhu Nang: treats kidney water disorders. Bladder deficiency, various atrophies and collapse, weakness of waist and knees.
7. Yixue Qiyuan: “Secrets of Main Treatments” says it drains the bladder dragon-fire, facilitates discharge of bound urine, reduces lower-jiao edema, dysentery with early bloody stools, umbilical pain, tonifies kidney water deficiency.
8. Yongyao Xinfa: treats unbearable sore carbuncles.
9. Lan Shi Mi Cang: drains pathogenic qi of the Chong vessel. Treats summer qi surging up causing inability to breathe and noisy panting preventing lying down.
10. Materia Medica: used topically for pediatric head sores.
11. Modern Practical Chinese Materia Medica: for sprains and contusions, grind to powder and mix into a paste for topical application.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: decoction, 3–9 g; or used in pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, grind to powder and apply as a plaster, or decoct for wash.
Precautions and contraindications
Contraindicated in spleen-deficiency diarrhea and in persons with weak stomach and poor appetite.
1. Bencao Jing Jizhu: averse to dry lacquer (gan qi).
2. Bencao Jieshu: contraindicated in people with both yin and yang deficiency, diseases accompanied by spleen-stomach weakness, poor food intake and poor digestion, or concurrent diarrhea; those who dislike cold foods and like hot foods; kidney-deficient early-morning diarrhea; upper heat and lower cold with urinary incontinence; cold pain in the lower abdomen, cold uterus; blood deficiency infertility, yang deficiency heat, stagnant blood, postpartum blood-deficiency fever, metal wound fever; heat after carbuncle ulceration, food-injury fever, yin deficiency urine difficulty, small water not flowing after smallpox, blood deficiency insomnia, blood-deficiency irritability, spleen-yin insufficiency causing diarrhea, etc.; in these patterns salty methods are contraindicated.
Formulas using Phellodendron bark
1. Treating pediatric dysenteric bloody stools: Phellodendron bark (Huangbo) half liang (about 7.5 g), Red Peony Root (Chi Shao) four qian (about 10 g). Grind to fine powder, form pills with rice and swallow the size of sesame seeds. Each dose one to twenty pills before meals with rice water; for larger children increase pills. (Yan’s Pediatric Formulas)
2. Treating dysentery: Phellodendron bark 300 g, Fanbai herb (Fan Bai Cao) 450 g, Qin Pi (Qin Pi) 300 g. Boil Fan Bai Cao and Qin Pi fully and 200 g of Phellodendron together twice, combine decoctions, reduce over low heat to a paste, grind remaining 100 g Phellodendron to fine powder and mix into the paste, stir, low-temperature dry, grind to fine powder. Each dose 1–2 g, three times daily. (Selected New Therapies of Chinese Herbs, Liaoning)
3. Treating cold-heat diarrhea during pregnancy and postpartum: Phellodendron bark one jin (500 g), Coptis (Huang Lian) one sheng (unit), Gardenia (Zhi Zi) twenty fruits. Cut finely, soak in five liters of water overnight, boil three times, drink one sheng (approximate measure) continuously day and night until used up. For vomiting add Aged Tangerine Peel (Chen Pi) a handful and Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) two liang. (Qianjin Yifang)
4. Treating pediatric summer diarrhea: Phellodendron bark, roast to powder, form pills with rice broth the size of millet grains; take one to twenty pills with rice broth. (Shiquan Bojiu Fang)
5. Treating excessive thirst with frequent urination but good appetite: Phellodendron bark one jin, water one sheng, boil until three to five times boiled, drink when thirsty, drink freely for several days. (Duxing Fang)
6. Treating cold-invasion with yellowing and fever: fifteen ripe Gardenia (split), Licorice (Gan Cao) one liang (prepared), Phellodendron bark two liang. Boil these three in four sheng water to one and a half sheng, remove dregs, take warm. (Shanghan Lun: Zhi Zi Bai Pi Tang)
7. Treating muscle and bone pain due to damp-heat: Phellodendron (stir-fried), Atractylodes (soaked in rice washing water then fried). Grind both into powder, take with boiling water mixed with ginger juice. Both have strong yang-promoting qi; when external excess is present add a little wine. (Danxi Xinf a: Er Miao San)
8. Treating severe heat with night diarrhea, startlement and confusion, epigastric distention and dry tongue: Phellodendron (coarse bark removed) one liang. Grind to fine powder with silk floss, add Borneol (Bing Pian) one qian, mix evenly, bind with processed honey into pills the size of a wutong seed. Take one to nineteen pills with a concentrated decoction of Ophiopogon (Mai Dong). (Shengji Zonglu: Qingxin Wan)
9. Treating leucorrhea, nocturnal emission, seminal emission and sliding discharge: Phellodendron one jin (roast on new tile until red), genuine clam shell powder (Zhen Ha Fen) one jin. Grind to fine powder, add drops of water to form pills the size of a wutong seed. Take one hundred pills on an empty stomach with wine. (Su Wen Bingji Baoming Ji: Zhenzhufan Wan)
10. Treating spontaneous sweating from the lower yin, dizziness and sore waist and knees: Phellodendron three qian, Atractylodes four qian, Sichuan pepper thirty grains; add 2000 ml water, decoct to 600 ml. Each dose 100 ml, three times daily, finish in two days. (Zhongji Yikan (3):177, 1966)
11. Lowering yin fire and tonifying kidney water: Phellodendron (stir-fried to brown) and Anemarrhena (soaked in wine then stir-fried) each four liang, Prepared Rehmannia root (steamed with wine) and Tortoise shell (roasted with honey) each six liang. Grind to powder, mix with pork spinal marrow and honey into pills. Take seventy pills on an empty stomach with salted white soup. (Danxi Xinf a: Da Bu Wan)
12. Reducing heart fire and benefiting kidney water: Phellodendron three liang, Amomum (Sha Ren) one and a half liang, Licorice one liang. Grind to fine powder, make pills the size of a stick. Take five pills, use Cistanche (Rou Cong Rong) half liang chopped, soak in a large cup of wine overnight, next morning decoct on empty stomach to three or four boils, remove dregs, take with clear wine. (Qi Xiao Liang Fang: Feng Sui Dan)
13. Treating epidemic conjunctivitis with red eyes: Phellodendron, remove coarse bark, grind to powder, wrap in damp paper, coat with yellow clay and bake until dry. Use a pellet sized as a bean, wrap in gauze, soak in a cup of water, steam over rice and use the hot steam to wash and fumigate. One pellet can be used three to five times. (Yanke Longmu Lun: Wu Xing Tang)
14. Treating infant palpebral conjunctivitis: soak Phellodendron in breast milk and apply drops. (Xiaopin Fang)
15. Treating mouth and tongue sores: chew crushed Phellodendron and hold in the mouth. (Qianjin Fang)
16. Treating pediatric swollen tongue: soak Phellodendron in bamboo sap and finely apply on the tongue. (Qianjin Fang)
17. Treating foul oral ulcers: Phellodendron five qian, verdigris three qian. Mix to powder and apply to remove discharge and promote healing. (Xiaopin Fang)
18. Treating lip sores itching and pain: Phellodendron powder mixed with root juice of Epilobium and applied. (Shengji Zonglu)
19. Treating lung congestion and nasal sores and swelling: Phellodendron and Areca (Bing Lang) equal parts, crush to powder, mix with lard and apply. (Shenghui Fang)
20. Treating mastitis, various abscesses on the back and engorged breasts: crush Phellodendron to powder, sieve, mix with egg white, apply thickly; when dry reapply. (Buque Zhouhou Fang)
21. Treating carbuncles and toxic swellings: Phellodendron bark (stir-fried), processed Chuan Wu Tou (prepared) equal parts. Grind to powder and apply, leave on the head, frequently moisten with rice-washing water. (Bin Hu Ji Jian Fang)
22. Treating male genital ulcers and erosion:
(1) Boil Phellodendron and wash, then apply white honey.
(2) Coptis (Huang Lian) and Phellodendron equal parts, grind to powder, boil in lard and soak the ulcer until resolved, then powder. (Buque Zhouhou Fang)
23. Treating pediatric umbilical sores that will not close: apply powdered Phellodendron. (Zi Mu Mi Lu)
24. Treating pediatric suppurative sores all over the body not drying: Phellodendron powder mixed with a little dried alum and applied. (Simple Single Remedies)
[Dietary therapy]
1. Salvia and Phellodendron wine
Salvia (Dan Shen) 30 g, Phellodendron bark (Huang Bai) 10 g, white wine 0.5 kg. Soak Salvia in white wine; after 7 days take 20–30 ml daily, 2–3 times a day.
Effect: Clears heat, cools the blood, promotes blood circulation.
2. Phellodendron and mung bean soup
Phellodendron bark (Huang Bai) 10 g, Mung beans (Lu Dou) 250 g, white sugar a little. Decoction of Phellodendron strained, add mung beans and cook until soft, add white sugar, cool and drink as desired.
Effect: Clears and drains damp-heat, drains fire and detoxifies.

Phragmites Bamboo Shoot (Lu Zhu Sun)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%8A%A6%E7%AB%B9%E7%AC%8B
Name
Giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn)
Cultivation and processing of giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn)
Source
The young shoots of the Poaceae plant giant reed (Lúzhú). Harvested in spring, washed clean and used fresh.
[Original morphology]
Giant reed (Lúzhú) is a perennial herb. It has a rhizome and stout fibrous roots. Culms erect, 2–6 m high, 1–1.5 cm in diameter, often branched. Leaf sheaths longer than the internodes, glabrous or with long soft hairs on the collar; ligules membranous, truncate, about 1.5 mm long, apex with short fine hairs; leaf blades flat, 30–60 cm long, 2–5 cm wide, surface and margins slightly rough when young. Panicle rather compact, 30–60 cm long, branches dense and ascending obliquely, spikelets contain 2–4 florets; glumes lanceolate, 8–10 mm long, with 3–5 veins; lemmas also with 3–5 veins, the midvein extending into a short awn 1–2 mm long, the lower part of the back densely covered with white soft hairs slightly shorter than the lemma, basal disk about 0.5 mm long, inner glume about half the length of the outer glume. Flowering period October–December.
[Habitat and distribution]
Ecological environment: grows beside streams and beside houses in relatively moist, deep soils.
Resource distribution: distributed in southwestern China, southern China and in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Hunan and other areas.
Nature and taste
Chongqing Materia Medica: bitter in taste, cold in nature, non-toxic.
Effects of giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn)
Functions
The young shoots of the Poaceae plant giant reed (Lúzhú). Mainly indicated for lung-heat hemoptysis, steaming-bone tidal fever, dizziness, hot lin (hot strangury), ear obstruction, toothache.
Main indications
Clears heat and drains fire. Treats lung-heat hemoptysis, steaming-bone tidal fever, dizziness, hot lin (hot strangury), ear obstruction, toothache.
1. "Categorized Herbal Properties": shoot juice treats ear pain.
2. "Lingnan Materia Medica": mashed young shoots can draw out rotten bone.
3. "Chongqing Materia Medica": clears fire and relieves heat, suitable for various febrile conditions. Treats steaming-bone tidal fever, fire-related toothache, dizziness, hot lin, etc.
Usage and dosage
Internal use: decoct in water, fresh product 15–60 g; or mash to extract juice, or boil down to a paste.
External use: appropriate amount, mash to extract juice and drop into the ear.
Formulas using giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn)
1. For lung-heat hemoptysis: giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn) one jin. Mash to extract juice and add
white sugar
Take.
2. For otitis media: mash juice of giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn) and add
borneol (Bīngpiàn)
drop into the ear.
3. For overworked brain and mental disorientation: giant reed shoot (Lúzhúsǔn) boiled down to a paste and add
white sugar
Take, one teaspoonful per dose. (Selected formula from "Chongqing Materia Medica")

Plough-head Grass (Li Tou Cao)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E7%8A%81%E5%A4%B4%E8%8D%89
Names
Purple-gold lock (Zi Jin Suo), Small Sweet Water Eggplant (Xiao Tian Shui Qie), Dabei Grass (Da Bei Cao), Triangle Grass (San Jiao Cao), Plowhead Tip (Li Tou Jian), Flatiron Grass (Lao Tie Cao), Sheep Hoof Jia (Yang Ti Jia), Liye Tip (Li Ye Jian).
Heartleaf Violet (Xin Ye Jin Cai)
Dabei Grass (Da Bei Cao)
Cultivation and Preparation of Plowhead Grass (Li Tou Cao)
Source
From the whole herb of the Violaceae plant Heartleaf Violet (Xin Ye Jin Cai). Harvest the whole herb during the fruit ripening period in April to May, remove soil, use fresh or sun-dry.
Morphology
Heartleaf Violet is a perennial herb. No aerial stem or stolons. Rhizome short and thick, nodes close, about 4–5 mm thick; many branched roots, relatively stout and elongated. Leaves numerous, basal; petioles usually nearly equal to the leaf blade during flowering and much longer than the blade during fruiting; stipules short, adnate to the lower part of the petiole, about 1 cm long, the free part spreading; leaf blade ovate, broadly ovate or triangular-ovate, rarely reniform, 3–8 cm long and 3–8 cm wide, apex acute or slightly obtuse, base deeply cordate or broadly cordate, margin with many rounded obtuse teeth, both surfaces glabrous or sparsely short-hairy. Flowers pale purple; flowers do not rise much above the leaves; near the middle there are two linear-lanceolate small bracts; calyx lobes broadly lanceolate, apex gradually acuminate, basal appendage about 2 mm long, apex obtuse or truncate; upper and lateral petals obovate, lower petal long obcordate; spur cylindrical, 4–5 mm long and about 2 mm thick. Capsule ellipsoid, about 1 cm long.
Habitat and Distribution
Ecological environment: grows on forest edges, open grassy areas under forests, mountain grass clumps, and beside streams and valleys.
Resource distribution: distributed in the southwest and in Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan and other regions.
Taste and Properties
Bitter; slightly pungent; cold in nature
Effects of Plowhead Grass (Li Tou Cao)
Efficacy
The whole herb of the Violaceae plant Heartleaf Violet (Xin Ye Jin Cai). Mainly treats carbuncles and swellings, mammary carbuncles, intestinal abscess with bleeding, purulent osteomyelitis, jaundice, red swollen painful eyes, scrofula, external traumatic bleeding, and snakebite.
Meridians
Liver; Spleen meridians
Indications
Clears heat and detoxifies, resolves stasis and discharges pus, cools the blood and clears the liver. Indicated for carbuncles and swellings, mammary carbuncles, intestinal abscess with bleeding, purulent osteomyelitis, jaundice, red swollen painful eyes, scrofula, external traumatic bleeding, and snakebite.
Usage and Dosage
Internal use: decoction, 9–15 g, fresh 30–60 g; or take pounded juice.
External use: appropriate amount, pounded and applied as a poultice.
Prescriptions of Plowhead Grass (Li Tou Cao)
1. For nodules on the back: roots of Dabei Grass (Da Bei Cao), crush and mix with sugar or red pepper and apply to the affected area; surround the area with a ring of flour dust. (Nanjing Folk Herbal Medicine)
2. For carbuncles, boils, and unnamed swellings: equal amounts of fresh Plowhead Grass (Li Tou Cao) and fresh Wild Chrysanthemum leaves (Ye Ju Hua), mash together and apply to the lesion; or mash the whole fresh Plowhead Grass with a little white sugar and apply, change once daily. Also take one wineglass of the mashed juice internally. (Zhejiang Common Folk Herbs)
3. For abscesses, boils, carbuncles, mastitis, and felons: mash fresh Plowhead Grass and apply; or dry and grind to a powder, mix with egg white and apply, change one to two times daily.
4. For boils: grind Plowhead Grass into powder, make pills with rice paste about the size of a wutong seed, nine pills per dose, swallow with hot water.
5. For postpartum blood stasis with knife-like stabbing pain: one liang of fresh Plowhead Grass (about 50 g), chop finely, mix with two eggs and beat together, stir-fry slightly with oil, then add water and decoct for oral administration.
6. For venomous snakebite: mash fresh Plowhead Grass and apply to the wound, change one to two times daily. (Prescriptions from Jiangxi Folk Herbal Medicine)
7. For external traumatic bleeding: Plowhead Grass (Li Tou Cao), Wood Sorrel (Cujiangcao)
Each in appropriate amounts, mash and apply externally to the wound, cover with gauze and press and bandage; or use Plowhead Grass alone mashed and applied. (Jiangxi "Herbal Manual")
8. For brine poisoning: mash fresh Plowhead Grass to obtain two wineglassfuls of juice, dilute with boiling water and drink. (Zhejiang Common Folk Herbs)

input:
Prepared soybean (Dan Dou Chi)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%B7%A1%E8%B1%86%E8%B1%89
Name
Fermented Soybean
Fragrant Douchi (Xiang Chi), Douchi (Chi), Light Douchi (Dan Chi), Soybean Douchi (Da Dou Chi)
Fragrant Douchi (Xiang Chi)
Douchi (Chi)
Light Douchi (Dan Chi)
Soybean Douchi (Da Dou Chi)
Douchi (Dou Chi)
Dou Shi (Dou Shi)
Cultivation and Processing of Fermented Soybean (Dan Dou Chi)
Source
A fermented processed product of the mature seeds of the soybean, a plant of the Leguminosae (legume) family.
Properties and Flavors
Bitter; Acrid; Neutral
Appearance
This product is ellipsoid and slightly flattened, length 0.6-1 cm, diameter 0.5-0.7 cm.
Surface black, wrinkled and uneven, dull, with a brown strip-like hilum on one side, micropyle not obvious.
Two cotyledons, thick.
Texture soft, fracture surface brown-black.
Slight odor, slightly sweet taste.
Those with large, plump grains and black color are preferred.
Preparation
Decoct mulberry leaves (Sang Ye) and Artemisia annua (Qing Hao) in water, filter; mix the decoction with washed black soybeans, and after the liquid is absorbed, place in a steamer and steam thoroughly; remove and cool slightly, then place in a container, cover with the residuum of the decocted mulberry leaves and Artemisia annua, seal and allow to ferment until a yellow coat forms; remove and sun dry to obtain the product. (For each 100 jin of black soybeans, use 4 jin mulberry leaves and 7 jin Artemisia annua.)
Besides the above processing method for Light Douchi, other herbs such as Polygonum hydropiper (La Liao), Eupatorium fortunei (Pei Lan), Perilla leaf (Su Ye), Agastache (Huo Xiang), Ephedra (Ma Huang), Artemisia annua (Qing Hao), Notopterygium (Qiang Huo), Bupleurum (Chai Hu), Angelica dahurica (Bai Zhi), Ligusticum (Chuan Xiong), Kudzu root (Ge Gen), Radix Paeoniae Rubra (Chi Shao), Platycodon root (Jie Geng), Licorice (Gan Cao), etc., may be used; either decocted to obtain the herbal juice to cook the beans, or the herbs ground into powder and mixed with cooked soybeans and then sealed to ferment—various processing methods exist.
Effects of Fermented Soybean (Dan Dou Chi)
Efficacy
A fermented processed product of the mature seeds of soybean.
Mainly treats typhoid and febrile diseases, chills and fever, headache, restlessness, chest oppression.
Channels (Meridians)
Lung meridian
;
Stomach meridian
;
Heart meridian
;
Bladder meridian
;
Small Intestine meridian
;
Triple Burner meridian (San Jiao)
Indications
Releases the exterior, eliminates vexation, disperses constraint, detoxifies. Treats typhoid and febrile diseases, chills and fever, headache, irritability, chest oppression.
① Bielu: Treats typhoid headache with chills and fever, miasmatic and noxious influences, restlessness and fullness and oppression, consumptive panting and gasping, and cold painfulness of both feet.
② Yaoxing Lun: Treats epidemic febrile disease with sweating; when roasted and powdered, can stop night sweats and remove vexation; raw pounded into pills and taken, treats alternating cold and heat and wind, and sores in the chest; boiled and taken, treats bloody dysentery and abdominal pain.
③ Rihuazi Ben Cao: Treats medicinal poisoning, malaria, steaming bone disorder; also treats dog bites.
④ Zhenzhu Nang: Removes vexation in the heart, typhoid headache, irritability.
⑤ Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica): Descends qi, harmonizes the middle. Treats typhoid toxic febrile eruptions and vomiting with counterflow.
⑥ Benjing Fengyuan: Compress and squeeze juice with water to treat poisoning from accidentally ingesting bird or beast livers.
⑦ Huiyue Yijing: Stabilizes pregnancy.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoct as a decoction, 5–15 g; or incorporate into pill formulas.
External use: appropriate amount, pounded and applied topically; or stir-fry until charred, grind into powder and apply as a paste.
Precautions and Contraindications
① Yaoxing Lun: If it acquires a sour smell, it is considered good.
② Ben Cao Jing Shu: In cases where a typhoid disease has transmitted into the yin meridians and involved the central three yin, it is not appropriate to use.
Prescriptions of Fermented Soybean (Dan Dou Chi)
① For restless vexation and inability to sleep after sweating and purging, with vexation in the heart:
Gardenia (Zhi Zi)
Fourteen pieces (split), fragrant douchi four heaped measures (wrapped in cotton). For the above two ingredients, use 4 sheng of water, first decoct the Gardenia to obtain 2.5 sheng, add the douchi, boil down until reduced to 1 sheng, remove dregs. Divide into two doses; take one warm, if it induces vomiting stop, then take the second after vomiting ceases. (Shang Han Lun: Zhi Zi Chi Tang)
② For febrile toxic eruptions and severe epidemics difficult to treat: Black paste
Raw Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang)
Half jin (chopped), good douchi one sheng, pork fat two jin. Boil together five or six boils, reduce the liquid by one third, strain out dregs, powder; add Realgar (Xiong Huang) and Musk (She Xiang) each in amounts the size of a soybean, mix well and take it all; the poison will come out through the skin. (Bu Que Zhou Hou Fang)
③ For sudden severe diarrhea from typhoid and stagnant dysentery with abdominal pain: Douchi one sheng,
Allium macrostemon bulb (Xie Bai) one handful (cut into inch pieces). Use the above two items with 3 sheng of water, boil until the Allium is cooked, remove dregs, divide and take twice; if not cured repeat. (Fan Wang Fang: Chi Xie Tang)
④ For many years of wheeze and shortness of breath of the lung, gasping cough, inability to sleep morning and evening: Arsenic (Pi Shi) 1.5 qian (pulverized to a fine powder), Douchi (good quality) 1.5 liang (slightly moisten with water for a short time, press between paper to dry, grind into a paste). Pound the paste and the arsenic together until extremely uniform, make pills the size of mustard seeds. Each dose fifteen pills; children's doses according to size, and take with very cold la tea while lying down and swallowing, use as directed. (Ben Shi Fang: Zi Jin Dan)
⑤ For breast engorgement after weaning: Douchi half jin, decoct in water, take one small bowl, use the remainder to wash the breasts. (Guangxi Collection of New Medical Methods for Chinese Herbal Prescriptions)
⑥ For pediatric erysipelas that breaks into ulcers with yellow discharge: Char-fry douchi until smoking stops, grind into powder, mix with oil and apply as a topical dressing. (Yao Hezhong)
⑦ For painful ulceration on the penis: Douchi one fen, earthworm in wet mud two fen, pound with water into a paste and apply, allow to dry and repeat; avoid hot foods such as Chinese chives and garlic. (Yaoxing Lun)

Qing Yu Dan Cao (Qing Yu Dan Cao)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%9D%92%E9%B1%BC%E8%83%86%E8%8D%89
Name
Creeping Gentian (Man Long Dan), Opposite‑leaved Lin (Dui Ye Lin), Fish Loach Vine (Yu Qiu Teng)
Creeping Gentian (Man Long Dan)
Fish Loach Vine (Yu Qiu Teng)
Creeping Gentian root (Qing Yu Dan Gen)
Cultivation and Processing of Creeping Gentian (Qing Yu Dan Cao)
Source
The whole herb of the Gentianaceae plant Creeping Gentian (Man Long Dan). Harvested after autumn.
Original Morphology
Perennial, prostrate herb. Stems slender. Leaves opposite, papery, ovate‑lanceolate, 4–7 cm long, 1.2–2.3 cm wide, apex gradually acuminate, base rounded, margins entire, dark green; three main veins prominent. Flowers axillary; calyx tubular, 5‑lobed, lobes triangular‑lanceolate; corolla campanulate, 5‑lobed, pale purple, with secondary lobes between the main lobes. Berry subglobose, about 1.5 cm long, red‑purple, with a long stalk extending beyond the persistent calyx. Flowering in autumn.
Properties and Taste
Pungent; bitter; cool
Effects of Creeping Gentian (Qing Yu Dan Cao)
Functions
The whole herb of the Gentianaceae plant Creeping Gentian (Man Long Dan). Mainly used for wind‑heat cough, jaundice, rheumatic painful obstruction, and roundworm infections.
Channels Entered
Lung; Liver; Spleen channels
Main Indications
Disperses wind and clears heat, strengthens the spleen and drains dampness, kills parasites. Indicated for wind‑heat cough; jaundice; rheumatic painful obstruction; and roundworm infections.
Usage and Dosage
Internal: decoction, 15–30 g; or infused in alcohol; or cooked into congee.
External: appropriate amount, decocted in water for fumigation and washing.
Formulas Using Creeping Gentian (Qing Yu Dan Cao)
1. For jaundice: Creeping Gentian root (Qing Yu Dan Gen) three liang, decoct and drink.
2. For wind‑heat cough: fresh Creeping Gentian (Qing Yu Dan Cao) one to two liang, stewed with pork and eaten.
3. For rheumatism: Creeping Gentian root (Qing Yu Dan Gen) five liang, soaked in wine and taken; alternatively the vine may be decocted for fumigation and washing.
4. To expel roundworms: Creeping Gentian (Qing Yu Dan Cao) five qian,
Solomon's Seal (Yu Zhu)
three qian,
Rice (Da Mi)
one handful. Cook into a thin porridge and consume in two divided doses.

Reed Rhizome (Lu Gen)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%8A%A6%E6%A0%B9
Name
Reed Rhizome
Lumao Root (Lu Mao Gen), Reed Root (Wei Gen), Lugu Root (Lu Gu Gen), Shunjianglong (Shunjianglong), Shuizengang (Shui Zengang), Luchai Root (Lu Chai Gen), Lu Tong (Lu Tong), Reed-seed Root (Wei Zi Gen), Lu Sprout Root (Lu Ya Gen), Sweet Stemlet (Tian Geng Zi), Reed Head (Lu Tou)
Reed Root (Wei Gen)
Reed Root (Lu Wei Root)
Large Reed Rhizome (Da Lu Gen)
Lumao Root (Lu Mao Gen)
Lugu Root (Lu Gu Gen)
Shunjianglong (Shunjianglong)
Shuizengang (Shui Zengang)
Luchai Root (Lu Chai Gen)
Lu Tong (Lu Tong)
Reed-seed Root (Wei Zi Gen)
Lu Sprout Root (Lu Ya Gen)
Sweet Stemlet (Tian Geng Zi)
Reed Head (Lu Tou)
Cultivation and Processing of Reed Rhizome (Lu Gen)
Source
The rhizome of the grass-family plant common reed (Phragmites australis, Lu Wei). Harvested in spring, summer, and autumn; wash off soil, cut away remaining stems, buds and rootlets on the nodes, peel off the membranous leaves, and sun-dry. Or bury in moist sand for fresh use.
Nature and Taste
Sweet; cold
Appearance and Properties
① Fresh Reed Rhizome
Also called: Living-water Reed Rhizome. Cylindrical or flattened cylindrical, of varying lengths, about 1.5 centimeters in diameter. Surface yellowish-white and glossy, tip tapered like a bamboo shoot, green or yellow-green. Nodes present along the whole length, internodes 10–17 millimeters long, with remaining rootlets and bud scars on the nodes. Light and tough, not easily broken. Transverse section yellow-white, hollow, peripheral wall about 1.5 millimeters thick, showing small pores arranged in a ring; outer bark loose and peelable. Odorless, sweet taste.
② Dried Reed Rhizome
Flattened long-cylindrical. Surface glossy, yellowish-white, nodes harder and appearing reddish-yellow, longitudinal wrinkles between nodes. Light and pliant, not easily broken, odorless, slightly sweet. Best quality are thick, yellowish-white, glossy, without rootlets, and tender. Produced nationwide.
Actions of Reed Rhizome (Lu Gen)
Efficacy
The rhizome of the grass-family plant common reed.
Treats febrile disease with vexation and thirst, stomach-heat vomiting, dysphagia and obstruction in the epigastrium, rebellious stomach qi, pulmonary consumption, and lung abscess. Also relieves puffer fish (fugu) poison.
Meridians Entered
Lung meridian; Stomach meridian; Bladder meridian
Main Indications
Clears heat, generates fluids, relieves vexation, and stops vomiting. Treats febrile disease with vexation and thirst, stomach-heat vomiting, dysphagia and obstruction in the epigastrium, rebellious stomach qi, pulmonary consumption, and lung abscess. Also relieves puffer fish (fugu) poison.
① Bie Lu (Bielu): treats wasting-thirst and hostile heat, stops small difficult urination.
② Yao Xing Lun (Yaoxing Lun): can relieve great heat, open the stomach. Treats intractable belching and hiccup.
③ Tang Ben Cao (Tang Ben Cao): cures incessant vomiting with inability to eat, stomach heat, and lingering illness after typhoid.
④ Ri Hua Zi Ben Cao (Ri Huazi Ben Cao): treats alternating chills and fever with vexation and oppression, heart heat in pregnancy, and also thirst in dysentery.
⑤ Ri Yong Ben Cao (Riyong Ben Cao): relieves puffer fish poison.
⑥ Ben Cao Meng Quan (Ben Cao Mengquan): relieves alcohol poisoning and fish or crab poisoning.
⑦ Ben Cao Yuan Shi (Ben Cao Yuan Shi): treats dry retching and cholera.
⑧ Yu Qiu Yao Jie (Yu Qiu Yao Jie): clears and descends Lung and Stomach, disperses constraint and vexation, generates fluids and stops thirst, relieves vomiting and inability to eat, treats dysphagia, belching, and agitation.
⑨ Yi Lin Zuan Yao (Yi Lin Zuan Yao): can leach dampness and promote urination, treats lung abscess.
⑩ Tian Bao Ben Cao (Tianbao Ben Cao): clears the heart and benefits the kidney, removes ocular haze, dizziness, tinnitus, sore ulcerations, confusing dreams and inversion, and seminal emission.
⑾ Zhongguo Yao Zhi (Zhongguo Yao Zhi): treats constipation.
⑿ Nanjing Folk Herbs (Nanjing Minjian Yao Cao): treats sore throat.
⒀ Shandong Chinese Materia Medica (Shandong Zhong Yao): treats edema.
⒁ Sichuan Materia Medica (Sichuan Zhong Yao Zhi): treats maculopapular rashes, dry tongue, and lack of fluids.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoct, 15–30 g for dried, 60–120 g for fresh; or pound fresh and extract juice.
External use: appropriate amount, decoct and wash.
Precautions and Contraindications
Use with caution in those with spleen and stomach cold deficiency.
Prescriptions Using Reed Rhizome (Lu Gen)
① For Taiyin warm disease with extreme thirst and sticky white phlegm that will not flow: pear juice, water chestnut juice, fresh reed rhizome juice, Ophiopogon tuber juice (Mai Dong), lotus root juice (or use sugarcane juice), adjust amounts according to the situation, mix evenly and take cool; those who strongly dislike cold may take in thick soup warmed before use. (Wen Bing Tiao Bian: Five-juice Drink)
② For the five types of dysphagia with chest obstruction, qi stagnation, vexation, retching and inability to eat: Reed Rhizome 5 liang (about 125 g). Shred and boil with three large bowls of water down to two bowls, remove dregs, no strict timing, take warm. (Jin Kui Yu Han Fang)
③ For persistent vomiting and reversal: Reed Rhizome 3 jin (about 1.5 kg). Cut and boil to a strong decoction, drink frequently. (Zhou Hou Fang)
④ For post–cold-disease vomiting, rebellious stomach and dry retching with inability to eat: raw Reed Rhizome (cut) and bamboo shavings (Zhu Ru) each one sheng (a traditional volume), polished rice three he, fresh ginger three liang. Take the four ingredients, boil with five sheng of water down to two and a half sheng, drink as desired. (Qian Jin Fang: Lu Gen Drink)
⑤ For bone-steaming tidal fever and pulmonary consumption with vexation and inability to eat: Reed Rhizome (cut to weight), Ophiopogon tuber (Mai Dong) (heart removed), Di Gu Pi (root-bark), each ten liang, fresh ginger ten liang (including skin, sliced), dried tangerine peel (Chen Pi) and Poria (Fu Ling) each five liang. Cut all six herbs, boil with two dou of water down to eight sheng, squeeze out dregs, divide into five warm doses to be taken about eight or nine li apart, three doses by day and two by night, then induce sweating; avoid vinegar-flavored foods. (Xuan Gan Chuan Shi Fang)
⑥ Cholera with vexation: Reed Rhizome three qian, Ophiopogon tuber one qian. Decoction and take. (Qian Jin Fang)
⑦ For fish poisoning with facial swelling, delirium, or deathly condition after eating seabass: drink plenty of Reed Rhizome juice; also treats crab poisoning. (Qian Jin Fang)
⑧ For bleeding gums: decocted Reed Rhizome water as tea. (Hunan Yao Wu Zhi)
⑨ For stomach-heat thirst: Reed Rhizome 15 g, Ophiopogon tuber, Di Gu Pi, and Poria each 9 g, dried tangerine peel 4.5 g. Decoction and take. (Anhui Zhong Cao Yao)
⑩ For pertussis with hemoptysis: Reed Rhizome 30 g, Selaginella (Juan Bai) 6 g, Mu Hudie 6 g, beef-skin jelly 7.5 g. Decoction and take. (Hunan Yao Wu Zhi)
⑾ For lobar pneumonia with high fever, vexation and thirst, wheeze and cough: Reed Rhizome 30 g, Ephedra (Ma Huang) 3 g, Licorice (Gan Cao) 6 g, Bitter Apricot Kernel (Ku Xing Ren) 9 g, Gypsum (Shi Gao) 15 g. Decoction and take. (Ningxia Zhong Cao Yao Manual)
⑿ For lung abscess with bloody sputum: fresh Reed Rhizome 1000 g, stew with pig heart and lung and take. (Chongqing Grass Medicine)
⒀ For lung abscess with cough producing foul-smelling purulent sputum: Reed Rhizome 30 g, Coix Seed (Yi Yi Ren) and Winter Melon Seed (Dong Gua Zi) each 15 g, Peach Kernel (Tao Ren) and Platycodon Root (Jie Geng) each 9 g. Decoction and take. (Ningxia Zhong Cao Yao Manual)
⒁ For infant vomiting and irritability with heat: fresh Reed Rhizome 1 liang (about 3.75 g). Clean and boil with one sheng of water down to seven ge, remove dregs; cook red rice one ge in the juice and feed as congee. (Shi Yi Xin Jian: Fresh Reed Rhizome Congee)
⒂ For pregnancy vomiting with inability to eat and concurrent expectoration of phlegm-water: fresh Reed Rhizome ten fen, dried tangerine peel (Chen Pi) four fen, fresh ginger six fen, Areca Nut (Bing Lang) two fen. Boil two sheng of water down to seven ge, take on an empty stomach while warm. (Jing Xiao Chan Bao)
⒃ For postpartum vomiting and diarrhea, cholera, and abdominal pain: Reed Rhizome, Ginseng (Ren Shen), and Loquat Leaf (Pi Pa Ye) each one liang. Pound and sift; each dose five qian, boil with one and a half bowls of water down to eight fen, remove dregs, take warm at any time. (Pu Ji Fang: Reed Rhizome Drink)
⒄ For stomach qi pain with sour vomiting: Reed Rhizome 15 g, camphor tree root 9 g. Roast in water and take twice daily. (Guizhou Grass Medicine)
⒅ For measles not erupting
(1) Reed Rhizome 30 g, Tamarisk (Cheng Liu) 9 g. Decoction and take. (Shandong Zhong Cao Yao Manual)
(2) Reed Rhizome and coriander (Hu Sui) appropriate amounts. Boil into a strong decoction and rub on the body. (Qingdao Zhong Cao Yao Manual)
⒆ For scarlet fever: fresh Reed Rhizome and fresh White Baimao Root (Bai Mao Gen) each 30 g, white sugar appropriate amount. Decoction and drink as tea. (Henan Zhong Cao Yao Manual)
⒇ For swollen, painful throat: fresh reed root crushed and strained for juice, mixed with honey and taken. (Quanzhou Ben Cao)
(21) For mouth ulcers: Reed Rhizome 4 liang, Phellodendron (Huang Bai) and Cimicifuga (Sheng Ma) each 3 liang, Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang) 5 liang. Cut the four, boil with four sheng of water down to two sheng, remove dregs and hold in the mouth until healed; hold while very cold then spit out, then hold again. (Wai Tai quoting Ji Yan Fang)
(22) For wind-fire toothache: fresh reed root 60 g, willow root 60 g, Huang Jing root and roadside ginger each 30 g, two-month soaked root and transplanted-seedling soaked root each 18 g. Decoction and take. (Chongqing Grass Medicine)
(23) For sudden swelling of the eyes: Reed Rhizome 5 liang, roasted Licorice (Gan Cao, Zhi) 1 liang, polished millet 3 he, sweet bamboo shavings and a chicken egg-sized amount of bamboo shavings. Grind into paste like mashed beans. Each time use 5 qian, boil with two bowls of water down to one bowl, remove dregs, take warm after meals three times daily. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Reed Rhizome Decoction)
(24) For hard constipation: Reed Rhizome, Prunella (Xia Ku Cao), and honey each 15 g, rhubarb variant (Tu Da Huang, Yang Ti), Gleditsia (Zao Jiao, Zhu Ya Zao), and Honeysuckle (Jin Yin Hua) each 6 g. Boil and take. (Guizhou Grass Medicine)
(25) For leukorrhea: Reed Rhizome (dry) 15 g, root of five-fingered mallow (Wu Zhi Mao Tao) 30 g. Decoction and take. (Guangdong Huiyang District Chinese Herbs)
Dietary Therapy Recipes
1. Fresh Reed Rhizome Congee
Fresh Reed Rhizome 100 g, green peel (Qing Pi) 5 g, polished rice 100 g, two slices fresh ginger. Wash fresh reed rhizome, cut into thin segments, soak with green peel in cold water for 30 minutes, bring to a vigorous boil over high heat, then simmer over low heat for 20 minutes. Remove herb residue, add washed polished rice and cook into congee. Five minutes before removing from heat, add fresh ginger. Divide into two warm doses per day.
Efficacy: drains heat and harmonizes the stomach, nourishes yin and relieves pain; suitable for peptic ulcer patients of the Liver-Stomach accumulated-heat pattern, presenting with epigastric burning pain, irritability, easy anger, acid regurgitation and bitter taste.
2. Chrysanthemum and Reed Rhizome Tea
Chrysanthemum (Ju Hua) 10 g, Reed Rhizome 60 g. Wash reed rhizome, chop, put together with chrysanthemum into a pot, decoct and strain to obtain the liquid. Drink as a tea.
Efficacy: clears lung heat, promotes urination, and vents rashes. Indicated for pediatric measles, chickenpox and similar conditions.

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%A1%82%E6%9E%9D%E5%8E%BB%E8%8A%8D%E8%8D%AF%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Guizhi Decoction Without Shaoyao (Guizhi Qu Shaoyao Tang)
Ingredients
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shanghan Lun).
Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) 3 liang (peeled), Licorice (Gan Cao) 2 liang (honey-fried), Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) 3 liang (sliced), Jujube (Da Zao) 12 pieces (broken).
Therapeutic actions
Promotes sweating, releases the muscles, dispels wind, removes yin and communicates yang.
Actions of Guizhi Decoction Without Shaoyao (Guizhi Qu Shaoyao Tang)
Indications
Taiyang disease; after purgation, in cases with a hurried pulse and chest fullness.
Administration
Use 7 sheng of water, boil down to obtain 3 sheng, remove the dregs, take 1 sheng warm.
Commentaries of various authors
1. On Further Discussion (Shang Lun Pian): Use the acrid and sweet nature of Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) to promptly disperse the Taiyang pathogenic factor; as for the intention of removing Shaoyao (Shao Yao), the two words "sour" and "contractive" are insufficient to fully express it, and because it may mistakenly purge one does not dare to use it, fearing it will again lead the yang pathogenic factor downward into the abdomen.
2. Collected Pearls on Cold Damage (Shanghan Guanzhu Ji): The pathogenic qi still resides in the yang division, therefore Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi), Licorice (Gan Cao), Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang), and Jujube (Da Zao) — sweet, acrid, warm medicines — draw it from the yang and expel it; those who remove Shaoyao (Shao Yao) fear that its sour and cold flavor would be sufficient to retain the pathogenic factor in the chest, and would also deprive Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) of its nature.

Cinnamon Twig Decoction (without Peony) with Aconite (Gui Zhi Qu Shao Yao Jia Fu Zi Tang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%A1%82%E6%9E%9D%E5%8E%BB%E8%8A%8D%E8%8D%AF%E5%8A%A0%E9%99%84%E5%AD%90%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Guizhi Decoction without Paeonia plus Aconite (Guizhi qu Shaoyao jia Fuzi Tang)
Source
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shang Han Lun).
Ingredients
Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) 9 g (peeled) Licorice (Gancao) 6 g (honey-fried) Jujube (Dazao) 12 pieces (split) Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 9 g (cut) Prepared Aconite (Fuzi) 5 g (processed)
Actions of Guizhi Decoction without Paeonia plus Aconite (Guizhi qu Shaoyao jia Fuzi Tang)
Indications
Releases the exterior and dispels wind, warms and tonifies yang qi and generates body fluids. Used for Taiyang disease when, after mistaken application of purgative methods, the pulse is rapid, the chest is full, and there is slight aversion to cold.
Administration
Use the above five ingredients with 700 milliliters of water, decoct to obtain 300 milliliters, strain off dregs, take 100 milliliters warm. For recuperation, follow the method of Guizhi Decoction (Guizhi Tang).

Cinnamon Twig and Licorice Decoction (Gui Zhi Gan Cao Tang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%A1%82%E6%9E%9D%E7%94%98%E8%8D%89%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Guizhi Gancao Decoction (Guizhi Gancao Tang)
Source
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shanghan Lun)
Composition
Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) 12 g, Prepared Licorice (Zhi Gancao) 6 g
Efficacy
Tonify Heart Qi, warm Heart Yang
Explanation
Excessive sweating injures the Heart Yang; when the Heart's central Yang Qi is damaged it causes palpitations below the heart and a desire to press and restrain, hence clasping the hands over the chest. In the formula Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) enters the Heart, its acrid warm nature assists Yang; Prepared Licorice (Zhi Gancao) is sweet and warm and benefits Qi, further aiding the restoration of the Heart's Yang Qi. The two herbs combined, with acrid and sweet properties, transform and restore Yang; as Yang recovers and Yin is aided, the Heart is calmed.
Efficacy of Guizhi Gancao Decoction (Guizhi Gancao Tang)
Indications
For excessive sweating where the person clasps their hands over the chest, has palpitations below the heart, and desires to press the chest.
Prescription and Administration
Decoction in water, taken warm in three divided doses (Adult usual dosage: 10 doses)

Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%A1%82%E6%9E%9D%E5%8A%A0%E9%99%84%E5%AD%90%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Guizhi Jia Fuzi Decoction (Guizhi Jia Fuzi Tang)
Source
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shang Han Lun).
Composition
Cinnamon Twig (Guizhi) 9 g (peeled) Peony (Shao Yao) 9 g Licorice (Gan Cao) 9 g (honey-fried) Fresh Ginger (Sheng Jiang) 9 g (sliced) Jujube (Da Zao) 3 pieces (broken) Aconite (Fuzi) 6 g (processed)
Actions of Guizhi Jia Fuzi Decoction (Guizhi Jia Fuzi Tang)
Indications
Harmonize the Ying and Wei, secure the exterior and support Yang. Indicated for Taiyang-stage disorder in which sweating after sweating is excessive causing unceasing perspiration, aversion to wind, scanty and obstructed urination, slight stiffness of the four limbs with difficulty flexing and extending. Used to treat exterior deficiency with leakage of sweat, stubborn night sweats, sinus bradycardia, collapse in children from deficiency, hepatitis B, etc.
Usage
Combine the six ingredients, add 700 milliliters of water, decoct down to 300 milliliters, strain off dregs; each dose 100 milliliters, taken warm. For recuperation, follow the method of Guizhi Decoction (Guizhi Tang).

Ephedra Decoction (Ma Huang Tang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%BA%BB%E9%BB%84%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Ephedra Decoction (Ma Huang Tang)
Source
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shang Han Lun: Bian Taiyang Bing Mai Zheng Bing Zhi Zhong)
Classification
Exterior-releasing formula - acrid-warm release of the exterior
Ingredients
Ephedra (Ma Huang) 9 g, Cinnamon Twig (Gui Zhi) 6 g, Apricot Kernel (Xing Ren) 6 g, Honey-fried Licorice (Zhi Gan Cao) 3 g.
Efficacy of Ephedra Decoction (Ma Huang Tang)
Actions
Induces sweating to release the exterior, disseminates the Lung and relieves wheezing.
Indications
Exterior contraction of wind-cold: aversion to cold with fever, headache and body aches, absence of sweating with wheezing, tongue coating thin and white, pulse floating and tight. (This formula is commonly used for common cold, influenza, acute bronchitis, bronchial asthma, and other conditions characterized by exterior excess due to wind-cold.)
Key diagnostic points
Aversion to cold with fever, no sweating and wheezing, pulse floating and tight.
Administration
Take the four herbs with 9 sheng of water; first decoct the Ephedra, reduce by 2 sheng, skim off the upper scum, add the other herbs, boil down to 2.5 sheng, remove dregs, warm and take 8 he. Cover to obtain a slight, near-sweat; no need to sip gruel; the rest is to rest and recuperate as in the Gui Zhi method. (Modern usage: decoct in water and take warm, cover to induce slight sweating.)
Precautions
1. Generally used in winter;
2. Mostly used in young and middle-aged adults;
3. More commonly used in northern regions;
4. Ephedra Decoction (Ma Huang Tang) should not be used in patients with sore throat. A sore throat indicates exterior heat; treating a heat pattern with warm-hot herbs will inevitably worsen the condition, therefore it is contraindicated.

Ephedra Decoction with Atractylodes (Ma Huang Jia Shu Tang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E9%BA%BB%E9%BB%84%E5%8A%A0%E6%9C%AF%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Ephedra Decoction with Atractylodes (Ma Huang Jia Shu Tang)
Source
Essential Prescriptions of the Golden Cabinet (Jin Kui Yao Lue), juan shang
Composition
Original Ephedra Decoction (Ma Huang Tang) plus Bai Zhu (Atractylodes macrocephala) 12g
Efficacy of Ephedra Decoction with Atractylodes (Ma Huang Jia Shu Tang)
Actions
Induces sweating and releases the exterior; disperses cold and expels dampness
Indications
Wind-cold-damp painful obstruction, generalized body vexation and pain, absence of sweating, etc. (i.e., exterior excess pattern of wind-cold entrapping dampness)
Note
The Bai Zhu (Atractylodes macrocephala) in this formula may be substituted with Cang Zhu (Atractylodes lancea). During the Eastern Han period, Cang Zhu and Bai Zhu were not distinguished.

Kudzu Decoction (Ge Gen Tang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%91%9B%E6%A0%B9%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Kudzu Decoction (Ge Gen Tang)
Source
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shang Han Lun)
Ingredients
Kudzu root (Ge Gen) 12 g; Ephedra (Ma Huang) 9 g (nodes removed); Cinnamon twig (Gui Zhi) 6 g (peeled); Fresh ginger (Sheng Jiang) 9 g (sliced); Licorice (Gan Cao) 6 g (honey‑fried); Peony root (Shao Yao) 6 g; Jujube (Da Zao) 12 pieces (split)
Explanation
In the formula, kudzu root (Ge Gen) raises the body fluids and moistens the tendons and vessels, serving as the chief; ephedra (Ma Huang) and cinnamon twig (Gui Zhi) disperse wind‑cold and induce sweating to release the exterior, serving as deputies; peony root (Shao Yao) and licorice (Gan Cao) generate fluids and nourish the liquids, relax spasm and relieve pain as assistants; fresh ginger (Sheng Jiang) and jujube (Da Zao) harmonize the Spleen and Stomach and stimulate the Spleen and Stomach to generate qi as messengers. Together the herbs produce sweating to release the exterior, raise fluids and relax the tendons.
Actions of Kudzu Decoction (Ge Gen Tang)
Indications
Induces sweating and relieves toxicity, raises fluids and relaxes the tendons. Treats exterior excess due to wind‑cold, with aversion to cold and fever, headache, stiffness of the nape and back, body aches without sweating, slight abdominal pain, or diarrhea, or retching, or slight shortness of breath; tongue pale with white coating; pulse floating and tight. Currently used for common cold, influenza, measles, dysentery, and joint pain when the above symptoms are present.
Administration
Take the seven herbs above with 1 sheng (1 L) of water; first boil ephedra (Ma Huang) and kudzu root (Ge Gen) down to 800 ml, remove the scum, add the other herbs, then boil down to obtain 300 ml, remove the dregs; take 150 ml warm each time, cover to induce slight sweating.

Kudzu Decoction with Pinellia (Ge Gen Jia Ban Xia Tang)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E8%91%9B%E6%A0%B9%E5%8A%A0%E5%8D%8A%E5%A4%8F%E6%B1%A4
Prescription of Kudzu Decoction plus Pinellia (Ge Gen Jia Ban Xia Tang)
Source
Treatise on Cold Damage (Shang Han Lun)
Ingredients
Kudzu root (Ge Gen) 12 g Ephedra (Ma Huang) 9 g (nodes removed) Licorice root (Gan Cao) 6 g (honey-fried) Peony root (Shao Yao) 6 g Cinnamon twig (Gui Zhi) 6 g (peeled) Fresh ginger (Sheng Jiang) 6 g (sliced) Pinellia tuber (Ban Xia) 9 g (washed) Chinese jujube (Da Zao) 12 pieces (split)
Therapeutic effects of Kudzu Decoction plus Pinellia (Ge Gen Jia Ban Xia Tang)
Functions
Induces sweating to release the exterior, relaxes the muscles, and stops vomiting.
Indications
Exterior contraction of wind-cold, headache, rigidity and stiffness of the nape and back, absence of sweating, no thirst, nausea and counterflow vomiting, white tongue coating, and a floating pulse.
Administration
Take the above eight herbs with 1 L of water; first decoct the kudzu root and ephedra, reducing to 800 mL, skim off the white froth, add the rest of the herbs, decoct down to 300 mL, strain off the dregs, take 100 mL warm, cover and wait until slight sweating appears.
